ResponsesInList.Text: First, apologize for the length of this.  Second, maybe by kinda understanding the restore process one might be able to 'get by' ... at least restore a 1.9 course semi-successfully. During the restore process, a numbered folder is created in moodledata/temp/backup/########## and Moodle uses it to rebuild the course as a version 2. The following is a few text clips of the process during which there are directories created then removed.  Again, maybe understanding the process will help in creating some of the top level directories used during a restore and one might be able to 'get by' until a true 'fix' is offered. during restore of a 1.9 course to a 2.x, in the moodledata/temp/ directory there is created an unzip directory. Then the uploaded 1.9 course is converted in the backup directory where a folder like: 2faf13c374ebe4de8952827fbaef06ad is created.  It's that folder that is used to 'rebuild' the course as a 2 backup to restore. Every 2.0s: ls -l backup/2faf13c374ebe4de8952827fbaef06ad                                                      Sun May 20 08:06:26 2012 total 19088 drwxrwxrwx 4 apache apache     4096 May 20 08:01 course_files What directories are needed? in moodledata/temp/ a 'backup' directory with permissions set to allow apache user/group to create not only folders but files ... as well as remove them.  There should also be a zip and unzip directory at that level. Since I used URL downloader as the repo to acquire the 1.9 backup, a ' download ' folder. In the moodledata/temp/backup folder, see if there is a 'hashed' file name ... something like: 3ffcd237806e50e1bf8584eef0a6b35d and a .log file by hash name that's larger than 0 bytes (0 byte sized .log files indicates successful restores).  Something like: ce2c6a564254ca3df9f5509539a585dd.log One cannot create manually those hashed named directories for files. Think the log file will help in cleaning up the 1.9 course to be backed up in 1.9 and restored.  OR in preparing the 2 with missing mods/blocks, etc. compat with version 2.  Hopefully, those addon mods/blocks etc. will be included in the next attempt at restoring. And a question ... in apache error log files are there errors that have the word 'unlink' in them?  Have seen reports that Windows servers not appropriately configured might not be able to remove temporary files/folders created during the restore process (permissions or a php bug if I re-call correctly). 'spirit of sharing',  Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Restore fails from Moodle 1.9 to Moodle 2.2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: There is a 'warning.txt' file in filedir.  To save you time, it says: "This directory contains the content of uploaded files and is controlled by Moodle code. Do not manually move, change or rename any of the files and subdirectories here." That also includes adding any files.  Those additions won't show in the file chooser anyway as there are no records in the mdl_files table to tell Moodle of their existance and location. Any folder manually created in the 'repository' directory must: 1. have permissions set so apache user/group can see/read/write 2. be linked in the course as a repository to use for the course (at course level 'add a repo instance'). Have found that using the Moodle 2 repositories for restoring 1.9.x courses adds to the 'complexity' of things in that the mdl_files table grows rather large AND if one does not use a 1.9.x backup to restore a course and then remove the 1.9.x backup, it will stay until the cron jobs move un-used files (actually now records in the DB) to another status, then eventually to the trash_dir and thus (finally) removed from the database . That's why eventually restorted to a web accessible directory containing the 1.9.x backups OUTSIDE of Moodle completely.  That structure also lends itself well to using URL repo to restore (thus, also, getting by the  lower php max_size_upload limitations set for site). 'spirit of sharing', Ken

I imagine there could be a substantial cost hit in most circumstances, but it may be necessary. The alternative is to make sure that your courses remain below a particular size. For me, 800MB for a set of courses on a shared server is not large, 800Gb would be outrageous, so it should be backing up. However, a multimedia course full of large videos, or courses that have really grown organically and are now candidates for redesign may imbalance a backup, causing issues. I have often suspected the composition of the backup is important, but do not know enough about it to be sure. While these are other issues, they may impact on the success of a backup operation and may need to be considered. Personally, I encourage people to keep their courses as small and as tight as they can by emphasising that resources can be found anyhere, it is the activities that are really important. For most courses, 50MB is usually a good limit, but for other courses, this is just not enough, so good design is critical.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moved hosting and need old moodledata
ResponsesInList.Text: As you can read in many other threads, upgrading/moving from one hardware to another, from one provider to another or from one Moodle version to another, may involve a lot of other steps to plan, befor you actually move/upgrade/change provider/etc. In your case I would have seen two options: a) do a whole database dump, transfer this dump to your new provider for import and copy the whole yourMoodle/data directory also to your new provider. This would have lead to a true clone, i.e. an exact copy of your previous server . The problem here is, while this works fine to simply change hardware, while maintaining URLs and DNS the same as before, you will have to replace all TEXT in the database, containing the previous URLs if they change along with your new hosting b) make only backup-zip files of every course you are interested in. Copy all those backup-zip-files to your new server, e.g. into a course you call OLDcourses. From there you should be able to restore every single course. The advantage is, that the importer will automatically replace the old URLs from https://yourOld.moodle.com to https://yourNew.moodle.com - On the other hand the only risk here is to lose some of your files, if they are too big or if they are not correctly copied into the backup-zip-file. In both cases you have to solve the question how to transfer your big files or the whole of your data-directory to the new host. Please check the backup-settings on your previous/old server. Maybe you have to specifiy what files you want to include in your backup-zip-files, e.g. user pictures and the like. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 1.9 Course Files Backup Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: First things first, the unwanted courses should be backed up, placed on disk, put into safe, secure storage and then deleted from the Moodle. ALL unwanted or retired courses - as soon as they become unwanted. (Of course, there is an alternative, develop a separate Moodle to store unwanted courses and it is only used when someone wants something from it.) The tidiest way is to delete the unwanted courses, that makes your production site manageable. Courses can only be deleted when someone, with the neccessary permissions to delete courses, hits the delete button. Moodle cannot and does not make that sort of decision for any reason.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone!  We are getting ready this summer to do our first attempt at moving our 1.9 courses from an old server onto a new server running 2.1.  We chose 2.1 as our first "new" version because we understand it will do a good RESTORE with the zip files we create from our 1.9 courses.  So far, I think we are on the right page. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Create New User Credentials for 2.2?
ResponsesInList.Text:
hi Jim, there is a number ofifferent ways you can do this, but the best bet is to take a user dump from the v1.9 database . You can use phpMyAdmin if you have it or whatever you might use for your database administration tool. In phpMyAdmin using the home page, go to the SQL tab, run the query below, and it will probably set them into pages of about 30 lines, but that won't matter. Take out the data from the fields like this: 
```text
SELECT
 
`username`
 
,
 
`password`
 
,
 
`firstname`
 
,
 
`lastname`
 
,
 
`email`
 


FROM
 
`mdl_user`
```
 This should work as is, but it might demand a WHERE clause, shouldn't, but...  You can then export the resulting file as a CSV file, or CSV for Excel if you want to edit it. Save the file you can then upload the CSV file into your Moodle v2.x using Site Administration > Users > Accounts > Upload Users which allows you to upload the CSV file. If you want to edit the file, you can clear out all the existing passwords replacing them with "changeme" which forces the user to change their password, but that might not be a good idea. You can also go throught the file and delete out those users who have not continued with you. You can do a search on their names and delete them as you go before uploading the file.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Create New User Credentials for 2.2?
ResponsesInList.Text: BTW , the SQL should work in any Moodle SQL database, but the rest of the instructions pertain to phpMyAdmin only, or if youhave PostGres , then they should apply equally to phpPgSQLAdmin.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup Hangs at "Zipping backup"
ResponsesInList.Text: I was having the same issue with the backup of some courses hanging at "Zipping backup". I was able to solve it by going to Site Administration - Server - System Paths, and adding the path to the system's zip and unzip programs. (In this case, /usr/bin/zip and /usr/bin/unzip). The documentation for these fields states that if the field is blank, then Moodle uses it's internal routines to create the zip file. In my case, something in some of the courses was apparently causing these internal routines to fail. Once I configured the system zip path/program fields, the backups completed successfully. I don't know if this will work for you or not, but at least it is an easy fix to try. Hope this helps! Greg

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup Hangs at "Zipping backup"
ResponsesInList.Text: I had the same problem with some larger courses. There were some notes in other forums about this, but I've forgotten where. My workaround was to go to the /moodledata/temp/backup folder where there were folders named with numbers (unix time). In those folders were the moodle. xml file and folders named course_files/, site_files/, and other files like moddata/ if there were forums and resources. There was also a zip file but this was corrupt because it was in the process of zipping the other folders into it when the backup process stopped. So just compress the other folders and moodle.xml file into a new zip file; you don't need the corrupt zip file. Then move that new zip file to another location because the cron job will clean out the /temp/backup folder on one it's next runs (whenenver it's scheduled). This worked for me for large files <250 mb, I have yet to see how it worked on the 600 mb file (only because I didn't have time to download it yet and restore it). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: White screen when I restore
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Karen, The backup file for Moodle 2 is actually a zip file but has the extension of .mbz. I had a similar experience, but one of my own making. I assumed I downloaded a backed up course, an .mbz file, then tried to restore it, and it just seemed to stall, do nothng, I clicked something and got a white screen. I looked closely at the file and it was registering as being the right size. I eventually tried to unzip the file, as .mbz is an accepted format in WinZip, and it just caused an error and the message was something like, "nothing to unzip". I changed theformat to .zip and got the same message. The file registered as being the right size, but it did not have anything in it, and I still have no idea why. Moodle's clicking is a result of an additional layer of security. for Moodle2. Eventually as techniques are refined, I suspect the number of click to achieve anything is going to be reduced for some things. The backup/restore pages are a lot more mindful of what you want to be backed up and restore as well. I think we need to concentrate of the  flexibility that was not in v1.9, rather than the number of clicks in v2 it takes to back/restore something. You can now restore a v1.9 file to a v2 site so unless the file is corrupt, it should all work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: White screen when I restore
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, then let us assume that there was a glitch in the installation of the backup and restore functionality. This has happened before, so if you have access to the code, I suggest that you might want to install a test Moodle on your local machine of the same version as your production server . Once you have it installed, test the backup/restore functionality. If it works then in your production site, using FTP , delete the backup folder and replace it with the backup folder from your test site. This works as the HTML-PHP functionality is actually connectionless, that is it does not depend on attached executables to remain in memory. Once it is used it is forgotten about and not used until it is called again. If that does not work, then you are going to have to look at the PHP and Server, mm you might want to look at the logs before doing anything though, if the error is there, it might save some time. If you do not have access to the code, then talk to the admin who does. Discuss it with them and talk to them about this solution. It can work if the issue lies in Moodle, if it does not, then there is either something else wrong wth Moodle, or the PHP and/or Server is blocking it. BTW , just a thought, if you have access to the PHP.ini file, make sure the zip functionality is set to on, that has also happened.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 1.9 to 2.x: Missing activities when trying to restore in 2.x
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Justin Yes, that's the 'general process' when upgrading Moodle - if you have installed any plugins (Blocks, modules, reports, filters, etc.) then you should make sure you have the most up to date version of the plugin for your existing version of Moodle (in your case 1.9.x). The critical piece of information you may have missed here , is that no plugins created for Moodle 1.9.x will work in Moodle 2.x.  That is, the developer of the plugin has to recode the plugin to work with Moodle 2.x, and then release that new version. For some simple plugins that is fairly quick and easy. For others, it requires a complete re-write. Your example of Questionnaire is a good one.  This is developed and maintained by Mike Churchward, a long time Moodle Partner and development guru.  So it's not too surprising that he has made the effort to create the new version that will work with Moodle 2.x. However, there are many, many other plugins that were developed for Moodle 1.9 that will probably never be updated by the developer - either because they don't have time, or the plugin is not really needed for 2.x, or the individual doesn't work with Moodle anymore, etc. So, you can check on the plugins page to see if there IS a version for Moodle 2.x.  If there is, you should be able to install this after the upgrade, and find it works (although it's advisable to test this first). If there ISN'T an updated version of the plugin specifically released for Moodle 2.x then you won't get the functionaility, and you can't use the old 1.9 version.  You could look at the new functionality of Moodle 2.2.2 to see if you can use core functions instead?, and also look at alternative plugins that may do a similar job to what you used before. Stu

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore Single Course from Site Backup
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rob " Is there a way to restore a single course from a site backup? " No, you can't Restore a single Course from a Site Backup. A site backup is logically for restoring a complete site. You can however Backup individual Courses, and then later Restore a Course (or parts of it). " Would you ever need to do this? " A typical scenario might be if a Teacher has accidentally deleted a vital Resource in a Course (and they can't find the original). You could then Restore this Rescource from the Course Backup. " Is moodle_data just files? What information is stored in the database? " Yes, Moodle data contains the files. The database contains everything else, e.g. logs, actvities, course setup, users, etc. etc. You should be backing up both From your questions I think you need to read about Course Backups, which is different to Site Backup: http://docs.moodle.org/22/en/Course_backup http://docs.moodle.org/22/en/Course_restore And then make it all automatic... http://docs.moodle.org/22/en/Automated_course_backup Stu

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup cycle lasting more than 24 hours
ResponsesInList.Text: Oooh, it took me until this week to SEE where the BUG was. In SLES 11 you have TWO php.ini files, one in /etc/php5/apache2, which was the one I tuned during the last 5 years. Two years ago I had switched from calling Moodle's cron-job via apache to php-command-line. But everything worked fine until last year, when my backups began to last for ever and ever. Despite tuning max_memory and max_executiontime, I ended up with my backups not being finished at all and every backup showing an error. Last week, to my surprise, I entered /etc/php5/cli and saw there was ANOTHER php.ini with installation defaults. So I tuned it with the same values 30 secs and 1024M memory and my backups began to run normally again. 12 hours actually to create backups of 280GB of data. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course back up error
ResponsesInList.Text: As you might already know, Moodle.org is indexed by Google.  Used this Google search: site:moodle.org error/moodle/cannot finish ui if not setting ui and found several hits, but none seem to have exactly the same issue nor the same solution. The following are suggestions: A. It could be there was a resource/mod/block whatever used in that 1.9 course that's in-compat with version 2.  If you still have the 1.9 site up, consider removing non-core mod/block items in the course.  Back it up then TIA (try it again). If you don't have a 1.9 up and running can 'loan' you one I've up and running.  You could acquire an account and restore.  We could both inspect it then.  Contact me off list if you'd like to try that. B. Upload the 1.9 backup to a web accessible directory.  In your 2, turn on URL repo.  Then in any course, hit restore button and choose the URL repo as method.  Copy and paste the URL to the 1.9 backup in that web directory.  At the beginning of that process it will warn about the backup not being compatible and it will try first to convert the course to a 2 version and restore.  Restore to a new course - not the one you are in.  Might loose some things ... like mods you had in the 1.9 that aren't installed in the 2 ... but, most of the course is there to begin rebuilding. C. could unzip the backup zip and inspect the moodle. xml file for things like those addons.  One could edit the moodle.xml removing the offending items and also removing the files related or other related in the folders of the unzipped backup. Have to zip up the edited/unzipped backup again making sure the moodle.xml file is at the root of the zip when it's unzipped. 'spirit of sharing', Ken

If I remove some of the large video files, over 300MB, from the courses that fail the backup will complete sucessfully. If I look under the temp/backup directory on a failed backup there is a zip file of appropriate size. I can download and open this file, but a restore with the file fails. Here is the error information from one of the failed backups. Copying zip file An error occurred while copying the zip file to the course directory Stack trace: line 1664 of lib/deprecatedlib.php: call to debugging() line 73 of backup/backup_execute.html: call to error() line 135 of backup/backup.php: call to include_once() Any help with troubleshooting this problem would be greatly appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Large Course Backup Fails 1.9
ResponsesInList.Text: Have run into the same thing ... on CentOS server ... backup (about 4.3 gig) does complete and can find them in temp/backup but can't copy them back to the course ID folders in the data directory. So 'cheat' on it!  Only if, however, you've determined that the large backup zip is a complete and usable zip.  To test, copy the large backup.zip out of temp/backup/ into a test directory and unzip it.  If that succeeds, then shall assume the backup is good. Next, to restore it to a 1.9, manually move the backup zip into any course ID directory ... make sure permissions are set for apache to see/read it.  Go into that course ID and Files -> Backupdata.  Select the option to restore. The other option is to unzip in test.  Find the largest files and make an achive of them (zip/tar no diff).   Example: you find the 'assignments' folder is the largest.  Move the assignments.zip out of the test directory.   Just remember where the assignments.zip was located for manually moving it back into position. Re-zip the backup keeping the same folder structure - moodle. xml must be at the root of the extraction. Might use a slightly different name for the backup zip file.  Moodle 1.9 doesn't really care about the name of the .zip file to restore, as long as the structure of the zip meets the restore function in finding moodle.xml. Restore the in-complete backup. Before using the course, manually move back into the course the zip you archived separately and moved out.  Unzip, and check permissions on those files.  In other words, in keeping with the example: unzip the assignments.zip at the same location where you created it in the test folder. Have sucessfully restored a 4.3 gig course with tons of recorded videos that were submission of student assignments in this fashion. Hope this is making sense! 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Strangely large back up file - Moodle 2.2

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Strangely large back up file - Moodle 2.2
ResponsesInList.Text: Sarah, The file repository is a place where Moodle can get files from.  When you place files from a file repository into a Moodle course, the files are copied into the course. Moodle is not just pointing towards the file in the repository (because the contents of a repository can change at any time and there are different ways to configure file repositories). Because you didn't replace the videos in the course with the new smaller versions, the big files are still in the course. You will need to delete the big files from the course and re-add the new smaller ones. On a related note, its important to realize that a file repository can take up significant space on your server, and Moodle backup processes won't back up the repository itself. Moodle backups are just backing up courses.  You would stil need an alternative backup method to back up repositories on the server and other site files (whatever you do for normal server backups). Cheers! Melinda

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Strangely large back up file - Moodle 2.2
ResponsesInList.Text: You have to edit the activity or resource, or delete it completely and re-create. If you edit it, you are going to link to the new smaller files and remove the link to the large ones. As for the copying and pasting of files on the server that we all know and love from 1.9, that's no longer possible.  You have to do everything through the Moodle interface now.  There's lots of discussion about this in forums - just search on the File Picker. Just because it sounds like you ran your 1.9 install much like we did, I will offer how we manage large files. We don't have FTP enabled on our servers, so I created a single "large file upload " file system repository that serves a silimar function to the "old" way of copying files to the server.  I share that folder with faculty who have big files, and they map a drive to it so they can move their own files in (though most of the time we end up doing it becasue we are ususally digitizing video for them for htis purpose). There's a great help file in the Moodle docs for 2.2 that tells you how to set up a file system repository (there are different ways depending on your security needs and how you manage files).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Duplicating Courses - Course Links Not Updating
ResponsesInList.Text: Solved. This copy of Moodle was moved (the directory and database ) from another server. All of the courses had links containing the old server name, so when backed up on the new server, the links were not backed up properly (Moodle does a find and replace on the links based on the CURRENT server name). We backed up all of the courses on the old server and use the restore process to import them on the new server. Worked like a charm, and now we can duplicate courses on the new server without a problem. Hope this helps someone.

ResponsesInList.Title: MS SQL temp tables issue on large course backups 2.x

I'd posted about this before here http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=193694#p843670 My most recent troubleshooting attempts lead me to force the backup and restore process to use a normal table, not a temp table, so that I could see better what was happening and why my query wasn't returning. When I did this, the backup worked . My latest hypothesis is that because ms sql 's temp tables are tied to database sessions, if the process needs to reconnect to the db at some point, it will lose access to the temp tables it had created. Don't know if this is a sensible hypothesis. The issue of course with using non-temp tables is that because the backup/restore deletes and recreates the tables as it runs,  only one backup/restore can happen at a time, or they'll stomp over each other. Still, it allows our automated backups to work again, and we're getting some courses bigger than 1Gb getting backed up ok. Can anyone offer any other clues, or info I should check into before posting this in the tracker? It still feels vague and wooly to me.

To make matters worse the way in which the default collation for fields is defined when the table is created is really weird. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Orphan Backup files ??
ResponsesInList.Text: I think, if you configured the Backup-files to be stored all in one server -directory, then you will not be able to see them in the courses' file directory, as we were used to in Moodle 1.9 and lower. But the same thing applies to 1.9 if you selected to backup everything into one dir. You may safely remove the backup-zip-files, unless Moodle 2.x is taking supplementary steps to keep its names in the files table which it really does with contenthash, pathnamehash and mimetype. Sorting by mimetype will show you that the backup-zip-files have an own type: application/vnd.moodle.backup So, in my setup with backups scattered around in the new file system (not in one dir), they appear in this table and should hence be removed through the Moodle-GUI. Unless there would be a cleaning cron job, removing these entries from the files table as soon as a referenced file would not be present on the os' file system any more. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: add users from one moodle site to other
ResponsesInList.Text: Export table mdl_user dump, wich contains also the hashed passwords and import in the other database with mysql command line or phpMyAdmin or similar tools if you use another database. If you want to enrol in existing courses at the same time, export to users to csv file. The problem might be the password here, as userimport from cvs file asks fro plain-text passwords not encrypted yet. But you could set the same passwort for everyone here and ask the users to change their password after first login. I am not sure, but in user-import you might be able to "force password change" at first login. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: add users from one moodle site to other
ResponsesInList.Text: I just carried out Rosario's second option - exported users to csv, included a password column with the changeme password and uploaded users to the new Moodle. I then exported (from Moodle 2.0.6) courses with all enrolled users, files, conditional activities etc and restored to new Moodle install (Moodle 2.2.2) and our users have access to all their course resources and their completed (or uncompleted) conditional activities. The restored courses has everything there, including user groups and groupings, as long as you include the appropriate information when backing up the courses. Cheers Ali

ResponsesInList.Text: Please be careful in changing/deleting things directly in the database because there are a lot of relational links between the different tables. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Files stored in Moodle data corrupt
ResponsesInList.Text: Doesn't FTP in ASCII mode mangle \n -> \r\n or vice versa? I think you need to make sure you use FTP in binary mode. Or, better, use a more sophisticated backup tool like rsync.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Files stored in Moodle data corrupt
ResponsesInList.Text: What version of Moodle you used to create the backup? What version you restoring to? The issue though, may have nothing to do with that either. Also, a judgement call. I have found that using Microsoft Word is not as stable as it could be, even in Word itsef. I prefer to use Adobe plugins for Word documents to export the files in the  *.pdf format.  I then use the *.pdf in the Moodle. This resolves any number of issues. If I need a response, then either Students create their own docs, which I ask for in the pdf format, or if I want it online, then I create an online text assignment. Most students are familiar with the pdf format and will save and upload files in that format. I have not had any problems with corruption of files since I started this regime.

Upgrading means to a Moodler this: http://docs.moodle.org/en/Upgrading . And transfering content is usually http://docs.moodle.org/en/Import_and_export_FAQ . And there is a third possibility, recreating the course manually in the new Moodle site. That is the most prudent solution for a compromised server. Usually which upgrade path, 1.5 -> ? -> ? -> 1.9 -> ? is a big discussion. See http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=197602 . You are on Linux but never mentioned the distribution. If it is Debian or a derivative this article might be useful: http://docs.moodle.org/en/Installing_Moodle_on_Debian_based_distributions .

ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you for the suggestion Mary. I had never set up a repository before and I was able to create an effective work flow. For those of you interested, this was the process I used: Follow the directions in Mary's link above to set up a repository. I created a repository folder in my moodledata folder and created a backup sub directory in that folder. Backup individual courses in your Moodle 1.9 install. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup restore with ssh
ResponsesInList.Text: I have written sort of a how-to somewhere in these forums because I changed hardware several times since 2004. And I also changed several times the Moodle-Data-Disk to offer more space to our users. Either you search for it for the details or you follow this rough instructions: do a daily dump of the database (or even twice a day) do a backup to tape of your database dump and both Moodle directories (one containing the php-files and one containing the data-files) if your server crashes, total loss or partial loss due to hardware or software problems of any kind: set up your OS, apache, mysql , php, etc. on new hardware configure network interface and IP as on old hardware copy/restore configuration files of php, apache, my sql , etc. to new hardware lock down your mysql-server configure apache to work fine copy/restore your database dump to new hardware and import the database dump copy/restore the Moodle-php directory and Moodle-data directory to new hardware configure any owner and access rights on these directories and files access your moodle server with a browser if you need to change the data-disk: mount old and new data-disk at the same time do an xcopy/cp/rsync of the whole data-direcotory of Moodle to the new disk there are copy switches to keep owner and access rights or you reconfigure them unmount the old data disk, but keep it for safety another 3 months or so check Moodle's config.php file to adjust the data-directory if needed (on linux I do mount both disks as /moodleData and /moodleDataNew or similar. Then I dismount the old one and rename and remount /moodleDataNew to /moodleData) Alternatively, if you want to change hardware and install the newest Moodle Version, do it and then simply copy every backup-zip-file to a course-FILE-directory to restore the needed courses from there. Pay attention, this works only in Moodle 1.x If you wanted to change to Moodle 2.x you need new Moodle 2.x backup-zip-files, unless using a third party backup-import-script/utility to import 1.9x backup-zip-files. And last, if you want only one course, copy the backup-zip-file onto a running Moodle-Server's data/courseDirectory and restore it with the Admin-Block-Restore function in that particular course. On a Moodle-Test-Server, or any Moodle-Server of a friend, etc. Rosario

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving moodle 1.9.9 on a new moodle which is 2.x
ResponsesInList.Text: Before you do anything like that though, I seriously recommend that you set up an Apache server, PHP and mySQL on your own computer, install a v1.9.9 and a v2.2 and see the differences in the set up. Test everything there first. What you do there will help you on your production site. Before you install anything on your production server, test it on your local computer. On your computer, create two folders, one called moodle19 and the other moodle22, then copy the installers to their respective folders. Install the v 1.9.9 and test to make sure that it is working properly. There is only one thing you need to do in the v1.9.x after installation, go to: Administration > Server > Session Handling and in the cookie prefix add something like m199 Then install your new v2.2 Moodle, and the first thing you do is go to Site administration > Server > Session handling and in the cookie prefix add something like m22 This means that your two Moodles can happily coexist, their session cookies will not clash. This will also mean that you have 2 databases, one for the v1.9.9 and one for the v2.2.x. As you now have the two Moodles you can test them out so you can learn things about installation and administration there. This also means you will do nothing that interferes with your production site - until you are ready to upgrade the site to v2.x. I also suggest that you keep the test server going after you upgrade, for the same reasons, test everything there first. Download some backups of some courses from your site, three or four at most. Restore them into both Moodles, see what works, what does not. If you are using v1.9.9 backups to restore to your v2.2, then you can see where the problems may exist. You can also get used to updating your v2.2.x site to v2.2.x+1, then to v2.3 so when ready, you can update your production site easily. Practice first, practice makes you better, practice, practice, practice as my old Farnarkling coach used to say, and when you have played a match, practice some more he would go on, and on, and on, and on.... I think there was an issue on GoDaddy with the PHP version and Moodle 2.x, but I would assume they have resolved that, I have not seen it come up recently. From memory, GoDaddy uses Cpanel, which has as a native tool phpMyAdmin , so you can look at the databases and see the differences between them. You can locate and download then install this same program to your new web server on your computer. It is a very handy tool to know and use. Oh, to find out how to create an Apache, PHP, MySQL server, or a WAMP if you are using Windows, go to these video tutorials . Although Sulinski is using Windows Vista, the same principles apply to Windows 7. The only thing you need to change is that you need a database that is an InnoDB and uses a utf-8_general_ci collation, not a developers database. The rest is easy, and the latest version of PHP can be installed as Sulinski displays it in the video.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automated backup is not working in Moodle 2.2
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Emadof I think I understand what you want: a weekly course-by-course backup of the whole site. That collection of course backups is not meant as a site backup rather for situations where an individual course needs to be restored to an old state. The problem with this approach is, the php driven backup process is very very inefficient. We had cases where powerful servers taking more then 24 h for the backup and thereby overtaken by the next backup process. OK, you have a dead line of 7 days, but that shouldn't mean your server may struggle with itself rater than servicing the visitors. A full site backup from the shell is much faster, you can script it and schedule for early hours so that the visitors won't notice anything. The disadvantage is of course you need to restore the whole site even if you need just one course. But the restore process could too be scripted, if necessary on the spare machine. Then you can manually backup the particular course from there without disturbing the production machine. And you avoid mishaps like this "the story of the misteriously filling up hard disk" http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=191275 ! All these are common Unix system administration tasks, I might post more information if the time permits.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: accidentally lost my main site ...........
ResponsesInList.Text: I know of no utility that will help repair the Role, but I suspect that quite likely you have managed to interfere with permissions somehow so you may have to fix it manually. Can you add in a new Admin account? If you have access to the database I would suggest that you select a test user, which most Moodles have left in the database, and see if you can update the account to an Admin account. Test what happens when it is logged in. If that is not working then in your test Moodle, have a look at what is different between the permissions tables, the Roles tables and the user tables. If you have no test Moodle then create one on a local machine. Once you locate the tables you need and made a comparison, edit your production site to mirror your test site, for your main role in those tables. Keep going on with it, until you bring it back to what it should be. I base this on your earlier comment that ordinary Users can still access courses, but Admins cannot. So is it something that existing accounts cannot do and new ones will be OK? Or do you have to go back to the start? Good luck....

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: accidentally lost my main site ...........
ResponsesInList.Text: There may be an issue with passwords and/or Roles. Go to the database and the User table. Copy the password for the guest user. Even if you do not allow guests, that should still be there. It is, encoded but you can paste it into your record in the user table, the password field, obviously. I tested this in another moodle and it worked there. The password for Guest is guest. If this works then there was something wrong with your password. While you are there, in the database, check your User ID number, the first field in the row containing your name. Look for the role_assignments table and look for your id number. I may appear more than once, but the role_id field should read 1. If it does not then somehow your Role has been changed. Once you have confirmed that you are still an admin, then go and try the password thing. This is pretty much a process of elimination until you can get to access the appropriate pages. Another thing you can do is go into the backup moodle.xml file, it can be opened and edited with a text editor. Look for your admin role there and see if it is properly assigned. If not, then edit your Role properly or delete delete it. Check to see all the course materials are actually there btw . Save the file, rezip it. Can Teachers get into the right pages? Can they edit? If so, then using FTP , you should be able to access the moodledata folder. replace the zip file in the backup data subfolder in that course. Use a Restore to delete and replace the exiting course, perhaps that will do it for you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: accidentally lost my main site ...........
ResponsesInList.Text: It is hard doing this if you cannot turn error messages on and get Moodle to tell you what is happening. So we need patience here. One source of information can be the server logs, have you checked them? There are usually three areas that can cause this kind of issue, Roles and Permissions, PHP and code. The fourth is that the server environment is interfering in the zip process, but that is a longshot. Go through your php.ini file and check that it has not been moved too far from its original. You might be better off deleteing it and replacing it with an older backup - one you know works. Assuming that the issue lies with the code to the backup and restore rather than permissions and roles, (and I assume you are still using v1.9), then you can restore all the code in the backup folder. Unzip your Moodle installer files on a test server, and set it up, if you do not have one. The Moodle code is exactly the same for all Linux environments, irrespective of the server, the machine, the OS. I have done this from my Windows box to a Linux server and it still works. Delete the code in the Backup folder and FTP the code from your Test server Backup folder into the now empty folder. That will take out any defective or corrupted code, which can happen if someone tries to shut down a backup when it is running, not often, but it can happen. You can repeat this process for everything, as long as you retain the config.php file, which will update, refresh, your entire Moodle. At some point you will eradicate the problem, unless it is in the php link between the backup code and the zip program, or the zip program itself. If you can get to Administration > Server >System Paths you might be able to refresh the connection to your Zip program. EDIT: thinking, thinking... mmm  this, to me, is now cascading. Might be better off replacing your entire code and clearing all the caches.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: accidentally lost my main site ...........
ResponsesInList.Text: Then it has to be that something has gone wrong at the server level. What has changed? These things do not just happen, there is a reason. Usually where there is something this catastrophic it means someone other than the Moodle Admin has done something in the server environment that has had a negative impact on the Moodle. One of my servers, someone turned on Magic Quotes in the php.ini file and it took me too long to pick up on it, by the time I did, the Moodle was essentially wrecked, (by me looking for this problem everything I did made it worse ), but easily fixed, the database and moodledata folder backups got us out of strife. I replaced the code and it added the backups and it was working again - after the magic quotes were turned off. ResponsesInList.Text: In the Apache shell? Has someone edited the httpd.conf file? Have you any previous site backups? Standard backup policy for v1.9 should be the database, the moodledata folder, do not need to worry too much about the code, but the others should be done regularly, weekly if considered appropriate, no more than monthly even on a moodle that does not change much or rapidly. Same with v2.x when you upgrade. Daily with big sites. (but is real easy to say when someone else has to do it. Create your own backup policy, and stick to it.) If you have admin access to the server, then you can install and use phpmyAdmin to back the database up, then a zip to backup the moodledata folder. Look carefully at the moodledata folder's structure. Use the course table in the database as a comparison. At least you will see if the moodledata folder has been corrupted. Compare the id numbers to the moodledata folder structure. 1.9 does not reuse course ids so they should match the moodledata folder. If they match then you are in with a real chance. In the meantime, look in the moodledata folder where the faulty backup started and delete anything that resembles the backup file.  Delete all your code and upgrade it, just do not delete the existing config.php file, reuse it. That should get rid of whatever the issue is. When you get back online, go into the course and go through it with a finetooth comb. Gawd.. hope this works, I am really running out of ideas... sorry.. And no, by the time I figured out the real issue, I could not log on, but I still had access to the Apache server, which was the only thing that got me out of it.

Re: accidentally lost my main site ...........
ResponsesInList.Text: OK, then all is not lost. How does the moodledata folder compare to the epo.mdl_course table? Do the id numbers match the folder structure? If they do, and you are sure that the data in the subfolders is good, then you can replace your entire Moodle code, except the config.php file, with new code. FTP into the Moodle code, delete it, and then upload the replacement code, I prefer to have it already unzipped. Here is the hard part for most people to get their heads around. the database, the moodledata folder and the codebase are actually three separate identities. We are used to programs that are self contained, but Moodle, as a PHP-App, is not. You can easily change the codebase, as it is the least important and most adaptable, of the three identities, without negatively affecting the other two parts. This should put you back on track. The config.php file is the lynchpin of Moodle, all elements revolve around that, so if you do not change that, and make sure it is clean, it should just operate the code normally when you go into it. I recommend that you test this out for yourself on your test Moodle, it normally does not take long. Once you are happy it works, then do it in your production site.

This is a real catch 22 then, it won't work properly until it is fixed, but it can't be fixed until it is working properly.. there is some logic here, but who's I am not sure.. .. PHP Applications are not handled like programs. The connectionless nature of PHP, HTML and so on allows the disparate elements of Moodle to be interdependent not dependent as they are in an exe program?  Upgrading a PHP-App usually changes only the code, everything else remains the same, except where the database is altered for efficiency or security reasons. The data remains untouched and the moodledata folder is never altered. If there is anything critical here it would have to be the config.php file, and that can actually be rebuilt if you loose it and not try and reinstall Moodle. The codebase is the least important and most easily remedied of the three elements of Moodle. Je ne comprend pas! A flat file contains a set of Users with their courses, it is uploaded and should not interfere with the User in the database, but should add their course enrollments. A csv file really, with the field names in the first row and User details in the next. username,password,firstname,lastname,email,role1,course1,course2 tom.smith,changeme,Tom,Smith,tom.smith@home.org,student,Algebra,Forensics henry.jones,,Henry,Jones,henry@nyt.com,student,Photoshop,10Maths The second data row, and you are going to have to check this in you own Moodle to make sure it works, has no password set. When you use the csv file you start by going to: Administration > Users > Accounts > Upload Users Browse for the csv file with the data in it. then click the Upload Users button. This will take you to this screen: You can see from the above that the password field for Henry is blank. You then need to change some settings: The Upload Type and New User password fields both need to change. Also, the Existing User details can be altered if required. Then click the Upload users button and when it is complete, you should see something like this: The Upload Users results screen will give you all the information you need to see if it worked or not. You can apply this same technique at any time, btw, works everytime

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Trying to Restore a course to a new site - seems limited by 2MB file size
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello. I think that there are several threads (maybe docs?) regarding increasing upload file size (it requires changes in php.ini, maybe also in apache configuration, and maybe also in another locations). But, it you just want to "get things done" or can't change php/apache configuration, and you have file access (direct or via FTP /Webdav/...) to the "moodledata" directory, you can copy the file directly in the "course files" area of your course, and then access it from inside Moodle. If you look at the URL of your courses, there is and "id=X" parameter (X can be any number, usually low). This is the unique id of that course. Inside the moodledata directory, there are numbered directories: each one contains the files of the course with that id. The course=1 is always the frontpage AFAIK . If you copy a file inside any of that directories, you will see it in the "course files" area of that course, and you can use it normally. Hope this helps. Greetings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Strange Log Error Message on Backup with CRON
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Hartmut, Sorry, only saw this message of yours now. I guess at this time you've already found the answer, but just in case, I'll post one here: Granting privileges on MySQL database can be done in various ways. Here is a way to do it in command line on My SQL : mysql> grant all privileges on dbname.* to 'username'@'localhost' identified by 'password'; where dbname - is your moodle database name, username is your mysql user that accesses moodle database name, localhost is the location of your database server. localhost should be used if mysql is located at the same server as your webserver. and password is a password for your moodle user. You can also use graphical clients for mysql, like phpMyAdmin , to manage access options - they usually come as standard with various hosting options. See http://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.1/en/adding-users.html for more information dealing with mysql user access rights. Regards, Alexander

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup in Moodle 2.2 Localhost
ResponsesInList.Text:
Ansley, If you're using XAMPP you're in a Unix environment, right? So, knowing that there are only three things you need to take account of (moodle code, moodle data, database) here's how I make a complete site backup to move to a production server: Backup moodledata `htdocs $ tar --exclude-from=exclude-mdata.txt -cvzf moodledata.tgz moodledata/` where exclude-mdata.txt: 
```text
cache/
sessions/
temp/
trashdir/



I have found in practice that it's best to exclude these directories from the tar file -- they get created automatically when moodle starts up again
```
 Backup moodle code: `markp$ tar -cvzf moodlecode.tgz moodle/` dump the database 
```text
markp$ 
MAMP
/Library/bin/mysqldump -u moodlebackup -p -CQe moodle_db  >moodledb.sql
```
 You really want to use the Unix command line utilities such as tar & mysqldump IMO . There are tons of online help besides the man pages. To restore on another server perhaps or in a different location. It's really important for you to understand the relative locations of moodlecode and moodledata. This will vary according to the configuration of your server. The moodledata directory should NEVER be placed inside moodlecode. My setup is /homes/mark/htdocs/moodle (for the code) and /homes/mark/moodledata for the data. Notice the relative positions. unpack the moodle code : tar -xvf moodlecode.tgz unpack moodledata : cd .. ; tar -xvf moodledata.tgz Now import the database -- you'll need to have already created a new database using either the mysql command or phpmyadmin. `mysql -u root -p -D moodle2_db <moodledb.sql` Tweak the ownership and permissions of moodledata to make sure that the Apache process can read and write. For example, if on your machine apache runs as user:group www:www then : change ownership $ sudo chown -R mark:www moodledata change permissions $ chmod -R 770 moodledata these will make moodledata have write access for the Apache process. Now edit moodle/config.php and change the paths, database details and web URL for this cloned installation. Now and only now open the URL in Firefox . It should start up exactly where you left off. I've done this dozens of times and have found that it's well worth learning to do this the Unix way! Hope this helps. Mark PS I hope it's obvious that the locations and filenames I use are for illustration only. They WILL be different on your set up so you need to use some common sense to figure out where things go or where they are run from.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving Users
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes you can, but it can be a litttle bit convoluted, or easier, depends on how you want to do it. You cannot use the Front Page backup to get the passwords, but you can use phpMyAdmin . In the old Moodle, open the database and go to the users table. Open the table and then go to Export and dump the data to an sql file. Repeat the process with your v2 install. You have two options here, open the files using a spreadsheet, Excel or Calc, and copy the user data to the v2 file. This may take a while as you have to make sure the fields are in the same order. There are additional fields in v2 that you need to account for in the data, some fields will be renamed. You have to fix these exactly right or it is not going to work. Depending on how many users you actually have, you may want to make the two dumps exactly the same in data and then run the sql file back to the v2 using just the insert data statement. Alternatively, with a lot of users it may be easier for you to delete non-essential columns and rows, save the important parts as a csv file and upload that as a flat file. The main parts are "username, password, firstname, lastname, email" but you may want to add in additional fields like idnumber or cohort. For me, idnumber and cohort represent unique identifiers and can be used throughout the moodle. In cohort, which will not be there, you may add in something that will differentiate staff from students say, or year levels, or anything unique to a group. Or you may want to addin a unique idnumber, which you can do easily using incrementing numbers. Or if you already have a student idnumber in place, then you may want to use that. Whatever you do, in using a csv file, you will have to clean up any single or double quotemarks or unneccessay commas in the spreadsheet and then save the file as a csv file. If I had anything more than 25 users, I would go with the csv file, much easier to delete stuff than it is to make sure every row is exactly right.  Use the technique described here , it will work as you want it to.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Looking for Automated Site Backup Software
ResponsesInList.Text: Here is a shell script to base your own off of. It runs on the server and handles the sql dump and copys your moodle pages and sql dump to another drive or location on the server machine. If you are using OS X you can get Carbon Copy Cloner to handle the backup to your home automatically to connect to the server and sync with your hard drive at home. It runs on your home machine and downloads on a schedule for you. It only backs up changes, not the whole site every time. I like doing it on a separate drive so my backup to my office is not hitting the server files at all while other people are accessing it. It also allows me to have a backup drive to swap out if the server main drive goes bad. All I need is someone at the server to swap it instead of transfering the backups to there. #!/bin/sh # paths for backups pathtosqlbackup="/put your path here/sql_backup_location/"; pathtowebsiteoriginal="/put your path here/Website/"; pathtowebsitebackup="/put your path here/web_backup/Website/"; # mysql user name dbuname="name for database"; # mysql password dbpwd="password for database"; # mysql db name dbname="moodle db name"; # mysql host name # name for backup folder date and time stamped foldername=`date ''+%Y-%m-%d-%H-%M-%S''` # Backup SQL (if it's Sunday) day=`date ''+%u''` # if [ $day = 7 ]; # then echo backing up sql .... # echo message echo backup script // processing .... # navigate to backup dir if cd $pathtosqlbackup then echo ... successfully navigated to Backup Dir! else echo ... Backup Dir NOT Mounted! Exiting Script #exit script with error exit 0 fi # echo message echo ..... making export directory # create directory for the current backup script if mkdir $foldername then echo .......... exporting directory successfully created # chmod the directory chmod 777 $foldername fi # echo message echo ...... exporting SQL dump if # dump the db into a .sql file in the directory mysqldump --user=$dbuname --password=$dbpwd --flush-logs --lock-tables $dbname > $pathtosqlbackup$foldername/$dbname.sql; then # echo message echo ...... SQL dump file created successfully else # echo message echo ...... mysqldump error! exit 0 fi # echo message echo ...... compressing SQL dump file # navigate into folder cd $foldername # compress and gzip tar -cf $dbname.tar $dbname.sql if gzip $dbname.tar then echo .......... $dbname.tar successfully gzipped rm $dbname.sql echo .......... $dbname.sql successfully removed echo backup script // finished .... fi # fi echo backing up web .... launchctl unload /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/org.apache.httpd.plist rsync -av --delete $pathtowebsiteoriginal $pathtowebsitebackup launchctl load /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/org.apache.httpd.plist echo finished backing up web and settings .... echo ---- backup complete! ----

As you are keeping 20 copies of Moodle data in your local disk, it will take more space unnecessarily. I want to suggest you to use a backup software to take incremental backup of your Moodle data. You can download the Moodle data to local system and take incremental backup to backup the modified bytes alone. So, eventually it will take less disk space only. ResponsesInList.Text: Couple of ways to do this.  First one might work better with your existing backup deal.  A while back, we were having trouble with backups thinking they were all ready running and so someone came up with a line that you could add directly to the automated backup php file.  I think you could do the same to get your maintenance mode enabled.  You would need to place the following code at the beginning of the backup/util/helper/backup_cron_helper.class.php file.  I am running on 2.0.1 and similar changes have worked for me though I have not tested this exact one. UPDATE `<database_name>`.`mdl_config` SET `value` = '1' WHERE `mdl_config`.`name` = 'maintenance_enabled' LIMIT 1; Then place the same command at the end but SET value to 0. Not sure exactly how it would look in an sh script but if you have that partially written already, you could log into mysql from the script and change the field as follows: #!/bin/sh mysql -u YOURDATABASEUSER -pYOURPASSWORD YOURDATABASE <<EOF UPDATE mdl_config SET value = '1'  WHERE mdl_config.name = maintenance_enabled EOF You might have to play with it a little - my coding expertise is pretty much  what I can find from someone else and then adapt to my needs.  I always make a copy of whatever php file I am messing with before I adapt any core code so I can put it back if (or maybe when!) I break something!  Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: back up and restore from moodle 1.9 to moodle 2.0
ResponsesInList.Text: Conversionthingy is very limited to Windows with its insistence on using Microsoft's .Net technologies - for me, a waste of time writing a potentially good utility, like using a Bugatti Vayron car body with a two stroke motor. mmm I got the sense that you are looking at upgrading the now defunct Moodle? I am assuming that you mean a really old version of Moodle... if it is before a v1.6.9 then you have a serious problem. You can go to Downloads and download v1.6.9 and try to update, then v1.7.7 and update again, then v1.8.14 repeating the updates then arriving at v1.9.15+. Once there, you can then take your courses, and backing them up, restore to your v2.2 - or if you are not on v2.2 then update to that version as well.  This is not an easy process and there are a number of serious pitfalls along the way. I suggest that you manually zip your moodledata folders, before starting, just in case. Also, backup afdtger every update and store them off somewhere else. I suggest that you do not include user data or user files. This may or may not work, but it clearly demonstrates the value of constantly updating, or rather, planning a program of regular updates, say a few as one a year, or to as many as one every month. If you cannot update your older Moodle, then you may have to have someone strip out all the text and manually adapt them to Moodle v1.9.15. While this is time consuming, it is actually not a terribly difficult task. Create a set of courses that shows you what your file structures look like. You can directly upload any files or images that your courses require. Such things as labels and the like, the bells and whistles, are not essential but the assignments, the quizzes, the resources and such you may be able to replicate them in the v1.9.15+ and circumvent the longer and more tedious process of rewriting all your courses. What you can then do is to make sure that you know where everything is going to go in a moodle. xml file and you can rewrite your own to include all the appropriate data. Just do the text materials. Alternatively, you can replicate your courses, one at a time, manually. Any way you do this, it is going to cost you time and money. Good luck.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: restore.php not found
ResponsesInList.Text: After playing around with this for a while, I think I found the problem. The course description looks like it was pasted from another document. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring a course created in 1.9 into moodle 2.0
ResponsesInList.Text: Larry: User error is unlikely: there's little you can do wrong and much it can get wrong. The issue you're having is a problem with the conversion: somewhere the process didn't see something coming and didn't deal with it well. If you view the HTML file--it's the conversion log--there may be some indication there of where a problem occurred or was anticipated. If there's no problem indicated, then there's a good chance the program is blissfully unaware that it's not making any sense.  If I were to guess, I'd speculate that you've got some question types it can't deal with, some resources or activities it's never seen before, some group/groupings assignments to content that it doesn't figure out. If you were to create a series of several backups from the original course--each containing discrete course componentes--and then run each of those through the process, you'd probably be able to identify the point of failure.  But that's an awful lot of work if waiting patiently is an option... Peter

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring a course created in 1.9 into moodle 2.0
ResponsesInList.Text: Larry: It turns out that this isn't actually a ConversionThingy 2 problem, but a timeout issue on the server.  I ran into the problem myself four times last night, as files which had restored perfectly on a development server suddenly failed to restore at all on a production server.  A quick look at the PHP settings showed that the dev server had a cosy excess in its maximum execution time (set to 300), while the production server had the max execution time set to 30. I'd speculate that all you need to do is increase PHP's max execution time setting on the server. The long processing time seems to accompany large question banks: a tiny Moodle2 backup file will demand a considerable restoration time if it contains a significant number of question bank categories/questions.  (I ran a 1.5MB backup file which had a couple of pages, a couple of quizzes, 47 question bank categories and 2200 questions: it took 3.5 minutes.) And because the restoration of a course site apparently starts with question bank processing, if it times out in that part of the job, the error message that gets triggered (usually something along the lines of sections failing to restore) is valid, as far as it goes, but it doesn't actually address the problem: the sections weren't restored because the process ran out of time. In the case of the file that was failiing for you, Larry, over 3000 questions in 438 question bank categories pretty much sealed the fate of the restoration timeout if you're running at a default max execution time of 30.  Crank that up to 300, and the site should restore.  You also, that way, get time to go out an get a cup of coffee while you're waiting... Peter

ResponsesInList.Text: I figured out a very effective way to restore a course created in Moodle 1.9 to Moodle 2.0. ConversionThingy didn't work at all for me. Using VirtualBox I set up Moodle 1.9.4 on an Ubuntu 10.04 virtual machine. The only tricky part was installing older versions of PHP packages, which I got from here . I saved the state of the virtual machine so I could use it again. I then restored the course. I had to increase upload_max_filesize in /etc/php5/apache2/php.ini because the backup file was quite large. Next I updated to Moodle 2.0. This only took a few minutes. I ran Update Manager (to get the newest versions of the PHP packages), made a copy of config.php, deleted everything in /var/www, unzipped the latest Moodle package into /var/www, copied config.php back, restarted Apache and then when I went to the Moodle home page on my virtual machine the upgrade happened automatically. The first time I tried this I was pretty excited because I thought I only had one step to go. I wanted to backup the course from Moodle 2.0 on my virtual machine so I could use it on a live site, but it didn't work. On this forum I found the solution - the maximum execution time was too low. In php.ini I increased max_execution_time to 300, then I could finally backup the course. I ended up with an 'mbz' file which I then restored to a live site. I can now reuse the virtual machine to do this again and again because I've saved the state of the machine just after installing Moodle 1.9.4 on it - I'm ready to convert more courses!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup all users profiles
ResponsesInList.Text: Of course there is, and it depeneds on what you want to do it with. I have techies who take care of this, but I understand we run a three-tiered backup policy. Courses are taken care of by their Authors, their maintainers. This can be the course itself with or without user data and files - up to the maintainer. The site is backed up occasionally, but I am not real sure this is necessary - the nature of Moodle is such that keeping updates current is usually sufficient to maintain the site and its files. The last is the most tricky, get this wrong and it all falls apart. Backup your database and include a copy of the Moodledata folder. I would recommend using phpMyAdmin for the database and you can please yourself with the Moodledata folder.User details/profiles etc are all kept in the database. User files are usually kept in the Moodledata folder. This is the largest backup, and I understand we use a tape drive and it is an overnight job. You can use the native cron job, but I think I would prefer to have complete control over it, that way I know I can get it done. It also backs up what i want backed up, and ignores anything i don't want backed up.

ResponsesInList.Title: full moodle installation backups
ResponsesInList.Text: I am searching for the perfect tool for creating moodle installation backups. I am using a simple mysql backup script for creating Monthly, Weekly en Daily full backups for all our Moodle installations. My sql backups are relatively small so there is no problemen keeping lots of backups. I would like to have an easy way to do daily full moodle codebase and moodledata folder backups that uses a minimal amount of disk space. What tools do you use? Oh, most of our Moodle installs are on Ubuntu server , but we do host on Windows if we have to.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: full moodle installation backups
ResponsesInList.Text: A tool called backupninja might solve all your backup needs. You can find it´s website here: https://labs.riseup.net/code/projects/backupninja - but is part of ubuntu, so aptitude install backupninja will give you all it´s magic powers. However, you should also think about a valid restore strategy - if you do only daily backups that means that will always loose at least 24 hours of data - on sites with many users and lots of discussions going on etc. this might be inacceptable. More complex setups of realtime-backups might involve database synchronization, like a master-slave setup for mysql or backing up the database write-ahead-log (WAL) of PostgreSQL - you can realize a good point-in-time recovery with these kind of setups, but it is more complex to setup and take care about. Good Luck! Bughunter

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: full moodle installation backups
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Bughunter, I have chosen rsnapshot for creating backups using the minimum amount of space. Rsnapshot makes a full copy of your backup folders. It is scheduled through a cronjob and can create daily, weekly an monthly backups. It's greatest feature is the ability to use hardlinks when creating an incremental backup. This ensures you have all backupdata in one place and your daily backup look like a full backup. You can use rsnapshot on a remote server and instruct it to create backups of linux servers using ssh. You will need to setup a key base authentication to your LAMP servers and make sure your backup server is very secure. For mysql I have written my own script that simply creates daily, weekly and monthly  full backup of every database available. We are working on an extra Moodle server that will have realtime synchronisation. It will not depend on a mysql master slave setup, we will be using a DFS, destributed file system, in combination with linux heartbeat. Every write action to a linux block device (the harddisk) will be duplicated to a slave server. If the master server dies the slave server simply mounts the local DFS disk and starts up the mysql / apache processes. See: https://help.ubuntu.com/community/HighlyAvailableLAMP We will need to test if this is really working and does not corrupt databases. If it works I think it might be a very elegant solution. Thanks again for your advice Bas Brands

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: full moodle installation backups
ResponsesInList.Text: I had a simple script to tar sqldump.sql, $moodle and $moodledata to a single file for each Apache virtual server. A remote machine fetched them via scp, and kept only 7 daily, 4 weekly and 12 monthly files. All of them were full backups. Can't claim to be the "perfect solution" but it did the job for years. The Highly Available LAMP you pointed out, is very interesting. I wonder whether it'll affect the performance though.

ResponsesInList.Text: As I say, this is off-topic, but I am taking the bait. All XAMPP is, is a quick and convenient way to install Apache + MySQL + PHP on top of any OS. As such, it provides a great way for people to get Moodle running on their own PC so they can test out new features, or, in my case, do developemnt. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Some Confusion on Backup
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dennis, this is like a lot of things in Moodle, once you understand what is happening, then it becomes easy. It like pushing against an open door very frustrating until you can see it is open. Also, if you are the Admin of the Moodle on a large intranet then it may not be your problem to back it up in its entirety, talk to your techies, that may be their problem. Moodle backups really come in three parts, the moodledata folder, the moodle code and the database. Backups occur at course level and site level and they can be subdivided to suit each need. If you want to do a site backup, then you are backing up all parts of the site and you are better off using a specific tool, whatever your favourite tool is, to cover everything you want. You can backup the code, but there is really no point, you should already have stored somewhere the code anyway. Or you can download and install the latest version - less than 22 minutes the last time I did it from starting the download to begin to restore the first courses - on a server btw . Specific tools, like phpMyAdmin are excellent to backup just the database, the tables without data, the data without tables or the tables and data, suit yourself. Course backups can be done internally, by Admins or by Teachers, either one. You can backup the course files, in whole or in part, the user files, in whole or in part, or the both as a whole lot, or any part thereof. You can suit yourself with the flexibility. Moodle does really not back itself up in its entirety, it can but a dedicated backup tool is a better option. As for the error message, it really does not make too much difference, but to get rid of the message, go to the Zend site and download the latest release, untar or unzip it and copy the php_mysql.dll file to your php/ect folder and update yours. That should take care of that issue. Alternatively, you may want to download the latest release of PHP and update it. This might not be for you to decide so talk to your techies let them know what is happening, it give them a chance to sort it.

ResponsesInList.Text: Dennis - I am in a similar situation as you, a new administrator.  The guy who i replaced had some things documented, but i am asking similar questions that you are. We store the DB separate from the application instance.  On our DB server, i am using MySQL administrator, and have a weekly scheduled task that backs up all 6 of our different moodle dbs into a single backupfile ( i keep three copies of it - in case one became corrupt and killed the lastest backup)  We have 6 different moodle sites and 6 different moodle db instances - so this is how we *automate them into a single task.  If I needed to restore one of the db's, i could load the backup file and parse through it using the MySQL administrator GUI - selecting the specific db and even the specific tables, if i only needed to restore part of the db.  If our entire db server crashed, I could restore all 6 of the dbs from one backup file. I am trying to figure out the best way to handle the per course backup, pushing that responsibility to the teachers as much as poss.  I do like the option as a *emergency backup, the automated course backup procedure mentioned in Mary previous post. http://docs.moodle.org/19/en/Automated_course_backup This feels to me like the smart thing to do, since moodle makes this provision for us, we should use it.  I will still *hold to the position, that it is the course creators responsibility to backup their course. As far as backing up the moodle core, probably not a big concern, as mentioned in Mary links, unless you start to add 3rd party plugins or customize the installation or tweak the code manually.  Even so, an occasional backup of the code is not a bad idea.  Especially before you attemp to upgrade moodle or install a third party moodle. I have set up a sandbox instance where i can experiment with different backup options (course and DB) to ensure i know what im doing.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to restore courses in 2.1+
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, to say the truth, I would not even consider running a "real" moodle install in a shared hosting environment. I did for some reason test moodle in such a restricted environment (this is a good test for evaluation of performance and robustness), but had the same problems that you are describing. It could be discussed, if this is a bug - I personally believe that software should be aware of the environment it runs in and warn the user before things (could) go bad - in this case it would be easy to check the moodle memory requirements and put a clear warning on the user screen that backup and restore functionality will be broken with not enough memory - leading you, the user, into a really bad trap. Developers should think about these kind of things, as they are common in real world migration and backup scenarios. In your situation you might ask your hoster for a mysql dump of your moodle data and install moodle on a more capable server - another thing to watch out for is the max_execution_time PHP variable - moodle will not tell you about this value beeing to low, so you should choose a php installation where it is high enough, at least 60 seconds - many providers are limiting it to 30 seconds or even lower. You can check php limitations on a server by putting a simple php file into your directory with one single call of phpinfo(); - it will show you all relevant information. Good Luck! Bughunter

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: REALLY strange PHP error message???
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Doug, Moodle & PHP versions? It seems you're running PHP 5.3 code ( Dynamic access to static methods is now possible ) under PHP 5.2. To run under PHP 5.2, it should be modified like e.g. in the lines below: 
```text
    public static function get_behaviour_required_behaviours($behaviour) {
```
 
```text
        $class = 'qbehaviour_' . $behaviour;
```
 
```text
        eval('$ret = ' . $class . '::get_required_behaviours();');
```
 
```text
        return $ret;
```
 
```text
    }
```
 HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: REALLY strange PHP error message???

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: manual backups fails
