ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Migrate a course from Blackboard to Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: 1) Yes, I think you are right. Everything is a course in moodle. Courses can have different looks, though, called course formats. There is topic (probably most common), weeks (like topics but with dates), and social (which is mostly oriented around discussion). There are some alternate formats, but I think these three are the most common. I think the reason you don't find the "all workspaces are some variety of course" described explicitly is because it is so basic that we all take it for granted. After all, moodle is an LMS, not a CMS. It was never meant to be joomla or drupal, so you won't find the same kinds of functionalities without modification. I can't remember BB as being any different functionally, although the admin areas are arranged differently. 2) The administrative tool block doesn't go on the main moodle page. I think that is because the front page is a "special" case of course and you are not supposed to treat it the same way you treat other courses/workspaces. As I said before, I have found it much more practical to create a special "course" as a workspace for managing uploads and conversions. I run a few hundred each year through that space and it works great! Your admin login allows you access to anything, so just make a course for handling your conversions and use it. You don't have to be an instructor and all that. I think, perhaps, in this one thing you are still more familiar with how BB does course restores than how moodle does them. If I remember correctly, I had a BB administrative area where the archives were stored and I restored from there. The use of the uploads and conversions course DOES represent an intermediate step that you might not have had before. But on the other hand, it works just as well once you get used to the idea of using a course as an archive repository. 3) I encourage you to add to the documentation in the wiki. You are in an excellent position to really zero in on things that a person ought to know in order to streamline this process. I, for example, have long since developed the "expert's blind spot" and take too many things for granted. So I think you can make a real difference in this regard! atw

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Migrate a course from Blackboard to Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: It will bring over test questions, yes. It will create a question category for each test in Bb. As for external links, I have a fix for that, but it won't work if there's spaces in the link (you would have to add %20 in place of a space... maybe someone else has a fix for that). The fix for external links goes something like this: The file you want is /moodle/backup/bb/bb6_to_moodle.xsl Add "<br/>" (no quotes... it's a line break) to the end of line 510 (with the Import tool... it might be a line or two off) to create a separator for the link and the title so it will autolink. The line should look like this before: <xsl:value-of select="TITLE/@value"/> and this after: <xsl:value-of select="TITLE/@value"/><br/> After line 510, hit return and add the following line to add the "URL" value to the body of the external link description. <xsl:value-of select="URL/@value"/> Hopefully this will work for you. If not, post back and I'll see what else I can do.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: An error occurred while copying the zip file to the course directory
ResponsesInList.Text: Scott, For what it is worth - had a nagging backup issue that I resolved, which may be related. Background: Moodle 1.93+ Php 5.25 All courses we have back-up fine, except for one very large media course (~500MB of videos).  This is a very common Moodle issue.  Initial attempts to fix included: increased memory and timeout limits in /backup/backup.php and /backup/restore.php added php.ini file to  /backup folder to increase memory and timeouts for php added external binaries for zipping These got us closer, but still nothing.  The backup zip file would be created in /moodledata/temp/backups - but then the process would hang (the temp folder was not cleared and the created zipped backup (when manually moved back into the course folder) was corrupt). As a last ditch effort we 100% maxed the php.ini settings with this: display_errors = Off max_execution_time= 9000 memory_limit = 1900M post_max_size= 220M upload_max_filesize= 220M session.gc_maxlifetime = 9000 But still no go. At this point I moved on to another workaround, but as a last ditch try, I decided to disable the external zip binaries and go back with the default moodle zipping. I then ran a backup with those settings (default Moodle zipping) and the php.ini of: display_errors = Off max_execution_time= 9000 memory_limit = 1900M post_max_size= 220M upload_max_filesize= 220M session.gc_maxlifetime = 9000 suhosin.post.max_vars = 400 suhosin.request.max_vars = 400 The backup appeared to hang again (again with all the temp files and zipped backup in the moodledata/temp/backups folder. But this time - moving the zipped backup copy over to course allowed the course to be restored! So in summary - I was unable to get the backup process to complete on this large course with the external binaries (despite working on smaller courses), but as able to by maxing the php settings above and using Moodle's default zipping.  Still - you may have to track the zipped file down in the temp folder. Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle import error
ResponsesInList.Text: At UCLA we've discovered a fatal flaw in the way that Moodle 1.9 and Moodle 2.0 is doing course imports. We've also posted the issue in Moodle tracker . To summarize the problem, if you are an admin on a very large Moodle site and try to do an import, you will see a blank page. This only happens once you get thousands of courses on your site, and only if you are trying to do the import as an admin. The reason for this, is that the SQL that is produced ends up being a string that is too long for MySQL to handle. One work-around is to log in as a teacher, do the import, then return to your admin role. We've also developed a fix for this on our system by modifying the sql from the default: SELECT * FROM mdl_course WHERE id IN ($tcourseids[0], $tcourseids[1], ..., $tcourseids[n]) to:

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle import error
ResponsesInList.Text: As an update to this issue, we ran into another problem where the memory limit in mysql was reached because SELECT course.* would select all the fields in the course table (some fields that are very large) even though only a couple are used. Our final, and working solution to this is modifying moodle\course\import\ activities \mod.php. We changes: if (!empty($tcourseids)) { $tcourseids = substr($tcourseids,0,-1); $taught_courses = get_records_list('course', 'id', $tcourseids, 'sortorder'); } To: if (!empty($tcourseids)) { $tcourseids = substr($tcourseids,0,-1); $sql = 'SELECT crs.id, crs.fullname FROM mdl_context ctx JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT ctx.path FROM mdl_role_assignments ra JOIN mdl_context ctx ON ctx.id = ra.contextid JOIN mdl_role_capabilities rc ON rc.roleid = ra.roleid WHERE ra.userid = "' . $USER->id . '" AND (rc.capability = "moodle/course:update" OR rc.capability = "moodle/site:doanything")) priv ON ctx.path LIKE concat(priv.path, "%") JOIN mdl_course crs ON crs.id = ctx.instanceid WHERE ctx.contextlevel = 50'; $taught_courses = get_records_sql($sql); } This fixes the bug where admins of very large courses weren't able to do course imports.

ResponsesInList.Text: We also had the same problem about backup of a course having a lot of and/or large files as course file since PHP can not treat a file over 2.0GB. Backup task will be failed in processes of generating zip file by using pclzip library and copying a generated zip file (in moodledata/temp/backup/uniqueid) to course file folder (moodledata/courseid/backup). The problem that pclzip cannot generate a large zip file over 2.0GB can avoid by using a external zip program. On the other hand, the problem about retrieving backup zip file from temporary folder to course was not so easy. We had resolved the second problem and reported it to tracker( MDL-18156 ) yesterday. Please read it and give me your comments. Our solution concerning the constraint of PHP is very simple. We use rename() instead of copy() for retrieving generated zip file to course folder. Function copy() cannot treat a file over 2.0GB, but function rename() can treat it. In process of backup, we only need to move it, do not need to copy it! Coping a large file needs long time, but renaming it need a bit time. Furthermore, if our solution is right, backup process at Moodle site will become so very light and speedy.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore problem - "An error has ocurred"
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Keith, that step of restore tries to delete old records from some backup_xxx tables and old files from the moodledata/temp/backup are. I would suggest you to: 1) Delete records from "backup_ids". Repair the table after deletion. 2) Delete records from "backup_files". ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to backup a course in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: I have had problems myself when backing up large courses. I suspect the size of the course could be one problem. I use a workaround for this, that probably will be frowned upon, but this is the way I do it when I am unable to backup any other way: go to the moodledata directory for this specific course (through my computer, not moodle) and move the entire contents (for this course only) to a temporary directory elsewhere. Now go to the course in moodle and backup as you normally would (shouldn't take long as the size will be small. If you want to keep this course, you then copy (not move) the files back to their original location. When it comes to restoring the course, you then restore within moodle and go into the file section to create the directory in the moodledata directory. after creating this, you go in back end again and copy and paste the files from the original course into the new folder, using the original structure. If you have done this correctly, you will now find all links work as they should.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Getting an error message every time I try to import a course
ResponsesInList.Text: ok James - if you go to Moodle on your server or via ftp client you should have a folder Moodle but OUTSIDE of that should be a folder moodledata (or in some installations it is called uploaddata) and that is where all the folders for each course are stored. For example site files that you get to from the front page are in folder/directory number 1. Each course in Moodle has its own numbered folder that gets made once you put something in a course in Moodle. If you have stuff in courses already then there will be folders with numbers - if you go to a course and click on a resource you will see the number in the URL . If you make a new course and want to see its number you can create the folder by just uploading any old thing into it - text file -whatever - and then you will see the number of your course folder. So upload your zipped/backed up course into a folder/directory via ftp and then go to that course and restore it from there. It has worked for me which means your backing up was successful so you didn't do anything wrong. edit - forgot to say - the moodledata/uploaddata folder *should* be outside of the moodle directory for security - I have never heard of softaculous but I guess it must be like Fantastico ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to Backup Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Here's what I found... The backup process uses php's internal zip functions which have a small size limit and so I was destined to failure. I setup the Server ->System Paths to use the Linux OS programs but they too are limited to 4GB.  This allows for a larger course but there are still limitations.  I ran out of file space several times because when you backup a course, moodle first copies all the files to a temporary area (so a 4GB course now takes up 8GB of space.)  The next step in the process is to zip the temporary files and so the course now takes approx 12 GB of space as the zip process runs, failures along the way leave these space gobblers littering the filesystem, not good. I tried another suggestion of being selective about the files I backed up but no matter what options I selected the zip operation started zipping up the whole course and therefore destined to fail eventually, and so the cycle of pain started again. Finally what I did was examine the course in detail.  Most of the space was taken up with a single directory of guff.  I stream gzipped the contents to /tmp, emptied the directory and then copied then copied (backup and restore) the course to its destination.  I then stream gunzipped the contents from /tmp back into the course. I was lucky as I had access to the server and filesystem and so I could carry out these operations. The astute of the readers will have been able to pick out the fact that although I was eventually sucessful in the course copying, the process is flawed (on many levels, and in different areas.)  The large static course content should be on a separate web server and only be referenced by the course, not included in the actual course.  This would also allow for a sensible, efficient backup strategy. The moodle backup/restore process should stream gzip content to overcome size limitations. It just needs more thought, need I continue ...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: IMS-CC package restore error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, some time ago we developed a Common Cartridge Minimizer which strips all content off a cartridge to reduce its size. It is offered for download by IMS on the CC Alliance site: Common Cartridge Minimizer The Common Cartridge Minimizer is a tool, developed at the University in Koblenz/Germany, to lighten the load when emailing Common Cartridges for inspection by others. It strips off all content from cartridges and retains just the structure of the cartridge. More precisely, it creates copies of cartridges where all non-xml files are replaced by empty files with the same name. This offers two advantages: The size of the cartridges is considerably reduced Content to be protected does not have to leave the owner's system Since the IMS Common Cartridge Specification does not specify internals of content files, these stripped-down cartridges are still tested faithfully by the CC test tool.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teachers can't include user data in backups?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Blair, The change is described in the Moodle 1.9.7 release notes : Teachers lose permission to include ANY user data in a course backup or restore a course including user data due to new capabilities moodle/backup:userinfo and moodle/restore:userinfo which are not set for the default role of teacher. Sites with custom roles should check permissions carefully. Admins can restore those permissions but are informed of the risks in doing so. It's a security issue, so access to the tracker issue is restricted.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teachers can't include user data in backups?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there. I can't tell you why it applies to your 1.9.6 rather than 1.9.7 but I can explain the rationale behind it - in short, it was a security issue. If teachers can backup user details then they could (in theory) enrol all the users on Moodle into their course, including the primary admin -then they could (in theory) back up that course and then (in theory) get the list of users from the backed up folder and then go to a password-cracking website and, if the primary admin's password was insecure enough, they could decode it - and then they would (in theory) acquire admin rights to that Moodle with the admin password. For this to happen it would need a lot of possiblities actually to come together and work, but it's better to be safe than sorry , so the ability for teachers to do this was removed by removing the ability to backup users along with the course information. EDIT_ oh well, Helen beat me to it! Never mind

ResponsesInList.Title: backing up course backups only
ResponsesInList.Text:
I just thought I'd share this, which was written by CyberNerd on the EduGeek forums at: http://www.edugeek.net/forums/nix/50073-how-can-i-write-v-simple-shell-script-back-selected-files-date.html This one line should work on all linux systems to go through the Moodledata (/usr/moodledata/ in this case) directory and pull out only the latest backups of each course, then copy them to /BackupDirectory: 
```text
for file in $(/bin/ls -d /usr/moodledata/*/backupdata/); do find $file -type f -iname "*.zip" -printf "%TY-%Tm-%Td %TT %p\n" | sort | tail -n 1 | awk '{ print $3 }' | xargs /bin/cp -v --target-directory=/BackupDirectory/ ; done
```
 As CyberNerd commented, if you were using this regularly, you'd want to change the cp command to rsync so that only changes get written. If you are able to change the directory where your server puts backups and only want to keep one backup of each course, you won't need this. However, I give teachers the opportunity to restore from old backups going back 5 days and I needed this to get out ONLY the latest .zip backup file for each course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: script to parse moodle.xml file for activity logs
ResponsesInList.Text: Here is some relevant javascript . I haven't used it for a while but it should work. The principle is simple. You open the xml file, retrieve the elements you need and extract the data from these elements. It can be executed from a webpage and produce csv text which can be copied/pasted into a csv file. Hope this helps. Loading the xml file: function loadXML(file) { if (document.implementation && document.implementation.createDocument) { xmlDoc = document.implementation.createDocument("", "", null); } else { if (window.ActiveXObject) { xmlDoc = new ActiveXObject("Microsoft.XMLDOM"); } else { alert('Your browser can\'t handle this script'); return; } } xmlDoc.async=false; xmlDoc.load(file); return xmlDoc; } Writing the desired data: function writeData(xmlDoc) { var str=""; var items = xmlDoc.getElementsByTagName(' item '); for (var i=0;i<items.length;i++) { var desc=""; for (var j=0;j<items[i].childNodes.length;j++) { if (items[i].childNodes[j].nodeType!=1) continue; var itemName=items[i].childNodes[j].nodeName; if (itemName==' desc ') { desc=items[i].childNodes[j].firstChild.nodeValue; // write text str+=desc+"\n"; } } } return str; }

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course cloning
ResponsesInList.Text: Concur with Ravishankar. We duplicate our courses with backup & restore to make a new classroom for a new bunch of students. Important items: If you have instructor prompts in forums that you want to keep, you'll want to b&r WITH users and perhaps with files. BUT, if you b&r with users, you will have all student work carried forward. We make "template" courses with instructor prompts but no student info and duplicate from the templates. This preserves instructor forum prompts without carrying students from one classroom to the next. Probably, you can use the reset button (I've never done it) to clean everything out & then re-enter instructor prompts to make a template. Do this in a cloned classroom, not the original! We never delete student materials. Record keeping! But also, students & parents tend to come back 6 months later wanting to view the classroom or recapture lost materials. Good luck!

I finally remembered that previously from the Site Administration > Server > System Paths I had put in /usr/bin/zip for the zip and unzip for an external path. The reason I had done this was because I was making a final backup of last semester's courses which contained some large video files students had submitted for an assignment. I removed the external paths so Moodle would use its own internal zip php ability and my restore worked just as it should.

ResponsesInList.Title: Backup / Restore Serious Problems
ResponsesInList.Text: I have read many of these messages and I believe there are two major problems with Backup and Restore. 1) You cannot upload even a SMALL course ZIP file (20MB+) because some Moodles only allow 2 MB, others 8MB. Right there you have to use FTP and find the backupdata folder in order to have the backup file even appear when you click Restore in the left-hand sidebar of the receiving Moodle. 2) If you DO manage to get a ZIP file placed so that it shows up on another server 's Restore function, it usually complains that the 1.9.x Moodle that made the backup is a different VERSION than the 1.9.x Moodle being asked to restore. These would seem to be true statements for the 1.9.x Moodles. Backup and Restore works within the SAME Moodle because the upload restriction does not come into play and because, being the same Moodle, the version numbers naturally are an exact match. You cannot upload a backup file in another Moodle (to install a course) without server access by FTP. The Moodle itself CANNOT do this because the USER upload limit is applied to ADMINs when they try to back up and restore, preventing the procedure. The versions of creating and restoring Moodle software must be IDENTICAL or the process CAN NOT be used to move a Moodle course from one server to another. The chances of this being the case are very slight effectively prohibiting the use of Backup and Restore to send a course to another Moodle.—Sherman Keene

After restoring a few courses all seems well, but the issue I have is that students who are listed as enrolled in courses cannot enter them. When I log on as a student enrolled in a course, I get the message: Student not enrolled in this course . I have checked the assign roles and the students are listed as enrolled. I have tried unenroling, re-enroling, changing auth to manual, making the course enrollable but nothing seems to work. Students also can no longer see their courses listed in their profiles. This is not an issue for teachers. We use ldap authentication - everyone can log in to the vle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup and restore and lost enrolments
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello all, I think I have located the problem. It would seem that the Student role has become corrupted. I have duplicated the role and tested this by assigning it manually to a student who has problems accessing courses. This now allows access to the course. The issue appears to be with the role ID in mdl_role_assignments. In my set up the default Student role Id is 5. My duplicate Student role id is 37. I think if I change this id in this table for all users with roleid="5" to roleid="37" I can sort the problem out for all pupils or staff who have the current default student role in any course. I have tried the following sql statement: UPDATE mdl_role_assignments SET roleid='37' WHERE roleid='5'; This throws up: `#1062 - Duplicate entry '37-37-######' for key 2 error` The id ##### corresponds to a user contextid field, so I changed the roleid from 37 to 38 and ran the sql. It has changed all roleids from 5 to 38 without error. I have checked a large number of both staff and pupil accounts which have the new student role and they can now all access their courses. I have also changed the default role for users in a course ( defaultcourseroleid - found in admin > users >permissions > user policies ) to my new student role. I renamed my new student role to "Student..." as this means no explanation to course admins is needed as they won't even notice the ellipsis. As we upgrade from pre 1.7 versions of Moodle we now find the legacy role option in Roles. Some of my additional roles for students like student_course_editor (which allows some students to edit a course like the school council course) were set to legacy:student. This meant that when I used my internal enrolment plugin (Facility to Moodle) to transfer teaching groups F2M simply looked for the first legacy:student role listed in roles. My new student role mentioned above was way down that list. I removed all other legacy:student roles or removed the legacy option, changed the sortorder for my new student role in the db in mdl_role table and away we go. This has now fixed the broken Student role in my Moodle. I hope this helps anyone else who might have a similar issue. Cheers, Ed

ResponsesInList.Title: Moving courses between moodle 1.9 +(Build 20080401) and moodle 1.9.5 (Build 20090513)
ResponsesInList.Text: We have recently decided to overhaul our Moodle install. However, instead of upgrading we went with a complete new install. So it has been left to me to move the "data" from one installation to the other. I initially thought this would be simple by using the backup & restore routines. However, I have since ran into a problem "The backup did not complete successfully". I have tried searching here for a solution but i am mindful that I need to apply the right solution to the right build. The error message i get is as follows Name: backup-farm-20091012-1529.zip Creating temporary structures Deleting old data Creating XML file Writing header Writing general info Writing course data Course info Blocks Sections Writing users info Writing categories and questions Writing scales info Writing groups info Writing groupings info Writing groupings-groups info Writing events info Writing gradebook info Writing modules info Forums Course format data Copying user files Copying course files Copying site files used in course Zipping backup Copying zip file An error occurred while copying the zip file to the course directory Any help would be greatly appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving courses between moodle 1.9 +(Build 20080401) and moodle 1.9.5 (Build 20090513)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ian, in general, any problem at that step in the backup process means that there is some sort of problem with: 1) Permissions in destination directory. (99% chance of) Those backup files are copied to "XXX/backupdata" under your dataroot directory (where XXX is the id of the course being backup-ed). 2) Disk full or error. (1% chance of). In any case, perhaps enabling debug in Admin -> Server -> Debug to its maximum level (DEBUG_DEVELOPER) and/or looking at web server error logs, can give some more precise information about what's happening.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving courses between moodle 1.9 +(Build 20080401) and moodle 1.9.5 (Build 20090513)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I've got the same problem with moodle 1.9.5+. I did check permissions (including open_basedir) and that should not be the problem. I got following messages from developer debugging turned on: An error occurred while copying the zip file to the course directory The backup did not complete successfully Stack trace: line 1664 of lib/deprecatedlib.php: call to debugging() line 73 of backup/backup_execute.html: call to error() line 135 of backup/backup.php: call to include_once() Any ideas? Thanks, David

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving courses between moodle 1.9 +(Build 20080401) and moodle 1.9.5 (Build 20090513)

Or is the restore process executed "immediately" without showing that "choose a course" page? In any case, if my memory isn't wrong, there are two bugs that could, potentially be causing problems like that under certain circumstances: - MDL-19246 : When fixing this bug, a lot of code in the "new/current/existing" algorithm was fixed to improve all those combinations that were causing problems before. - MDL-18469 : That prevents some problems with sessions to cause problems with courses being restored in different courses and other data lost. Now all the restore settings are checked before continue with the restore process. Both bugs are already fixed in current Moodle 1.9.5+ weeklies and will debut officially in next Moodle 1.9.6, so I'd suggest you to upgrade to any of them. Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup to an external server
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Edwin rosado, YES, it is possible, you can use amazon aws and s3 to create instances and use scalr to maintain your instances, and as jody wanted we have something called snapshots, which takes an entire image of your files and stores in S3. (No need to fear space consumption because of the images which are taken by snapshots, its an incremental backup ;)) checkout scalr for more details, i heard amazon themselves have comeup with a service similar to scalr which does all these.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup to an external server
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you. I actually have an external server that I would like to use. My question is how to specify or direct course backup to go to the server in moodles course backup config? Thanks for the help.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup to an external server
ResponsesInList.Text: If you just want the backup files to be saved to an external server, the easiest way to do that is to do the following: 1) Mount the directory on the external server in a place Moodle can write to using NFS/samba/whatever. 2) Go to Admin->Courses->Backups and set the "Save to" (backup_sche_destination) to be the mounted network location. 3) Enable scheduled backups (if you haven't already). -Greg

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup to an external server
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks, Greg. I'll give that a shot.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup to an external server
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear edwin rosado, as greg lund said you can follow his steps to save the course backups alone to an external server, But in case of disaster i dont think you will be able to recover your entire site with just course backups. . So it is always advisable to make a database dump sequentially and tag it with the course backups and perform a rotational backup mechanism on them so that you save space by avoiding the huge piling up of backups.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Whole Site Database back up and restore

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Files missing upon Restore
ResponsesInList.Text: In case this is affecting anyone else, I wanted to post my solution here. I traced the problem to a more general problem with unzipping files through the Moodle interface in general. The problem was that Moodle was not correctly creating the subfolders as it decompressed the zip file, so it could not move the files into place, since the destination folders did not exist. To resolve this problem, I added a line to the function unzip_process_temp_dir, in dirroot /lib/moodlelib.php, line 7573: if (is_dir($fullfile)) { mkdir($descfile); // added to fix directory recursion problem // recurse into subdirs unzip_process_temp_dir($fullfile, $descfile); } This fixed manual unzipping from inside the Files directory, and also fixed course import/restore functionality.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle 1.8 - backup courses (problem with backup_sche_destination)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all of you, I had the same problem with Moodle 1.9 today. I figured out that the function (backup/backuplib.php:copy_zip_to_course_dir) that is copies the final zip file to the destination directory tries to read a propterty of the passed $preferences object. More precisely if the property $preferences->backup_destination is not empty it will copy the file to another directory than the default course directory. This property should be added to the object in one of the two functions called in the backup/backup_execute.html, backup_fetch_prefs_from_request or backup_add_static_preferences, but none of these functions add this property. So to get it work for my system it modified the backup_add_static_preferences function (in backup/backuplib.php) and added the following two lines at the method's end: $backupconfig = backup_get_config(); $preferences->backup_destination = $backupconfig->backup_sche_destination; Now the backup will be copied to the directory entered in the backup_sche_destination box on the backup setting's page. Hope it helps someone as long as that issue isn't fixed in the source code. Thanks, Marcel

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Importing a file to multiple courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Dan, The best solution that I know of (for what you have listed) is to create a new "shared" folder in your course/files/backupdata folder using symbolic links. Here are the steps: 1. Create a new folder in course/files/backupdata folder using unix symbolic links (search symbolic links in these forums - it allows you to essentially map a single common folder on the server to multiple "symbolic" folders). 2. You HAVE TO create it in the course/files/backupdata directory folder as Moodle backup/restore will NOT make copies of this folder upon backup/restoring.  If you place it in the course/files directory itself backup/restore can/will make copies of this upon course restore (bad thing). 3. The symbolic folder will need to be manually created after each new course is created in Moodle. Pros - You can share a common file among XXX courses.  You don't break any moodle core code Cons - These "shared" files will not be backed up during normal Moodle backup. They also wont be visible in the "new" course until the symbolic folder is created again. Ken

ResponsesInList.Text: Here at the Open University we have a vast number of people involved in the production of annual course presentations, and the roll forward process of backuip and retore helps with the subsequent reuse of existing course materials. I had the task of investigating a bug reported by a member of our course production team "Backup without course and site files doesn't work. I tried to back up the course without course or site files so that I could just have the basic template of the site. However, all files were pulled across to the course I restored the backup to. I assume that when you select no course or site files it shouldn't pull them through?" I found this to mean that any files stored in the course files folder which were not used as course resources, were included in the backup zip file. The expectation of the production team was that this should not be the case.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup - too much added to zip file
ResponsesInList.Text: The basic issue is this: When you backup a course, even if you have turned off 'backup course files', then it still backs up any files that are linked to by a file or directory resource. That is probably a good thing. However, sometimes, while we are building a course here, we add the file resource before the actual file is ready. Then we make it hidden. That serves as a reminder to upload the actual file when it is ready. The problem is, if you backup a course while it is in this state, then it includes all course files, even if you have turned off 'backup course files'. This is because a directory resource with a blank file reference means a directory resource showing all course files. All we are proposing to do is, in the backup code for resources, if the file reference is blank, then only backup all course files if the resource type is directory. Does that make sense? Which branches do we want the bug fix in? (I guess we should file this in the tracker.)

ResponsesInList.Text: Carrie, Experienced this on several courses as well, in several different forms.  The "worst" is the case where the images are "mapped" back to their original URL (say course ID=5 - and by mapped back I mean the URL is the same in the original course as well as the new restored course).  When I (as the admin) view this I can see the image fine (as I can see images linked from all courses).  But a student cannot (unless they have access to course ID=5). If these images are NOT OK to have open to the public, then place them in a course that ONLY students and ALL students have access too (say it has the ID=2).  Then remap all your image URLs of course ID=2. The issue with Moodle remapping/or NOT remapping your URLS is a sticky one.  For example, say that http://www.yoursite.com/file.php?2file=picture.jpg is a static one that you don't want to change, but http://www.yoursite.com/file.php?200file=picture.jpg is - how can Moodle know which one of the embedded images to update? Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: backup failure BUG?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have several large courses scheduled to backup. Each time the backup cron is run the same 6 courses fail every time. I tracked the issue back to not having enough disc space. I have 3.8 gig and a 5 gig storage limit. When the large course 700 meg approx backup they fail and do not finish. Each day the scheduled backups run a temp folder is created in moodledata/temp/backups/(numerical directory name) is created and the moodle.xlm, user files, course files are stored here ready to zip. This backup data is then zipped in the same temp folder. When the zip is created in the temp moodledata/temp/backups/(numerical directory name)/coursename.zip thsi is then copied to the relevant backup location in moodledata outside of the temp folder. As you can see there are then between 3-4 copies of the course in uncompress and compressed files. so my 700 meg course is duplicated twice in the temp folder, once from the original course in moodledata and then again when the zip file attempts to copy to the moodledata/backup folder.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup failure BUG?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I found the solution to this issue. My installation for Moodle did not specify the server side system paths as this was setup and installed by a Moodle partner, I would have expected these to be populated upon initial configuration. To resolve the backup issue I entered values for the path to zip and unzip within Site Admin > Server > System Paths. As I am on a hosted package with limited disk space, when these values are left blank, Moodle's default behaviour performing backups generates them under the hosted account instead of at the server level ( Operating System ). If disc quota is close to its' limit and the backup process runs this will push the amount of disc quota usage over this limit and restricts the backups from completing hence the backup error message. By entering values for system paths Moodle will generate the backups at root level instead of the account level, which has no impact on the disk space allowance. The attached image should illistrate what's been done. So not a BUG just an irritating setting ok, well not that irritating, just overlooked. Steve

ResponsesInList.Text: There's a whole range of subtle reasons why this might not work. Here's just some I can think of, maybe others can add more: * What OS is this? Can you create a folder called 'backupdata' (if it doesn't already exist) in the course's files and can you upload files into that area? * There's a temp file setting somewhere in php.ini - the directory it points to actually has to exist. This is more of a Windows issue I think.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle xml not found at root level of zip file
ResponsesInList.Text: It sounds like the xml file is not where is supposed to be, meaning that when you have a zipped file called for example backup.zip, that when you see what's inside it, it should look like this (CORRECT): onefolder another folder xmlfile.xml If you look inside backup.zip and see this (INCORRECT): justafolder and then inside justafolder you see: onefolder another folder xmlfile.xml then that is the problem, and you need to move everything out of justafolder so that the xmlfile.xml is found in the root of the zip file.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Exclude a 6GB course from schedule backup
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Mo, A crude hack: First: Add a new field to the mdl_backup_course table.  Call the field something like backupskip.  Set inital value to 0.  Then edit the database row for the course you want to skip, by changing this value to one (1 = we want to skip). Second: Edit /backup/backup_scheduled.php to skip course if backupskip value =1.  Something like this (not tested - just as an example): Around line 88 (i'm running Moodle 1.93+) add the following: //Check if the course should be skipped in backup_courses $skip_course = get_record("backup_courses","backupskip",$course->id); // Skip backup if course indicated to skip $skipped = false; if ($skip_course > 0) { mtrace("            SKIPPING - hidden+unmodified"); set_field("backup_courses","laststatus","3","courseid",$backup_course->courseid); $skipped = true; } This will let you skip the course! A more elegant solution would be to get the coursesize report http://moodle.org/mod/data/view.php?d=13&rid=2121&filter=1 Then have the backup look at the course size (say 5GB+) and skip that size or greater.  No need for database tweaking there. Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: rsync two moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been investigating rsync recently. It is a one-way process - it copies files from one server to another. As such, it would not synchronise two Moodle's. It is only able to copy from one Moodle server to a different location - effectively making a backup or a mirror. Stu

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: rsync two moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Stuart Mealor, rsync is a one way process, <= yeah i agree with you

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: rsync two moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. rsync does a differential copy if there are already existing files in the same name Not necessarily. By default rsync updates files if the source file is newer than the destination. It won't copy over files that haven't changed, but it will update files that have unless you set "--ignore-existing". 2. rsync does a complete backups/mirror if the destination doesnt have a folder/files in the same name such as source. Note, however, that rsync does *not* copy the database over. Simply copying over the files from the /var/lib/ mysql (or wherever your server stores the My SQL data) will almost certainly result in an inconsistent and probably corrupted copy of the database. And if the site is large, you get a sliding window backup where things may change and become inconsistent during the course of the backup. To do a true mirror of two sites, you're probably going to have to do something like this: 1) Set up DRDB on the wwwroot / dataroot partition so that when the primary Moodle server writes something to disk, it's automatically written over the network to the secondary server. 2) Set up MySQL replication with the primary server as the master and the secondary server as the slave. Are you looking at some sort of cluster/load balance? Or are you looking to have a hot backup of the site for failover or disaster recovery? there are several ways to do it, but the solutions change depending on your intended use case. -Greg

ResponsesInList.Text: We found the problem. It was the size of the course. If you have a course that is large, with lots of graphics and video media, you cannot back up "with Course Resources". It chokes immediately. So we back up without course resources and it works fine. We have come up with a solution for multiple courses, that share media resources from one folder, instead of multiple duplicates, a challenge unique only a subset of moodle around the world. Our tech expert came up with... 1. Put all media resources into one folder in the moodledata folder and name the directory/folder "resources". 2. Use admin. replace.php and replace every instance of the file.php?id=xxxxx with "/resources" What that does is hard code all the links to resources to that folder as a static URL . Then when you back up, you are backing up without course media, only text, and therefore the back ups are manageable and the links persist. Hope this helps others. Now I need to make sure that auto back ups can be set to back up without course resources and we are back on line totally.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No backup ability. How can I save and move my work?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David I'm not sure if I can fully help with your query but I'll try to explain a little about backups... Also check out the Backup and restore FAQ on Moodle Docs . The Automated Course Backups ( Administration ► Courses ► Backups ) is the configuration screen to prompt Moodle to backup courses that have been altered recently. The actual backing up occurs on the specified day/time and is triggered by the cron. If you don't have this set up automatically you can browse to sitename/admin/cron.php to manually run it. The Front page backup is backing up the Moodle homepage (course 1), any activities you have and site calendar activities, as well as Messages & Blogs - this is not your entire site rather everything LESS the individual courses. A course backup is completed for each individual course and is accessed from the 'Backup' link on that course's Administration menu. If this link doesn't appear like the screenshot here the role you are accessing the course with may not have the Backup courses moodle/site:backup capability, Check this via Administration / ► Users / ► Permissions / ► Define role . With regard to your re install failing, I would check your database details, moodle and moodledata folders are correctly speficied in the config.php file of your site. I hope this helps a little Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Major Backup and Restore Problem in 1.9.5
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Geoffrey, some ideas that can be useful to find the cause of your problems: 1) In the new server, enable DEBUG_DEVELOPER, to see if the page shows you more info. 2) Specify how many activities are in your course and at what exact point you get the error (when unzipping, after the big form selecting what to restore...). Any detail will be welcome in order to be able to understand/reproduce the problem (1st step before trying to fix anything). 3) Check that both your apache and php settings are correct in order to support BIG file uploads and POST requests. Both the "LimitRequestBody" setting in Apache and "upload_max_filesize" and "post_max_size" should be set to, at least 16MB. Note that specially the apache setting uses to be really small in some linux distros and it prevents both file uploads and big forms (like the restore one) to work. See this section of the Administration FAQ in Moodle Docs . 4) Create one issue in the Moodle Tracker , detailing everything needed to understand and reproduce the problem. Any tiny piece of information about the process / configuration can be really important so, be exhaustive. 5) Finally, knowing that you are basically migrating your existing site to a new server... perhaps the best alternative to have the new one working easier and reliably... is to perform one Site backup to get everything in place. Then you can safely delete those parts you aren't interested anymore. Definitively, better approach that restoring courses individually. Hope it helps, ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: this week's 1.9.4+ broke restore/import on PHP4
ResponsesInList.Text: Bummer! it seems that the \p modifier in regular expressions was introduced in PHP 4.4, so it isn't available in any PHP 4.3 (info available at http://php.net/manual/en/regexp.reference.php ). So... can you make this, as a quick workaround: 1) Save your current (non-working) backup/backuplib.php to a safe place 2) Edit backup/backuplib.php and, in the line that you pasted above replace any occurrence of "\pL" (without the quotes) by "a-zA-Z" (without the quotes too). There are 4 replacements to perform. 3) Try again your backup/restore with debug enabled. Should work. 4) Feedback results here. I'll add those changes to CVS ASAP, so next weekly build (April 29th, 2009) will contain them. TIA and ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cannot backup course
ResponsesInList.Text: I figured out the problem. In backup.php, there's a segment: } else if ($launch == "execute") { include_once("backup_execute.html"); Previously, there is this line: " $param=preg_replace("/eval|system|passthru|exec|include|require_once|move_uploaded_file/i","", $param); " What's happening is, the variable $launch has the value changed from 'execute' to 'ute'. To try this out, put: print "Launch=".$launch; at the bottom of backup.php (before the footer) When you go through the backup process, you should see the variable 'launch' as it gets assigned different values. at the area it *should* backup, you see 'Launch=ute'. Removing the preg_replace line fixes it, but then it doesn't sanitize the variables. I just altered the line to look for launch being the value 'ute'. Restore has the same problem.

ResponsesInList.Title: Backups of Backups Shortcut

ResponsesInList.Text: Skywalker, This is an easy process ... but one that seems to have developed a bug of sorts, but for what it's worth. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to make archive in moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: Skywalker, 1. On that same left pane, find the BACKUP option.  When the screen opens, decide if you want to archive the user data or just the contents. If you are going to re-use the course again choose ALL the content and NONE of the student data.  If you are creating an archive to protect against grade challenges, then backup ALL content and ALL student data. 2. At teh bottom be sure to answer the questions about course...Users, Logs, User files, Couirse files, Site files, Grade History.  The choices you make will depend on you plans for the archive.  Once you have completed your choices, choose CONTINUE 3. You'll get a couple of review screens to double check your options 4. The file will appear in your course files as a backupdata zip folder 5. RIGHT CLICK on the file (not the options on the right side of the screen) and SAVE TARGET wherever you want to store it..(flash drive, C-Drive, desktop, etc). 6. When you are ready to re-use the archive, use the RESTORE option in the future course. Good luck Ted Burke

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course restore fails with memory issue
ResponsesInList.Text: the is a bizarre behavior in apache2 in which you have to put the php.ini file in each folder (of moodle or any other framework) in order for it to override the default system's setting of /etc/php/php.ini so, please copy the modified php.ini you made into several folders including /moodle/admin (as i did) in the past... using apache 1.x i used a .htaccess file with the php_flags set to what ever i needed and it was affecting the entire site and sub folders... not anymore unless you have a virtual server or a managed server in which "you are the boss" ! hope it helps

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course restore fails with memory issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Nadav Many thanks for your helpful suggestions. In the end it appears that the problem was to do with a parameter on my hosting server. It did not matter how many times I changed php.ini within my Moodle install or what values I put in there for a memory limit, there was an over riding parameter that limited it to 32 Mb server wide. and my hosts refused (reasonably I suppose) to change that just for me. Anyone else experiencing this problem should be aware that changing php.ini to have 128M in your Moodle directory will result in Moodle's phpinfo telling you that you have 128Mb, but your scripts will still fail if the global server parameter is set to 32 Mb and they are trying to use more. Obvious really as long as you know that the server wide parameter exists! (Which I didn't and neither it appeared did at least 2 support peeps at my web host) In the end I upgraded my hosting account to a VPS where I have control over parameters like this and bingo the restore worked fine as soon as I changed the global PHP Scripting Memory parameter to 128M. This cost me an extra £100 a year but compared to the stress of the last 48 hours that feels like peanuts I imagine this might also resolve the problem I have with automated backups of the "Large" (5Mb zipped) courses failing. Time will tell.

Hi Mary, I am encountering the same error.  I have checked the FAQ (shown below) but accourding to my phpinfo (shown below) I am runing the recommended version.  Any other ideas? Doug Restoring a course results in broken HTML tags. What can I do? This problem is due to a PHP bug in libxml2 2.7.1 (the same bug reported with version 2.7.2). All HTML entities, such as >, < and " are removed when a course is restored. To resolve the problem, you should use a different version of libxml2 such as 2.7.0 or 2.6.32. At Gentoo servers, you can use 
```text
echo ">dev-libs/libxml2-2.6.32" >> /etc/portage/package.mask
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help!  Need to restore from tape!
ResponsesInList.Text: For mysql database, just look for the data folder under your mysql directory. ResponsesInList.Text: Firstly, go to moodle site admin/security/site policies & check the maximum upload file size for your install. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore Problem "Required parameter (id) was missing"
ResponsesInList.Text: The problem as far as i have experienced is due to the 'post_max_size' within the php.ini, the default is usually re-configured to 16Mb this seems to be the default size for any type of file that is being uploaded. There are 2 ways to fix this problem: - 1. change the php.ini to a higher size 2. ftp the zip file to the 'upload courses' and then do the restore I have literally just done this in the last 5 mins so i know that it works. Hope this helps. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore Problem "Required parameter (id) was missing"
ResponsesInList.Text: And something I've just noticed... when editing the values of 'post_max_size' and 'upload_max_filesize' in php.in, DON'T include the 'B' in 'MB'! For example, to set post_max_size to 50 megabytes, the value should be '50M' NOT '50MB'! If you include the 'B' it all stops working properly and you'll start getting the 'requirement parameter (id) is missing' error, as well as other strange things happening.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.0 and zip options
ResponsesInList.Text: There was a good reason for this change, which I don't remember ... Oh, yes I do. The issue is to do with Unicode in file names. It turns out that almost every zip program out there screws up when creating zip files when the files have names containing non-ascii characters, even though the ZIP specification supports this, I believe. And Moodle 2.0 will support Unicode characters in file names, thanks to the new File API.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.0 and zip options
ResponsesInList.Text: In preparation for installing a Moodle 2.0 test, we installed PHP 5.2.8 on our Cent OS server, complete with zip enabled. On executing our nightly cron job, 2 courses failed at the zip stage. One was 2.2 Gb and one was 4.5 Gb. Luckily, with Moodle 1.9.x, we can still specify an alternate zip/unzip path. We did, and the courses backed up properly. Unfortunately, as currently designed, the option is not available once one moved to Moodle 2.0. This could be a serious issue for those with large courses. Can the option to define the path for zip and unzip not be left in Server ... System Paths screen for Moodle 2.0? thanks L

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.0 and zip options
ResponsesInList.Text: PHP has two different zip libraries. The only, that has been there since ages ago, and which Moodle <=1.9 uses if you don't give it the path to zip. And a new library which has been there since Moodle 5.2.0, which Moodle 2.0 uses, and which (at least since PHP 5.2.8) works better. So running Moodle 1.9 on PHP 5.2.8 won't magically make it use the new ZIP library. So you still have the problems associated with the old library.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.0 and zip options
ResponsesInList.Text: Tim, I think your response got truncated. In 2.0, will we have the option to chose alternate zip/unzip routines in case the default one fails to properly backup/restore larger courses? thanks L

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.0 and zip options
ResponsesInList.Text: Drat! yes, it did. PHP 5.2.8 (actually, 5.2.0, but there were critical bugs with it until 5.2.8) has two zip libraries. The old zip library that has been there for ages, and which current and older version of Moodle user. The has the well-known shortcoming that you talk about. And a new zip library that, that works properly with huge files, and with Unicode file-names (which most stand-alone zip programs cannot manage). Just upgrading PHP to 5.2.8 will not magically make Moodle switch to using the new library. The only way to do that is to rewrite the code Moodle uses to handle files, and that is what was done in Moodle 2.0.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.0 and zip options
ResponsesInList.Text: Ah! Makes sense now. Thanks so much, Tim larry

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup of Moodle directory
ResponsesInList.Text: The simple answer to your final point is - have you recovered it and did it recover clean ? - if so yes, if not why not - you are at risk. If as I suspect the recovery from the network share is an absolute pig to put onto a new machine (not the old one but a new build server - built from your build instructions) then you have answered your own question. If it does work - for you - then you could consider sticking with this method tsting maybe monthly. Personally I think it is more trouble than it is worth and I would suggest you do it 'properly' but until you have tried the suggestions in the paragraphs above then you don't really have enough data to make a sensible cost/benefit analysis.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup of Moodle directory
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree with Neil. I have a lot of personal experience in reinstalling Moodle for whatever reason and thankfully, the moodledata folder is all in one place and suggest that you try and restore the database and select a couple or few courses to test from the "recovered" moodledata folder. The backup and restore is on a course by course basis. You can run the cron job to backup, in this case zip the course's files in the directory it was setup to save it to. If I were you (and depending on you database type), I would run a nightly job to backup your Moodle database and copy your moodledata folder to another drive, destination, etc. Then install the same version of Moodle on another machine and try to restore from the lastest database backup (not course zip file). Then try and point the moodledata to the backup location ... if all seem okay, yous should be okay. Remember, you need to keep track of all your plugins, setup/authentication settings or modifications, etc. I use to be a network admin and I always test restore to make sure they work regularly. Your users and management might not see the risk but inform them of what could happen and if they could afford the downtime ... then draft a doc of agreement and have them sign it =) trust me, after that they'll give you all the time in the world to test a restore.. good luck

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course -> No backup / restore for 2nd admin account
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Ben, I believe Moodle stores everything based on IDs. So courses will most likely be tied, in the database, to the respective creator's ID, instead of his email address. I believe the email address is only used (asides mailing people, of course) as a way to prevent people of making multiple accounts. (Hence also why hotmail and other public email systems aren't allowed.) Hence, I also believe that when you delete a person, and then recreate one, the emails no longer get sent to that person, even if the recreated account gets the same email address. (And for this, you'll have to change the email address in the old account, first since, as Chris pointed out, accounts never get deleted, only flagged as being deleted.) This is because Moodle will attempt to mail the course creator, who's looked up through his ID, and then the email address from that row gets pulled from the database. And to answer Chris' questions ;); I indeed made admin2 a site admin through that method, yet his backup and restore possibilities still seem to be schizofrenic, at best. I have even gone as far as opening up the database and searching up if the admin2 account had the administration rights assigned to him. He had, so that can't be it. ResponsesInList.Text: Best regards. ResponsesInList.Title: Restore failure in 1.8.4 -- restorelib.php edit Fix
ResponsesInList.Text: I created a new instance of 1.8.4, restored the database from a 1.8.2 class. sql file, let Moodle upgrade alter the database tables. Everything seemed fine. I created a backups of a course (both with All user data and one with user data set to None) and the backups were created successfully. Upon restoring either file to a new course, I received this error: Fatal error: Call to a member function after_restore() on a non- object in [path to my installation]/m18/moodle/backup/restorelib.php on line 871 After several hours of adding removing modules, hacking the partially created temp/backup files, and puzzling over the error, I commented out line 871 of restorelib.php: //$blockobj->after_restore($restore); I reran the restore process for both the backup that contained All the user data and for the backup that contained None. Both finished successfully and restored the courses. The Blocks included in the original course worked fine in the restored courses. The partially completed backups before I made the edit contained no blocks at all.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Internal Links don't work when the course is copied
ResponsesInList.Text: The difference with, and without, the ?file=, is to do with the 'Use slash-arguments' admin setting. The problem that backup and restore has to solve is that a lot of URLs in Moodle, for example, .../course/view.php?id=123, contain the id of something in the database, and this will almost certainly change during backup and restore. Also, $CFG-> wwwroot may change. The solution adopted is, that during the backup, all URLs are encoded to a symbolic form. I can't remember exactly what it is, but it is something like $%COURSEVIEWBYID-123%$. Then on restore, that is turned back to a real URL , using whatever the correct ID that course 123 got restored to. There are only a few ways that this can go wrong: 1. When the backup is made, Moodle forgets to encode the URLs in that bit of content. (For example, you can be pretty sure that something common like forum posts will be handled correctly, but perhaps the person to coded up backup and restore of shortanswer questions forgot to get links in the feedback for specific answers encoded correctly.) 2. Moodle fails to correctly encode a particular type of link. (For example, common links like ../course/view.php?id=123 are sure to be handled correctly, but perhaps the link to review a particular student's quiz attempt is not encoded properly?) 3. and 4. are the mirror images of these: 3. Moodle forgets to decode links in a certain type of content when it is restored. 4. Moodle cannot correctly decode a certain type of link when it is restored. To determine whether your problem is 1/3 or 2/4, try putting in a link to something common, like the course view page, into the content you are trying to backup and restore; alternatively, copy the problem URL into some content that you are sure is handled correctly. To determine whether it is 1/2 or 3/4, look in the backup file. If you unzip the backup file, you fill find a file called moodle. xml in there. Somewhere in that XML will be your content, and you will be able to see whether your URL was correctly encoded. If it was, then the problem is at restore time. If not, then it is a backup problem. (Hmm, I think I just typed something useful. Someone should probably copy this to Moodle Docs , with a title like 'How to diagnose backup and restore re-coding problems'.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup and Restore doesn't  work
ResponsesInList.Text: After having flawless backup and restore functions for a full year, our 1.8.1 version of Moodle suddenly froze up at the last leg of these procedures.  The "backup" allows us to save part or all of the entire content of courses and the "restore" allows us to  transport part or all of these courses into other courses.  Thus, the web pages dealing with how to enroll, the privacy curtain, posting ones hunches and ideas for others to see all can be easily transported to a new course.  Meanwhile, as the modes of expression in one area improve (due to feedback from participants or fresh ideas on my part), then it is quite easy to bring the improvements in one course to bear upon all the earlier courses as well. So when the backup and restore functions ceased to work , I was surprised and than a bit alarmed .  Moodle has worked so flawlessly for the last year, that I had become rather complacent about its invulnerability . My first thought was that the problem was created by our server in San Diego, so I gave them a phone call and asked a good dozen questions.  No, nothing changed on their end. So, then I began taking a closer look at Google php files.  Moodle did generate a code error telling me that the problem was the following: Notice : Undefined variable: nonrestmod in /usr4/home/catherinecollege.net/htdocs/moodle/backup/restore_form.html on line 328 Thanks to my earlier work in programming, I knew very well what an "undefined variable" was but I didn't have a clue as to where "nonrestmod" gets its content and, more importantly, why (suddenly) after a full year of flawless operation, it suddenly failed to get its content. So then I went to the discussion boards for Moodle.  Quite fascinating really!  Tens of thousands of users are recording their successes and failures, their improvements and their revisions to Moodle.  So I did a search for ver. 1.8 and "failure to backup."  This brought it down to ten posts.  It was comforting to know that others were experiencing exactly the same problem that I was. After a few hours of altering small bits of code (always clearly recording what changes I made so that, if the whole thing crashes, I can always go back to an earlier working condition), thanks to the discussion of George M., I was up and running, at least as far as backup is concerned.  The import function also functions but generates twenty or so small errors.  The restore function still hangs up. Some of the posts were in Spanish so I was stretching my feeble language abilities to make sense of it.  Then I thought of using the Google language translator.  Here is the first line of a post: Bom.. o mesmo problema acontecia comigo e no meu caso foi observado o seguinte:  pós avaliar os fonts do site constatei o seguinte: The translator ( Bom .. Comigo same problem or event and my case was not observed or Seguinte: postoperative fonts do you evaluate the site or constatei Seguinte: What?  This is barely intelligible.  Why isn't "comigo" (the verb, ending suggests first-person singular subject) being translated?  From context , I could guess that "sequinte" means "the following," yet it too is not translated.  Could it be that the Spanish user is using technical words that the Google translator is incapable of translating?  Maybe.  Yet, I wouldn't expect this to show up in the first line.  So maybe it's not Spanish.  So, I try Portugese and get this: Good. The same problem happened to me and in my case was noted: after assessing the site's fonts found the following: Ah, much better.  So it is Portugese!  Here are the changes I made: http://translate.google.com/translate_t#) gave me this: Found solution at Original code in both places: } else if ($launch == "execute") { Changes made: line 125 (backup.php) } else if ($launch == "execute" or $launch == "ute") { Line 154 (restore.php) } else if ($launch == "execute" or $launch == "ute") { While exploring the php files, I came across this ominous note: This directory contains my try to create a backup/recover admin option to moodle. I don't know when and how it'll be finished, but I'm going to try it, sure. Some day, if this is fully functional, it could be integrated into the main Moodle distribution (ask uncle Martin). Code here may not be tested - so there are no guarantees as to the quality of the code in here, even if part of a stable Moodle release. So what is the upshot of all this? 1. The backup and restore functions that worked flawlessly for one year now demonstrate deep flaws (bugs).  Why?  I don't know. . . . and I don't have the time to find out.  [Help appreciated!] 2. I want to upgrade our current Moodle 1.8.1 to following the advice of the managing director of Moodle, Martin Dougiamas , who says the following: Each of the new releases contains long lists of minor bug fixes (see the ... I note also that the 1.9 version has upgraded the grading system and the  teacher's grade book--features that are of no current interest to us.  Moreover, since this is my first upgrade and since I notice many posts regarding features that fail to work after an upgrade, I do not want to make the leap to 1.9 until maybe a year in the future.  So here is what I plan: 1. In the next two weeks, I'm going to upgrade our Moodle system to 1.8.6. 2. I will choose the date to fall on the day after our server in San Diego does its weekly system backup.  This will allow us to scrap the entire upgrade and to revert back to 1.8.1 just as we left it SHOULD SOMETHING DRASTIC GO WRONG. 3. I've also made a CD-rom copy of our entire Moodle system as it exists on my hard drive in my office.  Since I've made a half-dozen code changes that improve the system, this will allow me to recover any or all of these changes and to import them into the new php files that will be overwritten in the upgrade. If you have any suggestions for me, they will be very welcome. Thanks, Aaron Dr. Aaron Milavec 2739 Queenswood Dr. Cincinnati, OH 45211 Vice-President Catherine of Siena Virtual College www.catherinecollege.net www.didache.info [More] release notes for details). Thanks to all the developers and users who helped with finding and fixing these. Several security vulnerabilities were also fixed in all versions, making it important that you upgrade existing Moodle sites. Even if you can't make major upgrades in the near future, you should at least upgrade to the latest stable package for your version. (For example if you have 1.8 already, then it's very safe and easy to upgrade it to the new 1.8.6 because there are no new features, just bug fixes). http://www.ohloh.net/projects/moodle http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=109022

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Transfering Data Moodle to Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Beth, Assuming you are using the same Moodle site for both online and onsite (e.g. myschool.edu) you simply hit the import button to import from one course to another. Then choose the course, select the items you want to import, and you're golden. Try this in a replica site before you do it live! If you are moving from myonsiteschool.edu to myonlineschool.edu (from one Moodle site to another), then you'll need to go thru the backup & restore process, including downloading the backed up part of a course to your hard drive and then re-uploading. Again, use a test site before going live.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup Stripping HTML  Angle Brackets in Course Files
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, The solution that we used. There appears to be a few out there but this one was easy for us. Please try this on your test server first. We killed our test server a few times trying a few different things, but this one worked on our test and live server. We are running Fedora 9 x64. Go here: http://rpm.pbone.net/index.php3/stat/2/simple/2 Search for: libxml2-2.6.32 We download this one: Fedora 9 download.fedora.redhat.com/pub/fedora/linux/releases/9/Fedora/x86_64/os/Packages/ libxml2-2.6.32-1.fc9.x86_64.rpm Search again for: libxml2-python-2.6.32 Downloaded: Fedora 9 download.fedora.redhat.com/pub/fedora/linux/releases/9/Everything/x86_64/os/Packages/ libxml2-python-2.6.32-1.fc9.x86_64.rpm Terminal: rpm -i /blah/libxml2-2.6.32-1.fc9.x86_64.rpm --oldpackage --force rpm -i /blah/ libxml2-python-2.6.32-1.fc9.x86_64.rpm --oldpackage --force We rebooted. Run yum Uninstall libxml2-2.7.1.fc9.x86_64.rpm (this will also uninstall libxml-python 2.7 version) Rebooted. It should work now. Yum will ask you if you want to update libxml2. Don't do this. You can add libxml2 to not be updated. Thanks, Jason and Josh (who did the hard work)

ResponsesInList.Title: I found a possible solution for the problem of non generating  backups
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, The problem of non generating backup copies have been appeared several times in this forum. All the solutions given seem to be based on a possible corruption of the moodlelib.php file in the lib folder. You can try to replace this file with a fresh one downloaded from the same Moodle generic version you are using, but sometimes it didn't make any different. Researching into that problem this morning, I noticed that, what is stopping the backup copy from being generated is the following instruction (line 333 of moodlelib.php): $param = preg_replace("/eval|system|passthru|exec|include|require_once|move_uploaded_file/i", "", $param); //mixed preg_replace ( mixed pattern, mixed replacement, mixed subject)

ResponsesInList.Title: Backing up the backup file - stopping the backup
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi we are hosting our own server for Moodle. I have automated course backups turned on which collect on the server overnight. We have a backup system in place that basically copies whatever we tell it on to tape. However recently the copy process has been getting stuck on the zip files that the Moodle backup tool creates. Has anone else had this sort of issue and if so do you know what caused  it? And more importantly how did you fix it? Thanks Heather

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backing up the backup file - stopping the backup
ResponsesInList.Text: You may have already thought of this and checked it, but in case you didn't: If the Moodle backup process is on-going when the tape back-up starts, there will be files that are OPEN, (at least the one that is being built up, and perhaps others that are going into the zip or database entrie keeping track of the process) and in that case the backup program won't be able to handle it/them. If this is the case, make sure that the two backups are taking place at different times.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: error trying to restore a course
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been hitting the same problem on courses with lots of quiz attempts. A quick search found the following about xmlize.php (I presume this is the same PHP routine used by Moodle?) (The emphasis is mine). " NEW: This Version works better with PHP 5 -- contributed by Eloy Lafuente xmlize() is a function written in PHP to traverse an xml file and put it's contents into a PHP array. It works best with small xml files, as big ones (larger than 1 megabyte) will result in a large array , too. There is a function called traverse_xmlize() that helps describe the structure of the array that xmlize() outputs" (from http://www.hansanderson.com/php/xml/ ) A number of places on the Moodle site suggest increasing a PHP memory limit. E.g. "Check your memory limit . It may also be that the "memory_limit" in your php.ini is set too low. Please check your php.ini file and allocate the recommended amount (see Moodle requirements ). For Moodle version 1.8 and above at least 40MB is recommended." (from Moodle docs ) Whilst this will circumvent the problem if the file is sufficiently small to process the whole thing 'in-memory', it doesn't provide a backup-file-size independent solution. It would be nice to see one.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving backup folder
ResponsesInList.Text: Kim - It's pretty easy. Enter your course. In the Administration section, click Restore. You will be presented with a list of save files. Locate the backup file you made and click on the file name. A dialogue box will open giving you the choice of opening the file or saving it. Choose save and click Ok. Depending on your computer's settings, the backup file will now save as a zip file in the default folder you have designated for Downloads. If you need to use this "backed up" backup, you will need to use the Restore option and Upload this zip file first, and you can then complete the Restoration. Good luck. DF

ResponsesInList.Title: Moving from one server to another
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been looking through and I may have passed over my answer, so if I have, please bear with me. I have been assigned to administer a new moodle implementation on a new server to support a new intranet. However, we have an existing moodle deployment on a older server which is to be retired. I need to know how to move all of the information, classes, users, teachers, etc. from the old server into the new one. We are hoping it will be possible and a reasonably easy task. Thanks in advance for assistance Tony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving from one server to another
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tony, It may not be a reasonably easy job, but it is possible. You need to do individual backups for each of your old courses and then restore each of them (one at a time) on the new server. That being said, there are quite a few things that can go wrong, so you need to thoroughly check all of the restored courses on the new server to make sure all of the content (images, videos, quizzes) etc were transferred specifically. As a side note, I've found that there are a few quirks with restoring to 1.92 on a Linux server that if you create a "blank" course with the same title, upload the backup file to that new courses file folder, and restore on top of the new course that it can mess up some of the dates and the length of the course depending. In this case I would recommend uploading the backup to the file folder for another course first (go to another course and select restore, upload the file and then click on restore) and when restoring choose "create a new course". More reading: http://docs.moodle.org/en/Course_backup http://docs.moodle.org/en/Restore
