ResponsesInList.Title: Restoring course with user data adds new user accounts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi -- We're setting up our Moodle server using LDAP authentication. We want user accounts to only be created from our LDAP directory. I've noticed an issue with course restores, where new user accounts are being created if a teacher restores a course (with user data) that includes user accounts not in our Moodle user database (i.e., LDAP), e.g., restoring from a Moodle course backup created on another Moodle install. We absolutely do not want this to happen. Is there a way to prevent the creation of new user accounts from course restores? I imagine we can instruct our teachers NOT to include users when restoring backups, but I can see this still happening. I'm concerned about teachers who may try to restore a Moodle course created on another server that has different users. Have I missed something obvious in how we've configured our Moodle install (1.9.2) that can prevent this? I hope this makes sense. Thanks much in advance.... Brian

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring course with user data adds new user accounts
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a similar situation so I'm just posting so that I get notified of any answers to this question. Brian, thanks for asking the question.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring course with user data adds new user accounts
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually, you may have times when you need to carry user information forward. For example, in a Q&A forum where you want the students to answer a question before they see each other's answers, *someone* needs to ask a question. We do large numbers of sections of each course, so it's no fun to go in to each classroom to ask the question. Our solution is to create template courses where the user is a global account called "[Your institution's name here] Teacher." We have no other users in the course and restore that one for each new term. Obviously, bringing that user forward.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring course with user data adds new user accounts
ResponsesInList.Text: We found a way, at least for now. We will prevent non-administrators from being able to restore courses. They can backup, but they can't restore. Administrators can restore. We simply can't allow for the creation of new accounts via restore. I find it hard to believe that this is the way it works. It seems very counterintuitive to allow account creation via a course restore. If desired, admins should be able to completely control account creation. This seems like a major hole. Brian

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring course with user data adds new user accounts
ResponsesInList.Text: Update: I restored a course in 1.9+ today where I wanted to keep the forum "starter questions" posted by [generic instructor], who posts in all our multiply replicated courses. During restore, I unselected all user data, then selected user data for forums, selected "none" at the bottom of the restore (where I was offered "course" or "none" for "users"). The forum starters were there when the restore was over, and [generic instructor] was a class participant, but the other users who were in the backup (but had never posted to a forum) were not carried forward into the new classroom. Note: [generic instructor] is a global user in both our old and new server. Thus, your mileage may vary.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving courses from one server to another (deploying)
ResponsesInList.Text: I just went through the exact process yesterday. Create a blank course on the new server and note the course number. I named it Transfer for simplicity.  Make sure it has enough weeks or topics to match or exceed the largest course you are moving.  Back it up.  That created the backup folder. Download all of the zipped backups of the courses you want to move to your computer. FTP to the new server and locate the uploaddatta folder.  Locate the folder number for your the course created.  Go to the backup folder and upload all of your zip files. Now login to the new server, go to the new course and restore the courses one by one as new courses. You can delete the Transfer class when done.

ResponsesInList.Title: Proposed new Restore type - Update existing course
ResponsesInList.Text: As part of the incremental Backup work for the OU, I did some work on a new method for restoring courses. Currently, when restoring a course backup, we can "Restore to a new Course", "Restore to an existing course, Adding data to it" or "Restore to an existing Course, deleting all data first" For the Incremental Backups, we needed an option that Restores to an existing course, updating the data. To do this, it uses a new table called "backup_guids" and each row in a module table  gets assigned a sha1 – for example, a forum course module gets a GUID/Sha1 based on the site identifier, the module type(forum), the id from the course modules table, and the instance of the module(which will generate a unique identifier for the record), forums also get GUIDS for Discussions and Posts so they can all be updated. - this "GUID" is also stored in the backup file like this: <MOD> <GUID>fd6d7a3001806017859a7b4268117fca72c0f0b1</GUID> <ID>20</ID> <TYPE>forum</TYPE> or:

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposed new Restore type - Update existing course
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for starting this post Dan. We'll soon have this option available in our VLE at the OU and already we're finding uses for it. for example we're involved in pilot work on some courses and we're considering creating a duplicate course and keeping it to date using this feature. This enables us to separate the pilot from the live version while using the live VLE features. It also has the potential to massively reduce the space required for backups when you need to be able to restore to a specified date for any reason. We're also working with other institutions that are unable to provide direct access to our VLE. This solution makes it much easier to provide our courses on their in house moodle and keep them updated as courses progress. A little work has also been done to improve the reliability of the backup process and make it easier to track down bugs when they occur. So I'd really like to see this feature get added to core as soon as possible. Not only to make backup that bit more reliable but to support additional functionality not currently available.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: All Backups Fail - An error occurred while copying the zip file to the course directory
ResponsesInList.Text: Once I had similar problem when I changed from one server to another. All backups stopped during file compression. It was because in the new web server (was apache and OS was linux), it was open_basedir restriction in effect and the executables, located on /usr/bin/ could not be executed. I found the problem after selecting debugging info to list all warnings, and then i did a manual backup. I hope it helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ang: Trying to move a course too big to upload
ResponsesInList.Text: Find the course number from the addres-bar in any course you want to use for the restore proces. Example given: http://xxx/course/view.php?id=195 means you are in course number 195. When you ftp to the site look for the folder 'Moodledata'. In this folder look for the folder '195'. Upload the zip file to this folder and shut down ftp. In Moodle navigate into course 195 and enter the file system - et voila! The zip file is there ready to be restored. The frontpage has course number 1, but some people are warning us not to use this for restoring courses. Best regards Morten

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scheduled backup fails for 2 courses out of 36
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, if the problem is reproducible only when "Course Files = yes", it means that something inside your $CFG->moodledata/XX directory cannot be read by Moodle when trying to execute the backup. XX = The course id you are trying to backup (you can know it by going to the course home page and looking to the URL . That's the number). So, you should examine file/dir permissions inside such dir, making everything there readable for apache (or www, or the username being used by your web server). Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scheduled backup fails for 2 courses out of 36
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eloy, I verified that the problem is not permissions related. In fact, it appears that my issue may in fact be a 'BUG' in Moodle version 1.6.1. My attempts to resolve this issue led me to placing a trolley load of debugging code in /backup/backuplib.php and other script files. I found that if I added a 'Display a directory' resource to my course and set the Display a directory setting to 'Main files directory', then this caused the course backup to fail. I further discovered that the backup process treats the Display a directory resource type as a regular file directory, and copies any subfolders and files in it as part of the backup process. From what I can figure out, this is in fact the problem, because when the backup process reaches the 'Copy Course Files' phase, it is attempting to copy files that have already been included in the backup, and is therefore failing somewhere along the way. I verified this by removing the extraneous 'Display a directory' resource from my course, and the backup completed successfully! To contradict my findings, I tested a similar scenario on a 1.6.1 Moodle installation on my laptop. In this case, the backup worked regardless of whether or not my course contained a 'Display a directory' resource. Confusing????

ResponsesInList.Title: Location of Backup Files
ResponsesInList.Text: I cannot seem to locate the backup files (or folders) on the server . Where do I find these folders/files?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Location of Backup Files
ResponsesInList.Text: To find the backup file for a course, go to the front page of that course, click Administration->Files, and look for a folder named backupdata. The backup file for the course should be found in that folder. If you don't see a backupdata folder, or if the folder is empty, then backups are not being made. A course backup can be made manually by clicking "backup" in the Administration block of any course, or it can be made automatically at scheduled intervals by setting up a cron job (only the administrator can do this). Every course will have its own backupdata folder. So, for example, if you have ten courses on your site, you'll find ten backupdata folders, one in each course. Each folder will contain one or more backup files.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Location of Backup Files
ResponsesInList.Text: When you log onto the server (using ssh or ftp ), you will find the course files under the moodledata directory. Under moodledata, there will be a numbered directory for each of your courses. The backup file for course 2 will be in moodledata/2/backupdata, and so-on.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Location of Backup Files
ResponsesInList.Text: If you have administrator privileges (you didn't make this clear), then go to the Administration block of the front page of your site and click the Restore link. This will take you into the backupdata folder of course number 1 (the front page course). Upload your zip file, then click the Restore link to the right of the file name. You will be asked if you want to (a) create a new course or (b) merge the backup with an existing course. Tell it to create a new course. If you do not have administrator privileges, you must ask your administrator to do this for you.

Here is an outline of a little script you can run on Unix to backup the database (it works well to have such a script run daily via a cron task): 
```text
cd /my/backup/directory
mv moodle-database.
sql
.gz moodle-database-old.sql.gz
mysqldump -h example.com -u myusername --password=mypassword -C -Q -e --create-options mydatabasename > moodle-database.sql
gzip moodle-database.sql
```
 For the files, you can use rsync regularly to copy only the changed files to another host : 
```text
rsync -auvtz --delete -e ssh mysshusername@example.com:/my/server/directory /my/backup/directory/
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Manual course backups fail in 1.9
ResponsesInList.Text: Find the username your web server runs under and then in a shell (as super user (root) or that username) type in chown -R www-data /var/www/html/moodev3/ I assume all of your Moodle files are in /var/www/html/moodev3/ so this command will change the file ownership to the web server, assuming the web server username is www-data. Although this is the easiest method and it should fix your backup problems, the other alternative is messing around with file permissions. You'll need to go through quite a few files so I suggest taking the first option. Note that if you have a group of users editing those files, you should also add them to some Unix group (such as moodevgroup) and then set the moodev3 directory permissions to: chmod -R g+rw /var/www/html/moodev3 chown -R www-data:moodevgroup /var/www/html/moodev3 First command is setting the group permissions to read write and the second one sets the file ownership to user www-data and group moodevgroup. "-R" means it does it for all the files contained in /var/www/html/moodev3

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I am wondering about the best approach for handling courses from previous terms? I'd like to remove them from the active student and faculty view so they don't get confuse old courses with current courses, but I'd also like to keep them fairly accessible in case faculty need to access them. What have other schools done? Thanks, Janet

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Thoughts about what to do with course from previous terms?
ResponsesInList.Text: Our university actually makes a new moodle instance every semester. You can do this several ways, by judicious copying of your database prior to upgrade or by simply restoring all the courses to a new instance. Depends on how many courses you have and how many people you have to do the work. We put an html block on the front page of the site and it contains links to previous semesters. Instructors and students can go back to any of them to see what they did. Because we use LDAP , the passwords are all the same no matter when the course was originally taken. We stop the cron and backups after we create the official backup of the instance so that it does not take system resources. We chose to do this because if you keep all the semesters on the SAME instance, it gets awfully hard to navigate the "my courses" block. We wanted the access, but also to separate it from the current instance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle and RedHat
ResponsesInList.Text: Guys Apologies if this an old chestnut but we are new to Moodle and Redhat as we have migrated from a Windows environment for this application My quesiton is based around the backup and restore enviroment for this. We typically use Symentic Backup Exec V10.d for all our windows servers and the relevant agents, such as the SQL agent for SQL servers. We are running Moodle on RedHat V5.1 and using PHP and MySQL Talking with Veritas we are informed that there is no MySQL agent, which is not a good start.  We have deployed the Linux (Legacy Support Agent) and are able to backup most of the Linux environment excluding a few folders So how do we go on for backing up the Moodle data and the MySQL tables successfully ? How do you do this and recommend it ? Do we need to script a shutdown of the MySQL environment ? Do we need to purchase a different backup solution ? Can you recommend one ? How do we ensure that ALL the Moodle environment is fully backed up ? Thanks in advance for any support over this issue

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle and RedHat
ResponsesInList.Text: There are three key components to backup: 1. Moodle database (MySQL) 2. Moodle data files (moodledata) 3. Moodle web files (/htdocs/moodle) It would seem to me that all you need to do is make sure that your moodledata folder and a folder containing a backup of your mysql database files are copied (either using a backup system or MySQL's built in backup system... which is what I use). You'll also want to copy your moodle web directory if you do any modifications to code from the standard distribution (otherwise, it's optional... you can always grab the latest build from moodle.org). I run a Windows box, but we're trying to get away from it due to PHP/ Apache memory leaks and hoping for better performance, so this is something we've examined a little as well. We've just moved to a software suite called " Microsoft System Center Data Protection Manager " which our network administrator seems to really like. It doesn't support Linux unless it's virtualized in a Microsoft OS, but that won't keep us from doing a backup of our server onto another Windows server off-peak and then using this program to back up that server. Best of luck and I'd be interested in hearing how it went from Windows to Red Hat, since this is our planned path as well (assuming I can't resolve these leaks). Perhaps we can share some ideas on these subjects.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle and RedHat
ResponsesInList.Text: Steve - Generally speaking you do not need to schedule a shutdown of the database to do a backup. I have tended toward using MySQL Administrator to create a backup which utilizes the mabackup command. Essentially you perform a dump of the mysql database to a text file and back that up. For the files end, I've been a fan of rdiff-backup but others may have other ideas. I suspect that if you do a little searching about how to backup a MySQL database you will find what you need. If you have any specific questions just let me know. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Does Moodle limit memory usage (override php.ini) for backups using ini_set?
ResponsesInList.Text: The ini_set and the moodle-specific command to set the memory_limit (raise_memory_limit - see moodle/lib/setuplib.php line 60) are used in several files relating to backups: To set the max_execution_time to 3000s (50min): moodle/backup/backup.php line 122, moodle/backup/lib.php line 690, moodle/backup/restore.php line 142 and moodle/backup/try.php line 21. To raise the memory limit to 192M in the files moodle/backup/backup.php line 123, moodle/backup/lib.php line 691, moodle/backup/restore.php line 143 and moodle/backup/try.php line 22. You might want to experiment by changing the memory_limit to 512M as in this post , or try using the GNU zip and unzip programs in Server -> System Paths -> Path to zip, Path to unzip. If you're using Windows, get them from here . To confirm that in tests with Moodle 1.9, I can replicate your description of hanging with over 400MB of files when using the internal PCLZIP libraries. I don't think this is a Moodle problem though - it's looking more like a limitation of the PCLZIP library. Can you please try the workaround and use the GNU utilities instead? See this in the Performance docs. Hope this helps! Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Making backup more reliable
ResponsesInList.Text: We've commissioned a project with Catalyst to add incremental backup and restore capability to the backup component because Offline Moodle is going to rely heavily on backup. The development work is scheduled to end around mid June. As a result we need to make sure the backup and restore process is reliable. We've asked Catalyst to improve the backup reliability but many of the issues we initially raised have now been fixed. That's good to know but it means what should we focus on now. Obviously there's no point fixing things that other people are fixing. For the Offline Moodle project we're only focussing on delivering 3 core modules initially including; resource, label and forums. So we're really interested in bugs that affect all modules, the backup and restore process as a whole or bugs affecting these specific modules. When we start looking at the other modules we'll have time to address those bugs at that point. So far we've asked catalyst to look at bug MDL-12037 which asks for improved error reporting when things go wrong so it's easier to fix the problem. We've found that particularly with the Module backups there can be issues that are hard to track down so it makes sense to address this. Tim Hunt just raised bug MDL-14302 to my attention. While this is listed as a quiz backup up issue it seems likely it could affect all large backups. the problem, as I understand it, is down to the main difference between DOM and SAX in reading xml . Since the restore process reads the xml into a DOM using the xmlize function at /lib/xmlize.php the corresponding memory required becomes too large. Therefore this appears to be a bug worth tackling since it affects all modules. So if you have any major concerns you'd like us to address while we have resource committed then please raise then and we can discuss the pros and cons.

ResponsesInList.Text: I'm wondering if we should look at using the new DOM stuff in PHP 5 for Moodle 2.0 - would be interesting to see if that would make much of a difference in memory usage....

ResponsesInList.Text: php 5's simplexml might be another alternative - I wonder what differences there are in terms of performance.....

ResponsesInList.Text: ...me needs to research before posting..... this is an interesting article on processing large xml files.... (although his testing file isn't all that 'large') http://blog.liip.ch/archive/2004/05/10/processing_large_xml_documents_with_php.html Dan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making backup more reliable
ResponsesInList.Text: Still -- all this DOM stuff is memorybound. The only memory-efficient way to deal with XML is to use stream parsers

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making backup more reliable
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, that's my experience. DOM is always intensive on memory given what it does. So if you want to use it's features You can only work with relatively small xml nodes rather than the whole document. Loading it into memory itself can add a significant lag. so a balance between sax and dom could be a compromise. that depends on how good the php tools are for using xml. I think that's the kind of thing the article is relating to. On other projects in moodle I've chosen to use xml as the data layer but used the serialise and unserialise methods of the pear xml objects to get native php which should behave better programatically and with memory. I can imagine that that approach is too late in the day since xml is used throughout backup

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup files are extremly large!!!!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Omar, AFAIK when you perform one course backup manually, there is one setting to select only "course" users (in fact, that's the default value of the setting). With that setting, only *needed* users will be exported (where *needed* are enrolled + users that have participated in the course, usually, unenroled users that have performed some actions in the course, like forum posts...). If you are performing scheduled backups, you can find the same setting (that will be applied to all courses in your site) under Admin->Courses->Backup. That setting should be set to "course" too in order to backup only *needed* users. Ciao PS: If your settings are ok, I'd recommend you to create one detailed bug in the Tracker. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup and restore nightmare
ResponsesInList.Text: This happened to us at the beginning of this term. A teacher had used absolute URLs to link to images within the Moodle course, but when the course contents were restored to a new course, the links still pointed to the old course. Here's how we fixed it: Note the ids of the old course and the new course Note the names of two or three sample resourses in the old course Unpack the backup zip archive file into a folder (that is, NOT into Moodle) Use a good text editor to edit the moodle. xml file, doing a search/replace replacing the old course id with the new course id in the resource links Re-zip the folder into a new backup archive package Restore the new backup archive package into (on top of, deleting the contents) the new course in Moodle Voila! Links to resources that point to the current course.

ResponsesInList.Text: I wonder if that's what happened to Daphne. Maybe she solved her problem and forgot to tell us (not cool). The problem you described would be a bug in backup/restore. Backup/restore is supposed to translate absolute URLs (e.g., change the course number). In fact, it only handles absolute URLs correctly, and does not handle relative URLs correctly. Again, you didn't mention how your links were originally created. Were they created using the "Insert image" button on the HTML editor? Or in a Quiz, images inserted using the special "Image to display" button. Did you search the tracker to see if this is a known bug in 1.8.3?

ResponsesInList.Title: Copying student data from one course to another course within the same LMS
ResponsesInList.Text: Sincere apologies if this has already been asked & answered, but I couldn't find anything similar to what I'm looking to do. We have an LMS for one of our clients that has multiple schools. All schools for our client share the same LMS, and we have different instances of the same course for the different schools. Sometimes a student will move from one school to another. This presents some difficulty, as their completed work from one school does not follow them into the new school, whose courses are all different instances from the first school. If you're still following, what I would like to know is if there is a way to copy a student's completed work (submitted assignments, quizzes, etc.) from one instance of a course in Moodle to another. I thought about doing it through backup/restore, but I couldn't find a way to limit that to one student, and I have no guarantee that the grades will not just make new resources in the new course, rather that placing the grades & completed work into the appropriate, corresponding course. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Copying student data from one course to another course within the same LMS
ResponsesInList.Text: Basil - The short answer to your question is no - there is no way to gracefully or automatically get the data moved. If it is the same instance, you may want to explore basically making the new teachers like parents of the student so that they could see the progress in the other class. Traditionally, at least here in the U.S., when a student changes school, the only thing that is transferred is the grade for the class at time of transfer. There is no guarantee that a student from Spanish 2 at one school will have had the same assignments, etc. Even if they are the same, it is not to say that they would have been assessed the same. I would be tempted to go back to the paper system and have the student print up assignments, quizzes, etc. to show the new teacher what he has done. The biggest challenge with this would be quizzes. It would be unlikely that the same questions (as in the same id in the mdl_question table) were used. Something like an assignment would be more likely to transfer the data; however, I suspect it would be easier for the student to copy and paste or simply reupload the data. It very much depends on what type of activities (online, offline, uploaded assignments). There has been talk about a backup option for students but I am not sure what progress has been made. Best of luck. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Do we need an incremental backup, if so how best do we do it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Incremental Backup & Restore plan Ended up sitting down and having a serious think of the design for this over the weekend. These are my notes -- nothing definitive, but I think I am mapping out the problem. I started working out how and identity-based approach would work -- thinking of "identity" in the sense of the "identity of the content, for example, as shown by the SHA1 of a file. You know with certainty that any change to the file will change the SHA1 hash of it (let's leave aside for a moment perceived or real hash collision issues), therefore, as long as the file hasn't changed at all, you will get the exact same SHA1. There are lots of good things that you can do with that -- but the main requirement for this to work is that the output (from restore) is stable. If the files you are hashing are unstable (like an embedded timestamp every time you save them, or platform-dependent newline issues) then the hash will change though the content actually hasn't. I initially thought we would have to work at the module or resource level -- but once I started fleshing out the plan I realised that if we can guarantee a stable output from backup, we can just work with full backups without changing the format much. The plan's gotten much simpler -- this writeup is long, but the plan is extremely straightforward So the outline looks roughly like this: On the server, provide a basic workflow that goes from the "generate a backup file" to "publish the backup file". Every published backup file is kept for as long as this course is relevant, even if superceded. Internally, it will have a unique name: it's SHA1. If the published backup file will supercede older backup files, we generate static "incremental" against its last N precedessors (or maybe against all). These incrementals can be thought of as "diffs" or "patches" and are identified internall as "from SHA1 to SHA1". Other aspects of publishing also take place - but are out of scope for this. Backup generation MUST have stable output. If content has not changed, then the backup must be identical even if other things may have changed - Ordering of the objects in the XML file must be stable newlines and whitespace in the XML file must be stable any export-time timestamps, or export-operation metadata (user running the export, hostname, tz) must be removed. Might need a stable uid for stable restore purposes (see restore below) Restore must be stable - it must be clear to restore code how to determine if a resource being restored maps to an existing or previously seen resource. This might need a uid scheme similar to Midgard/Repligard. Scenarios: New resource Existing resource - unchanged locally Existing resource - changed locally Seen resource - deleted locally With backup and restore being stable, a simple compact diff/xdelta of the (unpacked) directory tree from the backup files will be efficient. The diff/xdelta does not need to be reversible, and can declare strictly the SHA1 of the file it must be applied to. This means that we can produce extremely efficient deltas by not including context or "content to be replaced". One way xdeltas can just declare byte-ranges where the new content is applied. Review possible xdelta algorithms that we can ship as a small binary for Win32/OSX/Linux or that are simple enough that we can implement in PHP quickly. The xdelta utility on linux/osx is very good for this - and probably has a Win32 port Together with the xdelta generation it is possibly a good idea to have a PHP-based script that can do a XML-aware compare and output the UIDs of objects that seem to have changed. This can make the restore faster / cheaper. It can can run on the server or the client, but itmakes sense to supply it as accessory metadata with the "patch" file. The client is free to ignore it (and load all the restore file regardless) or regenerate it locally. The client always keeps the downloaded backup files, and knows their SHA1 identity. So when it "browses" for course updates and finds an update for course X,it reads the "new" SHA1 and it checks the SHA1 of the last version it downloaded, so it fetches the appropriate - file. If that file does not exist (maybe this client has fallen behind, and we only keep deltas against recent versions) then it will fetch the full backup file. If it has fetched a patchfile, the client makes a copy of the unpacked restore tree, and applies the xdelta. If it has fetched a full zipfile, it will unpack it and run the XML-aware "UIDs changed" script mentioned above. Restore is invoked to execute over the unpacked directory, and can take advantage of the "UIDs changed" hints file to avoid restoring unchanged objects. The latest unpacked directory is kept to serve as the base of the next update. If the operation has been successful, earlier versions can be deleted. One thing to note is that I don't think that zip generation is stable -- IIRC it embeds a timestamp, and perhaps hostname too. If that's the case, we'll want to compute the SHA1 of the whole backup using a more stable approach, and ignore the literal bits in the zipfile itself. Actually - different compression settings will radically change the bits, so yes we should make the backup id something more similar to a git "tree" identifier. What is a tree? And how do we compute a tree identifier? It is a directory tree (with as many subdirectories, and files is has). To build a unique identifier of the tree what we do is we Compute the SHA1 of each file Build a manifest with the internal path and the SHA1, like moodle.xml course_files/Media_examples/Test.ppt And then we compute the sha1 of the manifest. That SHA1 is the identity of the "tree" Note that we only pay attention to files - empty directories aren't interesting. This plan uses some hashing tricks, but core idea is to publish relatively dumb xdelta patches around. This will work great but has some limitations - most notably, if files in course files are moved or renamed, it won't do anything particularly smart. For a rename X to Y there will be an instruction to delete file X, followed by the whole contents of Y. And while we can address that basic case (by doing a "smart compare" of the tree manifests looking for identical hashes), the not-so-uncommon case of move + small change is extremely hard to handle. We could address that by using the git-apply-patch utility, which handles this gracefully. I need to think more about this angle - there are a few issues with it I want to avoid funny dependencies, like having to ship executables for windows in the client installer. The Win32 and OSX versions of git are excellent, but it's one more thing to support. And while we can probably implement xdelta and related tricks in pure PHP, git-apply-patch is way too complex. AFAIK , the git machinery produces reversible xdeltas -- which means that while we'll save bandwidth in move operations, we will waste it in every other change, as it'll include the "old" data that the patch replaces, as well as the new data. Using a plain unidirectional xdelta, a naive move detector on the tree manifest and training course content maintainers avoid moving large resources is probably a better option. Edit: There's a nice win32 statically compiled xdelta.exe here http://evanjones.ca/software/xdelta-win32.html

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Do we need an incremental backup, if so how best do we do it?
ResponsesInList.Text:
This approach keeps the existing backup file format, though we need to make it "more stable" in the sense that no arbitrary bits should change. What we add is a kind of a "patch" file. Imagine you have a course which has seen 2 updates: CourseFoo-xxyyzz.zip # the initial one CourseFoo-yyzzxx.zip # first revision CourseFoo-zzxxyy.zip # second revision, current at this stage you'll also have 2 "patch" files. For clients that fetched only the initial course, you have: CourseFoo-update-xxyyzz:zzxxyy.zip This file is a special format -- and the Client Moodle can use it to patch the old file it has, and the result will be the "current" file, CourseFoo-zzxxyy.zip And you'll also have the patch file for those htat have grabbed the first revision: CourseFoo-update-yyzzxx:zzxxyy.zip My hope was to simply include the changed
files and create an xml file with the changed data It's not that different The problem is that creating an XML file "with the changed data" sounds simple, but is extremely complicated as we need to rig Moodle internals to keep track of what's changed. Using a delta algorithm is way simpler and actually gives you far better compression. And once you are doing that, you may as well also use a delta for the binary files. A couple years ago this would have been "a nice but unworkable plan" but these days there are several very reliable and portable binary delta/patch implementations. So all the bits we need exist, are well understood and they are looking rather bored waiting for us to use them Finally I just want to clarify (...) So the
student will need to go to a web page and
enter the info. To make it easier, we can craft a URL for the student to click, the URL should include courseid, and SHA1 of what we have. The server side will then issue a redirect to the appropriate patch file to go from your what the client has (SHA1) to the latest version. If we have a bit of time... it'll be trivial to do this using curl directly from Moodle, and save the user a lot of clicks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Do we need an incremental backup, if so how best do we do it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Colin, we've done a bit of a review of the plan, and I am fairly happy with the approach I've described. Don't think we managed to poke any holes at the core plan. The work to make restore stable (implementing a uid scheme) is not trivial, and it will require walking a good part of the current backup code. The file format will only see a trivial change (backwards compatible). We are curious about the use cases and the audience that the overall Moodle Client project is meant for at this stage. You have mentioned user data, like forum discussions, that we didn't expect from the original description, and made us think a bit about distribution of sensitive data. You mention distributing forum posts, which necessarily implies entries to the user table - we'll want to filter each of those rows, exporting only some of the fields. How will Moodle internals react to mdl_user rows missing their username and other important fields that are never displayed to the end-user is a bit of a mistery. You may be wanting to "feed back" activity logs to the central server -- so that tutors can see what students have been reading. This is can be spoofed, but is low risk as logs aren't directly used for grading (and if the user is knowledgeable enough to fake it, they can hopefully pass the course.) We would not use the standard restore facility however -- any data read from the user should go through a security-conscious importer, and the restore facility is not ideal for this. Would you expect students to make "local" forum posts (or other local activity like answering quizzes or completing SCORM activities ) that are then exported to a "backup" file, and uploaded for restore on the server? Again, we would not use the standard restore facility for security reasons. While it's not strictly "part of the brief", I worry that user data is a can of worms. As long as we stick to non-user-related content, life is a lot easier Thanks to Matt Clarkson and Jonathan Newman for some excellent poking and prodding at my plans...

ResponsesInList.Text: Ok I think I see how the patching works. Does the sequence continue like this then monday.zip tuesday.zip wednesday.zip thursday.zip monday-to-thursday-delta.zip tuesday-to-thursday-delta.zip wednesday-to-thursday-delta.zip It seems that the xdeltas will get exponentially larger. My concern is that If the course is live for say 9 months there is a chance that the file storage required for (9x30 days = 270) 270 xdeltas could be very large. Also it seems that the set of xdeltas must be reproduced every night and again this would take exponentially longer as the course remains live. If this happens on 1000 courses surely it's going to break the server. I'm wondering why it's not possible to provide just one xdelta for each day that contains the diffs of the last day e.g monday.zip monday-to-tuesday-delta.zip tuesday-to-wednesday-delta.zip wednesday-to-thursday-delta.zip Then the restore process would just have to loop through each xdelta as though its comparing monday.zip monday-to-tuesday-delta.zip tuesday.zip tuesday-to-wednesday-delta.zip wednesday.zip wednesday-to-thursday-delta.zip Sure, this would put the load on the client but then they've only got to restore the one course and if it'll only be a pain if they haven't updated for a long time. It also means that we may be able to download the xdeltas one at a time so that if the connection breaks we'll still have some xdeltas and can run some updates. So the next time they update they'll have less to download. I know some people have limits on what they can download per session so this would help them get round that. I know this means using the xdeltas in a different way but I think it provides a more flexible solution and I haven't heard an explanation for why it can't be done.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Do we need an incremental backup, if so how best do we do it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Your thursday view is correct. In terms of the delta generation strategy, we can tune this later. I am not too attached to the "Delta everything to the latest" but it is more efficient network-wise (if you change a large file, and then revert it...), and it is also somewhat safer. The "safer" part is a somewhat-irrational thing on my part - the xdelta application scheme checks that the md5 hash of the resulting file so we know 100% that we have the expected file. Still, a chain of xdelta patches *is* more error prone than applying a single xdelta patch - but we know this machinery *will* catch the error if it happens

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Do we need an incremental backup, if so how best do we do it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, just wanted to put those concerns out there. Obviously server load when creating these deltas along with download size is as important as network efficiency. Just wanted to ensure we had scope to refine this and give you time to consider the points.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Do we need an incremental backup, if so how best do we do it?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Cool. One nitpick though server load when creating these deltas
along with download size is as important as
network efficiency They are not equal - network efficiency is more important. In this case, server load for the delta creation is low -- but even if it wasn't... it is still done on a schedule, and we can throw hardware at it. And if it takes 30s instead of 3s it only needs one user to be patient: the editor that is pushing the "publish update" button. And if it was really slow we'd schedule it to run on a separate machine. Network efficiency (as in: "having smaller files") affects every end user, and every download, and we can't workaround it if we end up with huge files. The scheme I outlined is good in both aspects (I think!), and there are always tradeoffs. But a having a central server do a bit more work to benefit thousands of clients is a naturally good tradeoff in my book

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup page1 from 1.7 restore into page1 of 1.8 not getting all my quizzes
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, here's what I have figured out about page1 backups versus meta courses. Definitive answer to everything in the world. If you are in the situation like we are of supporting multiple secondary schools with multiple teachers teaching the same subjects, therefore they are sharing multiple quizzes with images, DO NOT put your quizzes into page1 ( Front page of Moodle). We originally did this because everyone has “rights” into this page so everyone can see all the quizzes and images associated with the questions. Now we know the drawback to this. The reason is that when you do backups of your classes and restore them later, every single quiz that each class links to will recreate the quiz with all its questions within its own category for the class. Everyone get that? All the questions and everything!! Therefore you get multiple occurrences of every quiz. The better solution would be to build a meta “Repository” class and build all your quizzes within this class. When you do a backup of the classes that link to these quizzes on a restore they will not duplicate all the quizzes and questions within their own class categories. They don’t try to “own” the quizzes and questions. The META label takes care of this. So, inside the “Repository” class, you build your quizzes and questions, and of course the link to each quiz, just as if you were doing a class. The only difference is that you utilize “topics” for your setup of the class and build the quiz links in the topics windows after the #1 topic window. Then in the setups you hide everything after topic window #1. The students can open the Meta course, but there is nothing to see except my note to them that this is just a holding area and students can not access anything within. They get the picture fairly quickly and go back to their class assignment. Just keep in mind that the Meta class must be accessible to students in order for them to see the quizzes and their associated images. I certainly wished I had understood this better when we had to rebuild our Moodle site. Or at least this is what I think I understand at this point in time. Someone should add bits and pieces of this to Moodle Docs .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to select a destination folder on another machine
ResponsesInList.Text: If anyone wants this info, I figured this out with help from my IT guy. The folder saved in Moodle has to be on a drive local to that machine. We made a .bat file that copies the local folder onto another machine. Finally we made a Windows Scheduled Task that runs the .bat file a few minutes after the scheduled time that Moodle creates the backup. The syntax of the file had to be tweaked a few times to get it to work. I'm not an expert on scripts, so there may be a more efficient example, but this one works. Replace "server1" and "anothermachine" with the name of your moodle server and the second machine to which you wish to copy the backup files. The path saved in Moodle in Administration->Courses->Backups is D:\Support\backup\moodle which corresponds to "\\server1\d$\Support\backup\moodle\" in the script in my example, and "\\anothermachine\common\Systems\Backup" is the folder location on the other machine. Everything from the "xcopy" to the "/y" is on one line in case the forum creates an artificial line break. Add the word "pause" before the exit line if you need to see it in action for testing/troubleshooting purposes. Copy and paste this text below into Notepad and then change the file extension from .txt to .bat. After you've gotten it to work, use the task scheduler to fire it 10 minutes or so after your scheduled time in Moodle. xcopy "\\server1\d$\Support\backup\moodle\*.*" "\\anothermachine\common\Systems\Backup" /y exit

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best practice for moving content to different servers (Linux/Windows)
ResponsesInList.Text: All you need is the moodle directory and the moodledata directory and a Mysql dump of your database which you should be able to easily get from PHP myadmin. On the Windows Server depending on how you have that setup you drop the moodle directory into your http or www directory. Put your moodledata directory somwhere else. Then go in a set your paths in the moodle\config.php. I'm assuming you have your WAMP setup going. Then you use phpmyadmin to restore your database. Make sure you can access the database confirm your settings in moodle\config.php.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best practice for moving content to different servers (Linux/Windows)
ResponsesInList.Text: You need to restore each course one at a time on the linux server. Unless you want and have the experience to resolve the permissions issues of copying files from a Windows machine to a Linux box. The permissions must be checked and set from Linux when you're copying files and directories from Windows to Linux. If you have backed up your course and have the zip file you just point at it and restore it on the Linux box. This assumes that you have the same version of Moodle up and running and at least one blank dummie course (in Linux Moodle) setup from which you can restore from. Usually I just create a blank dummie course and go in from there to restore my courses. Now to be for an extra measure of safety you probably want to copy over your \moodledata directory. Which means that your going to have to set Linux permissions on that directory. Which if you have a Control Panel or a version of Linux that has a GUI (most of them do) it shouldn't be that difficult. Basically Moodle should be able to write to the moodledata\directory. You can do it by trial and error. Just make sure your moodledata directory is NOT sitting in the same directory or downline path of your WWW or HTTP directory. If Moodle can't write to your \moodledata directory or if it's not pathed correctly in \moodle\config.php you're moodle start page will look very funky. Now that I think about it there's really no way around the Linux permissions. Because even if you used something like xampp to install on linux your still going to have to deal with them at some point. So unless someone has installed moodle for you the permission issue will come up. Hopefully if your not familiar with command line in Linux you have a GUI you can use. If not Google "Linux permissions" and you get numerous articles that will tell you exaclty what to do.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Transfer moodle to Hosting
ResponsesInList.Text: For our sins we have now moved our Moodle twice now, and it is not a process to be taken lightly. We found that just copying the database was not possible, as links to files, resources etc were all broken as many were listed in the database as the full url (ie http://oldhost/moodle etc). Someone else may chip in with an easy way to overcome this, but it sounds like you should consider using the backup and restore functions. You should be able to choose to include all users with courses as well as files. Here is the process we used to go from 1.7.2 to 1.8.3: Install moodle in your new hosting, get all the additional mods and theme installed. Try a backup from your existing site of a course Restore it on the new hosting Test to see it works, see some of the problems we had: For some reason, we lost all user avatars, they are supposed to be included if you include user files. Minor annoyance Be aware that if you choose a single authentication method for users on the new site, any users who were created using a different authentication on the old site may not be able to log in on the new. I had to manually change some users whose original accounts had used email authentication to enrol. If all is well, continue on with the rest of the courses. I managed to get 40 smallish courses moved in a day, but it is very tedious. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Not able to backup course
ResponsesInList.Text: My backup/restore now works - all because of some great help from Tim Kellers here. Thanks Tim. The problem got sorted out by upgrading from 1.8.2+ to 1.8.4. The steps I followed were: Download Moodle 1.8.4 tgz file from – http://download.moodle.org/ Upload the tgz file to your Moodle site say the moodlelearning.org folder, using a ftp program. Unpack moodle 1.8.4 in the moodlelearning.org directory. The command to extract the file is: tar -zxvf moodle-1.8.4.tgz It will create a moodle folder You need to edit the restorelib.php file in your moodle/backup folder. You need to comment out line 871 namely: //$blockobj->after_restore($restore); Create a new database in MySQL. Database name: test / New hostname: test.moodlelearning.org / User: tim / Password: xxxxxx Fire the SQL query - ALTER DATABASE test DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8 COLLATE utf8_unicode_ci; Put your Moodle site in maintenance mode. Repair any tables. Next do a database export of your existing Moodle course. Let's say that the file name created is class.sql Restore class.sql to the new database test. Remember to use UTF-8 Rename your old course folder say class to oldclass Rename moodlelearning.org_class_moodledata to moodlelearning.org_oldclass_moodledata Make changes in config.php namely: $CFG-> wwwroot = ' http://www.moodlelearning.org/oldclass' ; $CFG-> dirroot = '/home/tim/moodlelearning.org/oldclass'; $CFG-> dataroot = '/home/tim/moodlelearning.org_oldclass_moodledata'; Rename moodle folder to class folder With a web browser browse to your moodlelearning.org/class/ directory and follow the installation configuration instructions Check config.php of the new install for proper settings Add all plug-ins. Note : Modify the above folders as per your installation. Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: course restores for non-admin users appear ~7 years early
ResponsesInList.Text: There is a problem in the restore component of backup that causes the dates on forum posts to be wildly off (7+ years) when a course with forums is restored by a teacher. If a course is restored by an admin, the forum post dates come in correctly. What's happening is that /backup/restore_form.html has logic that checks to see if a course has a start date, and if it does, it gives the user the ability to modify that start date. However the problem is that this start-date-checking logic is tied to the "course creator" capability -- if you don't have the coursecreator capability (and teachers don't) then it doesn't do the check, and assigns the start date to 0, which triggers some date offset calculations, which results in the wonky dates. I've created a patch that fixes the problem by moving this logic out of the "coursecreator" portion of "restore_form.html". As a result, teachers will now see the "course startdate" field as well, and everything works as it should. I created a Tracker report for this bug and posted the patch there: http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-12922 More testing and support votes would be greatly appreciated. Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup cannot copy User Files - open_basedir restriction in effect
ResponsesInList.Text: What is happening is that our server doesn't allow Apache User permissions to use the function is_dir($dir) with any directory below httpdocs. So when the below function in moodlelib.php is called with $recursive=true this error always happens. This is a situation that only occurs on Moodle 1.8.3 because Moodle 1.8.2 backup never calls this function with $recursive=true. function check_dir_exists($dir, $create=false, $recursive=false) { global $CFG; $status = true; if(!is_dir($dir)) { if (!$create) { $status = false; } else { umask(0000); if ($recursive) { // PHP 5.0 has recursive mkdir parameter, but 4.x does not $dir = str_replace('\\', '/', $dir); //windows compatibility $dirs = explode('/', $dir); $dir = array_shift($dirs).'/'; //skip root or drive letter foreach ($dirs as $part) { if ($part == '') { continue; } $dir .= $part.'/'; if (!is_dir($dir)) { if (!mkdir($dir, $CFG->directorypermissions)) { $status = false; break; } } } } else { $status = mkdir($dir, $CFG->directorypermissions); } } } return $status; }

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jon Have you tried the suggestion of using the GNU zip utility given in the Moodle Docs ( http://docs.moodle.org/en/System_paths ). You can also use the GNU du program in the same way. Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Allowed memory size of 134217728 bytes exhausted
ResponsesInList.Text: It turns out that good old php.ini did the trick. I changed the memory size to 512 and timeout to 600 Funnily enough, my backup.zip is 40mb with an uncompressed wiki.xml of 70mb inside it. Shouldn't really break the bank. I was stuck for so long because I didn't get any error message nor log file on over ten backup attempts. I finally got the error message "Allowed memory size of 134217728 bytes exhausted " and it was solved. So to make this thread a little more searchable: if 1 wiki backup fails - wiki backup failed 2 no error message or "Allowed memory size" message is displayed 3 or timeout on backup then go to php.ini and change the memory size and process timeout parameters

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Allowed memory size of 134217728 bytes exhausted
ResponsesInList.Text: Your average wiki page is probably about 4kb, which is probably more normal. I suppose if you give PHP enough memory (and enough time ) it will spill onto disk. Glad everything worked out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Third-party module backup.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Third-party module backup.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Emmanuel, here is a small point about backup/restore : 2 files : backup.lib and restore.lib First it is really valuable you make a little graphic model of records dependancies just as in other full features modules. This will make your ideas clear about what to backup and how to restore. Backup needs only writing in correct XML the content of all the records, pursuant you take care of a small set of situations : Records that are instance dependant (they may have a direct <module>id field, or being attached to a record that has one). A good idea is to force redundancy in the data model for all those records, adding the <module>id in each table. This will make backup/restore, and module deletion operation easier. Records that are course dependant or site dependant. They sould be processed the same way, as to say : be carefull of what sharing implies when restoring. That is : two separate instance may have a similar record set for common records. This might create data redundancy in the backup, and should be taken into account when restoring. Records that are user dependant. These rely on some users and/or groups being in the context . Fortunately, when a course is backuped, all its users records are also backuped when required as an option. The bacup process is aware of if user data has been required or not. You'll need to implement at least : the <module>_backup_mods() that iterates among available instances to backup, and <module>_backup_one_mod() that knows how to make a complete backup of a single instance. Usually we break the backup process into parts, each part storing one single table. If you want to have some info reported, make the <module>_check_backup_mods() function, that will give some info upon what WILL be backuped. Usually, we count instances of each recordset we backup, using individual functions. Last thing is preparing correct encoding/recoding of links within contents. This is done through the : <module>_encode_content_links() API call. (i.e. in third party techproject) This is for backup. Fore restore, see next post...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Third-party module backup.
ResponsesInList.Text: You understood it was backuplib.php and restorelib.php .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Third-party module backup.
ResponsesInList.Text:
For restore, things are little different. You have to : get back data from the XML , navigating in the XML tree. This ios not very obvious, but the good way is to examine other restorelib.php files. We use to put a $basevar on a node that is just under the list of elements, and use it as an array or a hash. The data can be directly put back into records, but ALL FOREIGN KEYS MUST BE RECODED. This is because you generate new ids for all records. Fortunaltely, the core team provided to us a temporary table : _backup_ids, that stores a translation for all generated ids during the restore process. This is part of the explanation why you should not refresh the last restore screen (the restore process forbids you do this). Here comes a typical sequence for restoring an entity : //This function restores the scheduler_slots function scheduler_slots_restore_mods($old_scheduler_id, $new_scheduler_id, $info, $restore) { global $CFG; $status = true; //Get the slots array /* This sets up a variable just at the entry of the slot list. */ $slots = $info['MOD']['#']['SLOTS']['0']['#']['SLOT']; //Iterate over slots for($i = 0; $i < sizeof($slots); $i++) { /* We make the array element being a variable for convenience */ $slot_info = $slots[$i]; /* prints debug output using a debugging function */ //traverse_xmlize($slot_info);      //Debug //print_object ($GLOBALS['traverse_array']);        //Debug //$GLOBALS['traverse_array']="";                       //Debug //We'll need this later!! /* we get back the old id of the record, as it has been backup, and we keep it in the freezer as oldid */ $oldid = backup_todb($slot_info['#']['ID']['0']['#']); //Now, build the SCHEDULER_SLOTS record structure $slot->schedulerid = $new_scheduler_id; $slot->starttime = backup_todb($slot_info['#']['STARTTIME']['0']['#']); $slot->duration = backup_todb($slot_info['#']['DURATION']['0']['#']); $slot->teacherid = backup_todb($slot_info['#']['TEACHERID']['0']['#']); /* this field MUST be recoded : it is a foreign key on the Moodle "user" table */ .... other fields .... //We have to recode the teacher field /* this is a very important step. The new id for the teacher can be found through this function call. We get it in the "user" table, where the old "teacherid" was. this can be done with virtually any record type, if you restored it before. This implies you CANNOT restore records in the order you want !! */ $user = backup_getid ($restore->backup_unique_code,"user",$slot->teacherid); if ($user) { /* we recode the record field giving the new value */ $slot->teacherid = $user->new_id; } //The structure is equal to the db, so insert the scheduler_slot $newid = insert_record ('scheduler_slots', $slot); //Do some output /* not so meanfull in first approach, but was in other scripts, so... */ if (($i+1) % 50 == 0) { echo "."; if (($i+1) % 1000 == 0) { echo "
"; } backup_flush(300); } /* finally we MUST tell future restores that our old id has changed, allowing future records to be correctly remapped */ if ($newid) { //We have the newid, update backup_ids backup_putid($restore->backup_unique_code, 'scheduler_slots', $oldid, $newid); } else { $status = false; } } return $status; } A last point is recoding correcly encoded links in content. This can be found also ion restore scripts from some complete implementations (techproject does it). Good luck !! And get a good XML editor to check the XML generated file !!

ResponsesInList.Title: How to Completely Backup Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm using Ubuntu 6.06 with MySQL 5.0.22. For my current backup strategy I backup my database by using: mv moodle-database. sql .gz moodle-database-old.sql.gz mysqldump -h localhost -u root --password= NewRootDatabasePassword -C -Q -e -a moodle > moodle-database.sql gzip moodle-database.sql I have set this on a cron timer for every other day. I was thinking about using rsync to back my moodledata & moodle folders. What does everyone else do?????

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to Completely Backup Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: I use MySQL Administrator to do the mysql dump. I was not that concerned with compressing the data. At the end of the year the database was a little more than 1G. I allowed the database to be backed up daily and keep the last week's worth of data using another cron job to find sql backups older than 7 days. I also kept a monthly backup (the one made on the first of the month) and a beginning of year and end of year backup. For the moodle folders and moodledata, I liked rdiff-backup as it provided me with the greatest flexibility and minimal transfer and ease of total restore. Essentially it does an incremental backup; however, it saves the information so that you can also reconstruct either the entire or a portion of the backup to a particular day. Again I performed these daily as well during off peak hours. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disaster Recovery
ResponsesInList.Text: I'd recommend backing up your Moodle directory also. That way you retain any custom themes, your config file, all modules you've been using, and any customizations you may have made to code.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disaster Recovery
ResponsesInList.Text: You are absolutely right, thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disaster Recovery
ResponsesInList.Text: Possibly - I would probably delete any data in the restored cache, sessions, and temp folders. It never hurts to have extra data in your backup. When I think of backups, I like to refer to as the Moodle trinity - data (the database dump), files (moodledata), and code (themes, customizations, etc.). I actually maintain a folder called patches in which I keep any custom or additional files stored separately so that when I am testing I can grab the latest from CVS and simply add my patches on top of it. I also keep a list of the version numbers of the customized files so that I can compare them to what is current in CVS and easily see changes that were made. I actually create diff files for my patches to make it easier on myself in creating a patched version of the file on the latest file. I would be curious as to what troubles you ran into with the database restoration. I have used MySQLAdmin and had to restore a couple of times when we were making some hardware changes and did not have any troubles. I try to remind myself that the backup is only as good as the restore. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Dumb newbie is confused
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there. In order for any of the regular, scheduled activities Moodle offers to occur, there must be a something running at regular intervals on your computer to trigger the processing of these events. In other words, all these scheduled things are only checked and processed when the moodle admin/cron.php file is executed. So, if you set up a cron job to run (lets say) every fifteen minutes, and that job executes the moodle admin/cron.php script, then all your forum emails, and scheduled events and backups will just work as you've scheduled them! Have a look at the Set up cron page, as suggested, and post back here if you have trouble. Cheers, - Luke

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cannot Restore Course
ResponsesInList.Text: I had the same problem, only I was restoring a course from 1.8.2 to 1.8.2. I suspect the same is true if you are trying to restore between versions. After many, many failures, I found the problem quite easy to correct. Whether you are backing up a course and restoring from your backup, or importing from another course you must do the following in order to be able to get clickable course elements in the new course: When selecting the elements to include in the backup, at the very least select the following: labels database assignment lesson quiz resource in the top grouping . Then, of course, select the quizzes and resources in their respective sections farther down the page, as well as any other modules you are using in your course. This will ensure that any quizzes and resources you have in the Quiz and Resource sections farther down the page are functional. If you ignore these top items in the interest of keeping a clean backup, you will have a list of icons that are not active. If you are using questionaires, exercises, feedback, surveys, etc, be sure to tick these items near the bottom of the list so they will be included in the import or backup. Hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup and restore in different moodle versions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Walter, I've had first hand experience with the utf-8 database migration because i upgraded our moodle from 1.5 to 1.7, last year. From Moodle 1.6 onwards, all language packs are converted to utf-8 and different languages may be used on the same page. Moodle 1.6 and 1.7 include a utility to migrate your database to utf-8. From Moodle 1.8 onwards, the database migration utility is no longer included, as it is assumed that you upgrade from a utf-8 encoded database. If you want to upgrade from 1.5.3, you must first upgrade to 1.6 or 1.7 , migrate your database to UTF-8, and then upgrade to 1.8 or 1.9. Read this documentation . Cheers, Chad

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making a copy of activity module.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello There is a way to do this - you have to go as if to edit the activity, then where it says "update" in the address bar, change this to "duplicate" - so /course/mod.php? update =543&return=true&sesskey=afR96GflDE becomes /course/mod.php? duplicate =543&return=true&sesskey=afR96GflDE then press return, and "Updating [activity] in Topic [n]" will become "Duplicating [activity] in Topic [n]", click on "save changes and you have your activity copy which you can then move to the topic of your choice.

ResponsesInList.Text: Oh, and for all of those who didn't figure this out by now. (Count me as one) The Max Upload Limit field uses BYTES. So, if you want to increase your max upload to say 5 MB you have to input 5 * 1048576 = 5242880.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Maximum Upload Size
ResponsesInList.Text: To clarify: the php.ini file (and many other byte size related configuration places) will let you specify M or K for Mega- or Kilo- bytes, repectively, and, as of PHP 5.1, G, for Giga- bytes. So, yes, if you specify: upload_max_filesize = 5 then it will cap uploads at 5 bytes -- not very much! But you can say upload_max_filesize = 5M and cap uploads at 5 Megabytes. (See http://us2.php.net/manual/en/faq.using.php#faq.using.shorthandbytes ) I don't know, however, if this "M" and "K" shorthand will work in the Moodle configuration/administration menu ("Maximum uploaded file size" or "maxbytes"). later...

I remembered that Hostgator upgraded its servers in July and they may have not set something right on the PHP or made some other change that is impacting it. I put in the following support ticket: I have a Moodle installation on my site at [site info deleted here]. Moodle is an open source learning management system that is available through the Fantastico scripts or via download . In June, we performed backups of all of our courses without incident. However, our server was upgraded in July and when we recently attempted to do backups or restores, Moodle did not function properly. After further investigation of the problem, it turns out that the $_POST array is not being populated, resulting in a redirect to the course list at line 73 (or so) in backup.php. We don't know whether this is a Moodle issue or server/hosting issue at this point. However, the only quick-fix workaround we could come up with is to change all of the "post" references to "get" in the following files (located in rlsei.com/academy/backup): backup_check.html backup.php restore_form.html backup_form.html restore_check.html restorelib.php The question, we have is, when the server was upgraded, were there any changes to the php or other functions that may be preventing the POST array from being populated? Could you please check the php settings to make sure that any scripts used during the upgrade functioned properly and all of the php settings are set properly. I would appreciate any suggestions that you might have to correct this issue. I got the following response: 
```text
The simple issue is that the server did work a bit differently before the upgrade and hence the backups made before this upgrade are not directly compatible with the server in it's present state. You may get the backups to work with some finessing but they will definitely not work out of the box. As far as specifics 90% of any issues with the backups will be from permissions. Also many controlling variables that were delegated by htaccess before must now be dealt through php.ini files. It is possible to adapt the backups mostly by changing the permissions.
```

In the meantime the $_GET workaround you mentioned should suffice well.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Labels in sections are not imported
ResponsesInList.Text: The same problem happens with backup and retore. Section summaries are included in the backup, but not restored in the restore process. There is bug report since March: http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-8848

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Labels in sections are not imported
ResponsesInList.Text: I had the same problem, only I was restoring a course from 1.8.2 to 1.8.2. I suspect the same is true if you are trying to restore between versions. After many, many failures, I found the problem quite easy to correct. Whether you are backing up a course and restoring from your backup, or importing from another course you must do the following in order to be able to get clickable course elements in the new course: When selecting the elements to include in the backup, at the very least select the following: labels database assignment lesson quiz resource in the top grouping .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Labels in sections are not imported
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Deb, my problem is only about the labels in top of each section. In time we found this explanation and solution: - While importing or restoring the process finds that there is an existing label and doesn't overwrite and skip it. What you can do ist this: - If you restore and choose during the initial steps "restore in a new course" the labels are correctly added.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Labels in sections are not imported
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Thomas, no its language independent. The problem is that the import process can't overwrite an existing element. A label exists at the beginning of each topic/week in each course. My idea was to add a check in the import/restore process if the label is empty or not. There are two workaraounds just now. Don't use the basic labels. Add an additional headline/text field and write your headline there. It won't be a difference for students. restore and import works fine. Use the restore in a new course feature.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to restore a course, step by step
ResponsesInList.Text: This is the logic I followed, but it took me some time to figure it out and get the info from many sources. I hope this helps others. Also please amend / give feedback on any mistakes ... 1. Backup manually the old course and download the resulting Zip 2. Open the file moodle. xml in the root directory of the Zip backup and see if there are any absolute links (eg http://mydomain.com/file.php/32/ ). Now open just that one file in a text editor, and do a FindAndReplace to replace all occurrences of " http://mydomain.com/file.php/32/ " with "$@FILEPHP@$". Save the moodle.xml file and overwrite the old moodle.xml with this new one. 3. On the new Moodle, create a new course and then visit that course and note the number in all the URLs for that course - eg if the course URLs are like this: http://mydomain.com/files/index.php?id=999 it means that all the data for this course is stored in the moodledata folder called 999 4. Upload the backup file to the new moodle using FTP (or any other method) into this specific folder /moodledata/999 5. Visit your new course and do a 'Restore' using the Administration menu within the course Write any other tips/tricks to doing a course backup to help others ``

ResponsesInList.Title: Backup function won't save Topic titles or text
ResponsesInList.Text: On testing the backup and restore function, we are experiencing a problem with saving Topic Block text/titles. The backup only appears to save the resources/files loaded to the course area, but NOT the text added to the Topic Blocks (e.g.to title the block, or to summarise resources). When the restore is performed, all this information disappears, leaving only the resources displayed in the Topic Blocks. This is a particular problem where lecturers are entering large amounts of text containing links to resources in the file area as the text and links are not restored leaving an empty Topic Block. Can anyone help?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup function won't save Topic titles or text
ResponsesInList.Text: I think I had a similar problem, where restore was only creating a list of icons with no text labeling and nothing was an active link to a course element. I was restoring a course from 1.8.2 to 1.8.2. After many, many failures, I found the problem quite easy to correct. Whether you are backing up a course and restoring from your backup, or importing from another course, you must do the following in order to be able to get clickable course elements in the new course: When selecting the elements to include in the backup, at the very least select the following: labels database assignment lesson quiz resource in the top grouping . Then, of course, select the quizzes and resources in their respective sections farther down the page, as well as any other modules you are using in your course. This will ensure that any quizzes and resources you have in the Quiz and Resource sections farther down the page are functional. If you ignore these top items in the interest of keeping a clean backup, you will have a list of icons that are not active. If you are using questionaires, exercises, feedback, surveys, etc, be sure to tick these items near the bottom of the list so they will be included in the import or backup. Hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Difference between BACKUP courses and EXPORT DB
ResponsesInList.Text: Does anybody know what the differences between doing a BACKUP of all courses is, versus EXPORTing the whole database ? I'm moving to a new server , and want to know what information will (or will not) get moved over in either case. Should I EXPORT the entire database, then IMPORT it on the new server, and then BACKUP all courses and then RESTORE them on the new server, or am I just duplicating work? Also, is there information I need to transfer over that will NOT get moved with either the EXPORT or BACKUP? Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Difference between BACKUP courses and EXPORT DB
ResponsesInList.Text: Jeff To bring down to a simpy denominator, if you work with backup files, u can always go back if something goes wrong. The second argument ist, you have a fresh, clean system and clean database, where you can make your modification without any disturbance. All information you need are stored in the backup files. I make a trick for me or for our customers. Make one course without any content and catch all user in this course. The risk to lost or leave anyone goes to zero! Be carfeull about meta courses and select the things u need, like user files etc. Note in both cases what kind of blocks, modules, 3rd party plugins or hacks, otherwise can grow up some problems! Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Export database then import with a new name
ResponsesInList.Text: Solved the problem... when you use phpMyAdmin to EXPORT a database, if you choose EXPORT from the Main Screen, it will ask you which database you want to export (it will export ALL tables), and it will then add the CREATE command to the file, so that when you IMPORT it elsewhere, it will try to CREATE the same database with the same name. The way to bypass this CREATE database, is to hit EXPORT from just about any other page except the main page of phpMyAdmin. In this case, you should get a list of all the tables in the database, and be able select which tables you want to export (any or all of them). When you go to IMPORT your file, it will NOT try to create the database, it will just import the tables into whatever database you want, even if it has a different name! See this discussion on the phpMyAdmin forum: http://sourceforge.net/forum/forum.php?thread_id=1810979&forum_id=72909
