ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore a webct course in moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: Please supply more information WebCT version How WebCT export was created Moodle version What steps you have taken What you expect to happen Errors or other messages You should be aware of the following bits of information: WebCT (at least, 4.1CE, the one I have access to) has two types of "course export" or "course backup". There is "Course Backup" which can be performed by an instructor (or someone who has instructor level access). DO NOT USE THIS . This "Backup" is encrypted and can only be used to restore a WebCT backup to WebCT. There is "Course Export" which is available only to the site administrator. This tool is available on the command line or can be installed into the web interface. Also, it can be made available to Insructors, but at the discretion of the site admin. DO use this tool. In my WebCT installation, it is accessible to instructors by clicking "Control Panel->Manage Course->Export Content->Export Course (radio button)" There is a WebCT-to-Moodle import tool. See the following: http://moodle.org/mod/data/view.php?d=13&rid=94 It works, pretty much. You will have to do a good bit of manual manipulation to get the course actually working in Moodle. WebCT and Moodle are just too different from an inherent design standpoint to analagously transfer content without any tweaking. good luck, seeyalater...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup Issues
ResponsesInList.Text: Having had problems with scheduled backups myself, though apparently not as serious as yours, I'm planning to stop using Moodle's own backup routine as my main line of defence. From my research and experimentation, if you copy your Moodle folder, your moodledata folder and the Moodle's database folder from within My SQL , you should be able to do a complete restoration of your Moodle installation by copying them back to the same places when your server is rebuilt, if it's a server crash which has made the restore from backup necessary.  (I can transfer an entire Moodle installation from our webserver to my local machine doing that, so you should be able to restore it back to the same machine in the same way.)  If you get those folders backed up to tape as part of your normal server backup routine you should be able to restore it if necessary.  Restoring individual courses would still be difficult, but at least you're protected against a complete server failure. Incidentally, I read in a forum post recently that Unix users can solve a lot of these problems by using a different zip program rather than Moodle's own internal routines (see about half way down your configuration/variables page).  If you're using a Unix-based server you could try that.  If Moodle's internal zip routines are flaky, I wonder if there's any chance of the developers extending this functionality to Windows-based servers so we could try using WinZip? HTH Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup Issues
ResponsesInList.Text: I wonder if there's any chance of the developers extending this functionality to Windows-based servers so we could try using WinZip? There's no need to. Use the GNU windows ports of this (as well as other unix commands) - see this thread . Zip, unzip as well as du are functional (although you need to make a moodle code change to get du to work on windows). Copying the .exes onto your moodle server into a shortnamed folder, e.g. c:\unxutils works best. Be careful though about the backslashes in moodle 1.7 and above! As for the backup question, I've also been using full mysql (mysqdump) and moodledata backups (ntbackup) on our windows box because of problems with moodle's course backups. As Chris points out, these are *site* backups - perfect for disaster recovery but not if someone zaps their assignment in a specific course (which has happened once so far). If you only have these site backups you'll have to do a full restore to a new database and a new moodledata folder - which is not much fun!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: restoring 1.5.3 course to 1.8

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: log.php file showing copying backup, then "error"
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi rajeesh, it seems that all the backup works perfectly but it fails when the generated zip file is going to be copied to its final destination. There are two possibilities: 1) If the "backup_sche_destination" in your server is empty, then Moodle will store backup files inside each course, in one "backupdata" directory. If this is your case, you must check that all those course directories are writeable by the user executing the cron task. 2) If you have defined something in the "backup_sche_destination", then Moodle will store all backup files inside such directory, so verify that the path is a correct full path and that the user executing the cron task has permissions to write there. Ciao

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi I recently had do just this - moving from a windows machine to a Linux machine. Using Course backup/restore would be daunting with 60+ courses. I upgraded the windows machine to 1.7+ and built the Linux machine up to and including apache2, php5 and mysql. Made sure phpinfo worked. Then I used mysql backup to dump the windows database . Copying raw mysql files can catch you out because your copy may not be consistent within itself. Hope this helps - Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring a BlackBoard course
ResponsesInList.Text: XSLT is an optional PHP 4.3 component.  If you run the phpinfo() function (which will print out much information about your PHP installation), you will see mention of an xslt support if it is indeed installed.  If you DO see that the xslt component has been compiled into your PHP installation and you are still getting the error, something interesting (bad) is going on. If you don't see xslt mentioned in your phpinfo output, then your PHP 4.3 probably wasn't compiled with the '--enable-xslt' option.  Compiling with that option does also require the sablotron development libraries. I hope that helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: unable to restore from backup
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi You say you managed to retrieve the backup from the old server which had a major breakdown (what exactly?) but is this a full site backup you are talking about? There are two main things you need to make a copy of - the database and the uploaded files. The Moodle scripts themselves are less important, since you can always download a fresh copy if you have to. There are many ways to do such backups. Here is an outline of a little script you can run on Unix to backup the database (it works well to have such a script run daily via a cron task): 
```text
cd /my/backup/directory
mv moodle-database.
sql
.gz moodle-database-old.sql.gz
mysqldump -h example.com -u myusername --password=mypassword -C -Q -e -a mydatabasename > moodle-database.sql
gzip moodle-database.sql
```
 For the files, you can use rsync regularly to copy only the changed files to another host : 
```text
rsync -auvtz --delete -e ssh mysshusername@example.com:/my/server/directory /my/backup/directory/

-----------------------------------------------------------------------


Is this how you have your backup?



Regarding the moodle.xml file, if you're not managing to extract it but
all the other files are ok, it could have been corrupted during the major breakdown?

Out of interest, do you have the moodle-database.sql file?
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring deleted courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Greetings, Kevin! Do you have any backups of the moodle data folder from that time? Or an alternative folder that your system backs up to? (you can have moodle backup within the course directory or elsewhere, depending on what you set up as admin.) If you could figure out what your course ID number was and you have the old files stored somewhere, you could get the archive and restore it. We do snapshots at the end of each semester and store them offline, as well as a variety of regular backups at shorter intervals. If you can get some information about the backup system you guys are using, maybe you would be able to find your archives (or even create a new moodle codebase somewhere and hook it up to a backup of your old database from that time, if you could find the backup). Good luck! atw

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help: can't backup a course
ResponsesInList.Text: Warning : is_dir() [ function.is-dir ]: Stat failed for /home/venny/moodledata/temp/backup/1181263260/moddata/ assignment /home/venny/opensource/moodle/backup/lib.php on line 314 Warning : mkdir(/home/venny/moodledata/temp/backup/1181263260/moddata/ assignment ) [ function.mkdir ]: Permission denied in /home/venny/opensource/moodle/backup/lib.php on line 317 (errno=13 - Permission denied) in Venny, If you take a close look at these first two error messages you'll see that the system is trying to create some directories in a temporary folder. So it's looking for moodledata/temp and then backup/1181263260/moddata/ assignment within this. My bet is that you don't have a directory called 'temp' inside moodledata, nor should there be one. It seems to me that the problem lies somewhere else -- possibly in where the whole Unix system locates it's temporary directory (or in the temp folder used in php.ini). You might want to check this out (perhaps with something like "locate temp" on the command line). Plus, you really shouldn't set permissions to 777 since that'll open up your whole moodle install to the world and invite hackers in to wreak ruin .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup own course contents only to external drive
ResponsesInList.Text: The following is assuming Moodle 1.8+. The instructions are roughly the same for older versions on Moodle, just with less options. To make a "Backup” of the a single course data use the Backup functionality in the administration block of your course. The Backup page is used to make a ZIP file of all the materials in a course ( activities , resources, etc) you select as well as the Students work (user data). By default all the categories, items, and user data are selected. When the back up is complete you will be on the “Files > backupdata” page of your course and should see the file you have just created.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I need to transfer a moodle-site, can i use backup?
ResponsesInList.Text: The basic answer to your question is "yes".  Back up all the courses and download the resulting zip files to your computer.  Then go to your new Moodle installation, upload the zip files, and then go through the 'Restore' process for each one.  If you've got a lot of courses then it will be a long and tedious job, because you'll have to do each course individually, but it should transfer all the courses from one domain to the other. I'm assuming that both domains are using the same version of Moodle.  If they're different versions that may cause problems, in which case check the Moodle site for information about upgrades, or hope that someone else answers your question here! HTH Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup entire Moodle site, how to?
ResponsesInList.Text: Those instructions include generic mysql options for mysqldump so should work fine in a Windows environment. However, a possible "translation" could be: c:\>cd \my\backup\directory c:\my\backup\directory>copy moodle- database -sql.zip moodle-database-old-sql.zip c:\my\backup\directory>mysqldump -h example.com -u myusername --password=mypassword -C -Q -e -a mydatabasename > moodle-database.sql c:\my\backup\directory>compress moodle-database.sql moodle-database-sql.zip On first run, the copy command may give a "file not found" error. You will also need to check that the path to the mysql binaries folder is in your system %PATH% environment variable.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do I restore a database?
ResponsesInList.Text: I am assuming you are using MySQL, and if so you should really take a good look at the documentation mentioned in the previous post. The following is a simple example of how to create and restore a database dump: Create a dump file at the command prompt: mysqldump -h <your_host> -u <your_username> -p <your_database> > <your_outputfile> Create a database to insert this data into, at the mysql prompt enter: CREATE DATABASE <new_db_name>; At the command prompt type: mysql -h <your_host> -u <your_username> -p <new_db_name> < <your_outputfile>

ResponsesInList.Title: Backing up multiple Moodles
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm (still!) having major problems getting our Moodles to back themselves up every day.  Most courses back up okay, but there are a lot that don't.  Sometimes the courses that don't back up are different each night, so over a few nights we'd catch all of them, but some courses consistently fail every night, so they're never being backed up, which is more worrying. I've been looking at various aspects of this, and I'm wondering if it's because there are too many things trying to back up at the same time.  One Moodle, for example, the other day started its backup at 0430 and crashed out at 1045.  Six hours seems a long time for one Moodle to back itself up, so I'm thinking there might be too many processes going on at the same time so they're all fighting for resources. We currently have something like sixteen separate Moodle installations on one server , and so they're not trying to back up while the server is busy dealing with actual students, I've got all the Moodles backing up overnight.  This means that one starts roughly every half an hour, depending on when the Cron triggers. (One or two are starting within 15 minutes of another one.) Does anyone know if the problem is likely to be that there's too many backups running at the same time?  Would it be better to space them out further, even if it meant some were running during the day?  Would the backups interfere with Moodle handling students, or would Moodle dealing with students interfere with the backups, or wouldn't it make any difference? Any assistance with this would be much appreciated! Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backing up multiple Moodles
ResponsesInList.Text: I think you've hit the nail on the head. I don't have as many instances as you (I have three), but solving my similar problem involved both setting PHP limits for uploads to a bigger file size to accommodate courses with a lot of content (see other messages in this forum) AND being careful to time the backups so they didn't overlap. But, with so many instances running, I suspect you'll have a problem not running into the school day, and that probably will affect performance for student activity. Have you considered splitting your Moodle instances across multiple servers with fewer instances per MySQL installation?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backing up multiple Moodles
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for that!  Do I take it from your reply that the size of the zip files created is limited by the upload limits set in php.ini?  That hadn't occurred to me, though I don't think that's contributing to my problems as I've already got it so I can set maxbytes in Moodle as high as 100MB if I want to.  (I usually keep maxbytes much lower, but it's useful to be able to raise it quickly on occasion.) Having just spent a few hours in Excel plotting the times each of the backups was running and the times that I got course failures I think it is just a question of having too many things running at once.  I've divided the period 11pm-7am into ten-minute slots, and in 18 of those slots I've got three backups running and in six of them I've got four! I think we might have to try letting some of them back up during the day, or only back them up every other night. Thanks for your help! Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backing up multiple Moodles
ResponsesInList.Text: "Do I take it from your reply that the size of the zip files created is limited by the upload limits set in php.ini? " Yes. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Lost, Lost. Lost
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Melanie, I think you're asking if there's any way you can access your data via the moodle.org site, in which case I'm afraid the answer is no - your Moodle installation wasn't uploading your data to the Moodle site (it would be a gross invasion of your privacy if it had been). Ask your administrator if the server was being backed up to tape, or anywhere else, or if Moodle was running scheduled backups anywhere.  If it was, then it should be possible to recover some or all of your data from there.  If it wasn't, then someone is guilty of neglect of duty, because data should be being backed up regularly.  That won't help you get your data back, but if your data wasn't being backed up then someone should get a kicking. One other possibility - don't let the techies re-format or scrap the drive which Moodle was on, because there are specialist companies who can try and recover data from crashed disk drives.  It's a bit expensive, we had to have a (non-Moodle) drive recovered a couple of years ago and it cost us about £350 (US$700), but depending on what happened to the drive someone MAY be able to get at least some of your data back for you. Good luck! Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Lost, Lost. Lost
ResponsesInList.Text: If it's not clear what types the different files are he may be trying to open files as text which aren't actually text (try opening a picture file with a text editor and see what you get!).  The files he's trying to open may be pictures, or database tables, or Word documents, or... I'd be inclined to get authority from someone at your school to take the drive to a disk recovery specialist.  I'm not quite sure how they do it, but they have some specialist machinery and techniques for reading scrambled data.  Don't let your IT guys play with it any more - they've done enough damage already, and the more they mess with it the less your chances of getting the data recovered.  Above all, DON'T let them try to defragment it or run scandisk/chkdsk. If you can get your uploaddata folder (and its subfolders) and your database recovered then you should be able to nail them into a fresh installation of Moodle, or even if you just get your files back you can then upload them one at a time into a new installation. The fact that your IT guy can get the disk to show something is encouraging - the drive clearly isn't completely dead, just badly corrupted.  I think you need professional help with this now - have a look in your Yellow Pages under "Computer Disaster Planning", or something like that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: where are the folder of the backups in moodle 1.7?
ResponsesInList.Text: When Moodle installs (under the default configuration) It generates a " moodledata " folder. this is usually above your moodle install directory. In that folder moodledata (if there are courses already setup) you should see numbered folders, a cache folder, users and so on. The numbered folders are where your course pictures and data goes (other then what goes into the database ) In those numbered folders is a sub folder called ( backupdata ). That is where you should find your backups. (if you preformed a backup for that course) Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Question About Online Backup
ResponsesInList.Text: Greetings, I've tried searching for this question, but have not been able to find my answer. My apologies if this is a question that has been answered before. Is the backup utility built into Moodle (and run automatically using cron or the Windows equal) able to be run with users logged in and using the system? If so, can the users continue to use the site as usual while the backup process runs? Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Question About Online Backup
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, users can remain logged in and use the system while the backup is running.  However, they may experience a bit of slow response while the server is running the backup, so it's probably better to run automated backups during the night while the server is quiet, but in principle backups and users can use Moodle simultaneously. HTH Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bacups available to ALL users??
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. You could probably put a .htaccess file in the backupdata folder, with directives excluding every ip address apart from the server ; e.g. Order deny, allow deny from all # specify the ip address of your server allow from 127.0.0.1 # replace the loopback address with the ip address of your server This will allow automated backups of your moodle data, but will have the undesired side effect that if you wish to do a manual backup, you will have to run it from the server. 2. You can automate the My SQL database backup of your Moodle database using the MySQL Administrator GUI Tool, or alternatively writing a script to execute a backup using the mysqldump utility. I use the latter option using a scheduled task/cron task to execute the script at a specific time. I don't have the script with me, but mysqldump --help will display a list of options for mysqldump. A sample script to run a database backup (dump) might look like: mysqldump --user=MoodleUser --password=******** --add-drop-table --lock-tables -result-file=moodlebackup.sql Moodle Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Help me understand confusing backup terminology
ResponsesInList.Text: I need help understanding the following backup terminology: student data user files course files The above three terms occur in the following paragraph, which is from the Backup/Restore documentation (see Moodle docs ): "Screen 1 provides options to select which activities and resources should be backed up. This screen also includes an option to include student data for each of these activities and resources. The bottom of screen 1 asks how to handle meta courses, users, log files, user files and course files . The continue button starts the backup process." Besides not being very helpful (I can read!), this paragraph introduces a brand new term student data which occurs nowhere on Screen 1. I believe the documentation means user data . If so, then unchecking all the user data boxes should mean that any student-related data will be excluded. Since the boxes apply to various types of activities, I assume that user data includes everything input by students for the activity, or side-effects of such input, like grades. For example, if I uncheck the user data box next to Assignments, then documents uploaded by students will not be included in moddata, and the grades given for such assignments will be erased from the gradebook. At the bottom of Screen 1 we are given the choice to include (or exclude) user files . But I already told you...no user data! So user files must mean something else. Images from student profiles, perhaps? Finally, course files . By process of elimination, I conclude that course files are any files which are neither user data nor user files; that is, files uploaded by the teacher to either the Course files area or to moddata. For example, in a Workshop, the teacher uploads two files (1) the instructions (2) the specimen assessment form, and both of these go into moddata. Saying course files = yes should preserve these in the backup, and saying course files = no should remove them. But if I say "no," what's left of the Workshop? To paraphrase Monty Python, Not much of a Workshop, is it?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Where are back-ups stored?
ResponsesInList.Text: The backup file(s) for each course are stored in the Files area of that course (Administration -> Files), within a directory called backupdata.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Where are back-ups stored?
ResponsesInList.Text: Sergio, The menu you showed (in Spanish) is the administration block on the front page of your site. Instead, look at the administration block in any one of your courses, and you will see a yellow folder icon named Files. Click on it and you will see another folder called backupdata. The backup for THAT COURSE should be in the backupdata folder (it is a zip file). If the folder is empty, the backup for that course has probably failed. You can see the results of your most recent backup attempt for all courses by running something like http:// yoursite/moodle /backup/log.php If the status is not OK or SKIPPED, then backups are failing. Most usual reason is running out of time or memory. Are you making backups manually, or automatically (using cron?).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backups taking a LONG time and killing the system resources.
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry to keep replying to myself, but my time to edit keeps running out. In ./school/backup/backuplib.php line 1750, function backup_encode_absolute_links follow on down to line 1774, and see if we don't see the code that's causing the issue here. Best as I can tell, "include_once" is causing the file not to be reloaded every time, but PHP is going so far as to lstat64() the file (and every directory along the way in the path to the file - each as a separate call to lstat64()), and the file is being opened before it is being not loaded because of the include_once use. I also note this from php.net - code was added to normalize the path to work-around Windoze: "This behaviour changed in PHP 5 - the path is normalized first so that C:\PROGRA~1\A.php is realized the same as C:\Program Files\a.php and the file is required just once." I am strongly suspicious that this 'path normalizing' code in PHP5.1.x is the cause of the exorbiant amount of lstat64() calls (one for each directory in the path to backuplib.php - which in my case is quite a few). Each call to lstat64 causes disk I/O, and doing a gazillion disk I/O calls in a short period of time causes exorbiant system overhead to be generated. So, guys (and gals) - now I have a more serious developer question: Me not knowing anything of significance about what is being done here - can someone point me to a good way to not have to do this include_once() call a few gazillion times during every backup run? And perhaps such changes might want to become part of Moodle proper - as I can't imagine I'm the only one running into this. Thanks,

ResponsesInList.Title: My large course backup problem solved - I hope!
ResponsesInList.Text: My problem with backing up a large course appears to be different from others' (see http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=63885 ) in that I can successfully backup from the Admin block but the backup was failing every night on one large course. I realized that cron.php was calling backup_scheduled.php, rather than backup.php, and backup_scheduled.php did not do anything to set execution time or memory limits. So, I added those commands and that solved my problem. Specifically, I added: @ini_set("max_execution_time","5000"); raise_memory_limit("500M"); Actual execution time of cron.php is now about 300 seconds and the size of the problem file is now 82MB, so these settings may be overkill. I'm not sure why this solved the problem because cron.php explicitly sets no time limit before invoking backup_scheduled.php, and I'd welcome an explanation. Still, I'm glad this backup is working again.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup don't finish the job...
ResponsesInList.Text: It took me some weeks to track it down. Here my results: 1) On one system safe_mode is OFF and everything works fine, no matter whether using external utilities with /usr/bin/zip and /usr/bin/unzip or leaving those paths empty and thus using internal pclzip.lib.php functions 2) On the other system the responsible admin turned safe_mode=On in php.ini After some tests I discovered that the slash in the previous post comes from the safe_mode_exec_dir setting when safe_mode is turned on. If I put a correct path in there, as should be, eg. safe_mode_exec_dir=/webserver/safe_mode_exec_dir, then the whole path is set before the cd command which is executed by the zip_files() function in our moodlelib.php, resulting in something like that: /webserver/safe_mode_exec_dir/cd which, again, does not exist. The admin had copied zip and unzip to that safe_mode_exec_dir path to allow the execution of those external utilities. But as I realised in my tests, the real problem is not COPYING the zip-file to its destination path, but the execution of the whole $command mentioned in the previous posts BECAUSE of safe_mode being on. I think this explains, why the zip files are not there even if we succeed creating them manually as root or webserver users and why some run into this problem while others do not have it. After that I dived into the problem of how to solve Moodle AND safe_mode. And the discussion is endless on php's side and on Moodle's side see the according forum: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=1374#286772 If I find a viable solution to have safe_mode ON and do Moodle course backups, I will post it there. We must differentiate also the case where Moodle is installed on a server where you have root access and where you DO NOT, eg. if you run Moodle on a provider's host . In the first case, Moodle runs normally as the web-server-user, and apparently everything should work fine even with safe_mode turned on, which definitely is not the case, as we can see whith Moodle's course backups. Not because of the different UID/GID which are affected by the safe_mode but because the safe_mode_exec_dir alters the simple commands like cd. (Please correct me, if I am mistaken by my tests or this problem can be solved so that cd gets executed correctly in $command.) On the other hand, on a provider's host, having safe_mode On, Moodle's php scripts run into problems much earlier because of the UID/GID being different when creating/copying/deleting directories and files. I hope this explains why course backups are not possible with external utilities when safe_mode is On. ResponsesInList.Title: How can I move an entire Moodle site from a Mac Intel to a PPC?
ResponsesInList.Text: I need to move an entire Moodle site that was developed on a Mac Intel computer, to a Mac PPC computer. Both computers are using Moodle/ MAMP installations. What's the easiest way to go about this? Thanks, -Brock

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I move an entire Moodle site from a Mac Intel to a PPC?
ResponsesInList.Text: Assuming that both versions are the same and you are logged in as the same user: On PPC Cntrl-click on the MAMP/data folder and create an archive (zip file) Cntrl-click on the MAMP/htdocs folder and create an archive (zip file) Use phpmyadmin, navicat or some other utility to data transfer / export the moodle database to a text file. Stick these 3 files on a thumb drive or cd ... or transfer to your intel remotely ON Intel, rename the original Intel folders to old-data and old-htdocs as a precaution Copy the compressed zip files to the intel computer (if not done so in #4); place inside the MAMP folder and expand; Use phpmyadmin, navicat or some other utility to backup your existing intel moodle database Use phpmyadmin, navicat or some other utility to perform a new query / import the moodle text file into the moodle database; thus overwriting the database. If the intel box is to have the same domain name as the ppc one, all should work. If the intel box has a different domain name, the MAMP/htdocs/moodle/config.php file file will need to be changed and the courses might have to be backed up from the ppc box and restored to the intel one to recreate the proper internal links ... testing will tell you. If things mess up, reinstall your mysql backup and rename your data and htdocs folder.

ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for getting back to me guys. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: selective topic backup?
ResponsesInList.Text: No, you do not lose anything if you make sure you select that you want the material added or appended, not placed in a new course. What you have to be careful of is WHERE you import the material. If you append material, the topics map across and if you have the new material in topic 1, it will "land" in topic 1 when you "append" the data to your course. So be careful that if you want the material restored in topic 5, that it is positioned as topic 5 in the backup. The other thing I should warn you of is if you try to restore a course with a lot of topics into a course with fewer topics, your material might all wind up in topic 1. I do not know that this is still a problem, but I used to run into it in Moodle 1.5 when restoring and converting old Blackboard courses. Sometimes the BB archive had more topics than the shell moodle course, and I would get everything dumped into the top topic! So my advice is to play with it a bit before you do it for real and take some care to align your materials properly. After that, it is pretty easy! I will also confess to you that I have pretty much mixed up restoring and importing in this post--I think you can use either method, the topic mapping should hold true regardless. Hope you are successful! atw

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: backup has problems with quiz questions
ResponsesInList.Text: I have had problems in the past with an old version (1.5? 1.4) version of moodle and lots of quiz questions and categories. You may find that upgrading moodle (after taking all precautions) helps. On the other hand others have mentioned that backups started stalling after the upgrade to 1.6. As I just advised eslewhere changing to internal zip/unzip routines, if you are not using them already, can change your backup and restore life enourmously for the better. By the way, you should be able to upload your course backups to the new server by ftp : 1) upload an empty text file to the site or course files. This will get moodle to create a folder in moodledata called "1", "2", "3" or whatever corresponding to the id of the course - "1" if it is the site files. 2) Upload the backup into the folder ("1","2", or "3" etc) in your moodle data folder using a ftp client in the same way that you uploaded moodle itself. 3) Return to the moodle GUI and restore the uploaded file.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup Issues with Moodle 1.5.3+
ResponsesInList.Text: Backups usually "hang" because the server has run out of time or memory to perform the backup. There are instructions on various places in the forums and documentation on how to increase the amount of time and memory allowed to the Moodle php routines that perform the backup. Do you have a lot of quiz categories? Are you using an inexpensive shared server? If the answer to one or both of these questions is yes, then suspect that your server is simply running out of time or memory to perform the backup. Consider using a Moodle Partner, or even your own dedicated server if that is within your budget and expertise. Very very occasionally there might be a problem with the database , due to a server glitch, or a way of setting up or filling your moodle database unforseen by developers. One way to test whether the problem is simply a question of processing power or something more serious is to install a moodle installation in your computer -the computer you used to post the message above. To do this download one of the installers on the downloads page or this WindowsXP Desktop Moodle . Then (assuming you have the expertise, ask again if not) you can dump your database from your server and put it in the database in your computer. Usually your 'client' computer will have enough processing power to perform the backup because it is dedicated to you alone. If the backup does not work on your client machine, even when it is the only task running and you have increased the memory and timeout restrictions to the full, then you may suspect a problem with the database. If then you do suspect a problem with the database then one thing that might improve things is upgrading your moodle to 1.6 (on your client machine as a test first or at least after backing up your database). I know that work was done on quiz categories to improve their display speed (for me in part, thanks Howard) and it is concievable that this would also have resulted in an improvement in backup speed too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Small glitch of restore.php and a quick fix
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear all: Just want to report a small glitch (and its possible fix) in the restore.php. I have confirmed that the problem exist in Moodle 1.5.2+, 1.5.4+, and 1.6.3+. In original state Moodle redirects instructor to system configuration page if restore is cancelled in the middle. This is undesired because instructors do NOT have access to admin page so they will be logged out. In this bug fix we have changed the code to redirect user to respective course index page if restore is cancelled. File(s) affected : /backup/restore.php Function/part of file affected : if user cancelled restore marked by "//If cancel has been selected, inform and end" Change: Replaced #92 or #85 print_continue("$CFG-> wwwroot /$CFG->admin/index.php"); with #92 or #85 print_continue("$CFG->wwwroot/course/view.php?id=".$id);

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Meaning of error message
ResponsesInList.Text: One more thing... Once I changed my original backup directory (listed In Admin->Configuration->Backup and the "save to" entry at the bottom) to grant write privileges to the group that owns the web server files ("nobody" group in my case). root> chmod 775 /var/moodle/moodle-backup Then my original settings for backup also began working. Moral of the story.  In linux or unix, make sure that permission on the external directories are set correctly.  This can be done in lots of ways (for example, if the owner group is "nobody:nobody" then let the "nobody" group or user write to this directory.   I chose to allow anyone to write.  This may not be the most secure setting.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup & restore - problem with group membership in forums
ResponsesInList.Text: Here's the solution!... There is a typo in the mod/forum/restorelib.php file which prevents grouped discussions being assigned a new group id, and instead they keep the group id from the source Moodle installation - meaning they are inaccessible. To fix this go to mod/forum/restorelib.php and at line 219 (ish) you should see this... $group = backup_getid($restore->backup_unique_code,"group",$discussion->groupid); ...it should be this...

ResponsesInList.Title: Vast: Please Disregard this Question - Problem Solved
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Error comes if there isn't any array in the foreach loop. If course don't have modules, error comes. There are three other foreach loops, which produce same error. And same situation on restore. Here is fix. In backup/backuplib.php is function backup_fetch_prefs_from_request(&$preferences,&$count,$course). At the end of it, about on line 2024, should be //If modules not exist, foreach loops falls without array if(!$preferences->mods){ $preferences->mods=array(); } I haven't test it in Moodle 1.7. Hopefully it's repaired there. - ari -

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore site backup - help please!
ResponsesInList.Text:
Pauline, Do you run the site
backup as listed at the following
url? http://docs.moodle.org/en/Upgrading_Moodle#Backup_important_data If
so most people just rename the old moodledata directory to something
different (so you still have it) and the put the backed up moodledata
directory in its place.  The same thing is done with the moodle
directory. The database is seperate and it depends on what
kind of webserver you are running.  If you are running mysql , A
backup of the database should be an sql or tar.gz file.  If it
is tar.gz you need to extract it until it is an sql file.  then
it needs to be imported back into a database on the mysql server. 
Be careful here, I have backups that try to import right back into
the same working database that moodle is connected to.  This
causes database problems that killed my moodle installation. 
The best thing to do is make a new database, restore the backed up
database into it, and change the moodle config.php file to connect to
this new database.  How you restore the database depends on what
system you are running. The reason that you have not found
anything on this is because there are so many different ways of doing
it.  It really helps to have someone who knows mysql database
maintenance because you can really get into trouble if you don't know
it very well.

ResponsesInList.Text: When I moved our site from an older server to a new server I used My SQL Administrator to do a backup of the database . Then I copied all of the files in the Moodle Storage directory to the new computer. On the new computer I installed PHP, MySQL and got things working with IIS . Then it was just a matter of installing MySQL Administrator on the new computer and running the restore of the backedup database. Looking at the log it seems the backup stops at "lesson" module each time.  The help file says: Some of your courses weren't saved!! There are three possible causes of this problem: 1. Error - this happens when the backup procedure has found an error and so hasn't finished the backup of a particular course. These are "controlled" errors and the scheduled backup continues with the next course. 2. Unfinished - this happens when the backup procedure dies without knowing why. When the cron is next executed it detects that the last execution went wrong, and continues skipping the problematic course. A possible solution would be to raise the PHP/ Apache limit in your installation (memory, time of execution...). By taking a look to your log tables you should be able to see if the "crash" is happening at exact time intervals (usually a problem with the max_execution_time php's variable), or if there is some exact point were all the courses are breaking (generally internal zip libraries, try to switch to external executables instead). 3. Skipped - this happens when a course is unavailable to students and has not been changed in the last month (31 days). This isn't an error situation - it's a feature, especially useful for sites with many unavailable old courses, saving process time. It seems to me that #2 is most applicable, and I can read all the words, but comprehension fails me.  What is the PHP/Apache limit in my installation and how do I change it?  Is there another log other than what I printed above I am supposed to be looking at?  What are external executables!?!?!  Can somebody please advise? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automated backup of course fails - OK to use manual backup instead?
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear M Gardner, Did you have a look at http://docs.moodle.org/en/Backup_FAQ ? There is one problem in there that is particularly relevant to the upgrade from 1.5 to 1.6 "Restoring pre 1.6 non-ISO-8859-1 backups to Moodle 1.6 - Unicode," but if it were an encoding problem it would probably not be intermittent. For me the most common problem is memory running out,and this may be more likely to occur in 1.6 since the functionality and number of options of moodle is increasing, and thus the memory required to perform a backup storing all these options is probably increasing likewise. I recommend using non php zipping and unzipping routines as is mentions in the FAQ by setting the zip and unzip variables in Admin settings ( http://yoursite/moodle/admin/config.php ) which are on my computer /usr/local/bin/zip /usr/local/bin/unzip That solves the problem for me since these programs use radically less memory than using php to perform the same task. Other than that you can try and reduce the amount of memory/time used by backup by.. If you are using only a limited subset of modules, you might also try turning some of the off on the admin modules page. Or if you do not need course files or user files or messages (etc.) you can control what you want to be backed up on the admin backup page. If you can't cut the above, then if you have access to your server then consister increasing max_execution_time in php.ini. Tim

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Newbie needs backup help!
ResponsesInList.Text: OK Art, I'll jump in.  Did you specify the day(s) of the week and time(s) of day when you want your backups to be made?  You must do this in Administration->Configuration->Backup.  Your cron.php may well be running on schedule, but unless you specify the backup time(s), no backups will be made. After setting backup time(s), run admin/cron.php manually from the browser and see the success/failure messages.  You can also run the backup/log.php script from your browser at any time to see a log of the most recent backups. Check under your 'moodledata' directory that each course has a directory called 'backupdata' with appropriate permission , e.g., 777.  If not, create them (that's what I had to do, and until I did, backups were failing). One final quirk that I discovered on my host was that my daily backup e-mail was being sent to me, but it was being treated as spam by gmail.  As a result, I thought my backups were failing. I hope at least one of these tips proves useful!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Where the heck did my course backups go?
ResponsesInList.Text: Greetings, Rob! The automatic course backup location is set in the admin area. http://yourmoodle/admin/backup.php One of the tasks is to set up the backup location.  If you don't set a location at all, the backups should be stored in the appropriate course folders.  If you set a particular location, the backups should be saved there. Did you (or your admin) perhaps change this setting?  If you did a manual backup as an instructor, would it be created in your course files?  Can you look in the moodle folders on your server and try to locate the files, or can you only see inside your own course? I am sorry, but I can't tell from your post whether you have admin rights or not.  That would make a lot of difference with respect to finding an answer! atw

By the time this third event happened, I already had some 1400 users on the system.  Out of the 26 new users, 16 had already had accounts made.  These did not seem affected, and the current account setting of IMAP was intact.  There were 10 new accounts created, all of them manual, since they did not exist on the new server.

ResponsesInList.Title: Some scheduled backups fail every time
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a problem with scheduled backups in Moodle 1.5 - I've tried everything I can think of to fix it without success, and it's driving me mad! We have 16 separate Moodle installations running on one server , and between them they currently contain 201 courses.  They're all scheduled to back up overnight when it's quiet (they're triggered by Cron at half-hourly intervals, so they're not all trying to back up at the same time). For some reason I can't get the backups to run at more than about 95% success rate - for example last night out of the 201 courses 10 failed to complete.  Some of the failures are random, a different course in one Moodle might fail on different nights.  (Out of the 16 Moodles 9 worked fine last night.)  That's fair enough, I know that some failures are inevitable, so I've got all the backups set to keep the previous five nights' zip files, so if something fails tonight I can pick it up from last night's backup if I need to. What's concerning me, though, is that some of the courses never back up properly.  For example, one of the Moodles only has 7 courses at the moment, but 2 of them have never backed up since I set the schedule up at the beginning of June.  Each course fails at the same point each night - one always fails on 'Messages', one always fails on 'calculating user files'. I've tried everything I can think of to fix this - I've defragmented the drive on the server, I've repaired all the database tables using the repair feature in phpMyAdmin , I've changed where the zip file should be saved (although it doesn't seem to be getting as far as trying to create the zip file), but nothing works.  For some strange reason, though, if I trigger a course backup manually from within Moodle it works fine, it only fails when it's run on the schedule.  It can't be because there's so much stuff to back up that the script times out, because one course, for example, when I back it up manually produces a zip file of only 73KB. I have no idea what's causing this continued failure of certain courses, nor why a manual backup works but a scheduled one doesn't.  Has anyone got any ideas what could be the problem or what else I could try, please? Thanks Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Restore breaking image references?
ResponsesInList.Text: I recently restored a course backup from a moodle 1.5.4 site (the "source site") into a course on 1.6+ site (the "target site").   The course contains about 1800 questions.   Most of the questions contain images. I'm not sure if this is relevant, but the course, which is #58 on the source site, was restored into course #1 of the target site.  This was done so that the images would become Site Files and would be visible everywhere in the target site  (all question categories are published in the target site).   This is supposed to work, and it seems to work just fine. After the restore, I logged in as a teacher in one of the courses in the target site to check out the questions.   To my surprise, many of the images appeared as broken links, while others displayed properly.  I looked for a pattern and discovered the following. Consider what happened to one of my images.  On the original site, the img src attribute looked like this: http://sourceSite/file.php/58/images/CBOS/CBOS 1-3-18.jpg Notice the space in the file name?  Yes, I know: a terrible practice, but it seemed like a good idea at the time After restoring the backup into course #1 in the new site, the img src attribute looks like this:

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore breaking image references?
ResponsesInList.Text: I timed out before I could add one more bit of information.... The original image files were uploaded to the source site as zip files and were unzipped through Moodle's files interface.  Moodle Unzip did not replace spaces in filenames by underscores, which (I am told) it should have done.  So the spaces remained as spaces.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore breaking image references?
ResponsesInList.Text: Two ideas for you, John: Do the images appear in the main site files? Course no.1 is the main site; if you are expecting these images to be inside a course, it will be a different number (2, 3, 5 or 7 by the look of your site); If the images are in the right place, are the filenames written in the correct case? Some servers care about upper/lower case whereas others do not. For example, your old server may have treated `CBOS  1-3-18.jpg` identically to `cbos  1-3-18.jpg` , whereas your new server might be slightly pickier .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore breaking image references?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris, The files were restored into the correct directory (moodledata/1) and the filenames are OK.  The problem turns out to be something entirely different. When I examined the contents of moodledata/1 more closely, I discovered that not all the image files in the zip archive had been restored, even though the quizzes that reference those images were restored.  The missing images were causing the broken links, not spaces in filenames! Now the mystery is why some of my files (actually, most of them) were not restored. Fortunately, I kept detailed records at each step of the backup and restore.   Here is the structure of the course files on the old system (the course was number 58 on the old system): moodledata | 58 | +----------------- images |                     | 78 images   +-------- C |         | |         214 images | +-------- K |         | |         91 images | +-------- Q |         | |         28 images | +-------- T | 39 images I checked that the zip archive created by backup contained exactly these files and directories. Here is the structure of the Site Files after the restore moodledata | 1 | +----------------- images |                     | 78 images   +-------- K | 14 images In other words, three entire subdirectories were omitted and one directory (moodledata/1/images/K) was only partially restored.  All 78 images residing directly in moodledata/1 were restored. I do not see any pattern in what files were restored or omitted.  For example, some of the restored images have names with blanks and some do not. Once again , every image is referenced by exactly one quiz , and all the quizzes were restored. Curious note: During the restore, this message was displayed: Copying course files..... File/Folders: 80 I have no idea where the 80 comes from.  There were no warnings or error messages during the restore that would have indicated anything was being omitted.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore breaking image references?

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris, A while ago you made the above suggestion, and I just got around to trying it.  I made a really interesting discovery -- possibly of a bug. Recall that I have a quiz question that has image reference with an encoded space (html %20): Following your suggestion, I downloaded the image from the old site and uploaded it to the new site (using the moodle "upload" button).  I checked the quiz but the link was still broken.  Then I noticed that moodle had replaced the space with an underscore when I uploaded the file: moodledata/1/images/CBOS/ CBOS_1-3-18.jpg Here's what I did next: Delete CBOS_1-3-18.jpg from the files area Zip CBOS 1-3-18.jpg (creates CBOS 1-3-18.zip) upload CBOS 1-3-18.zip (creates CBOS_1-3-18.zip) unzip CBOS_1-3-18.zip (creates CBOS 1-3-18.jpg) In other words, moodle replaced space by underscore in the zip file name, but not in the filenames of the contained files. I rechecked the quiz and the image was intact. So the solution is for me to make the transfer using zip files in order to preserve the spaces in their names.  I probably would have done this anyway, but this was an interesting discovery. Do you think this is a bug, or was it a conscious moodle design decision (or an intentional loophole)? John

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: simple backup procedure help
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Cody, The automated backup found in the admin section set for certain days of the week does a full backup of each course. You can set it to backup all content and user data if you like. The resultant zip files for each course will be saved in the backup folder of each course. You can tell it on the same screen to save them all in a designated folder, which is a good way of ensuring they are easy to locate and indeed the folder can then be backed up to tape or alternative server . This backup I call "automated course backups". Other backups include: site backup - where you use a tool like rsync to backup moodledata folder and do a dump of the database manual course backup - which is what you describe you do inside each individual course, click on the backup link and perform a one-off backup of that course I hope this answers your questions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Changing ISPs and 1.5 to 1.6
ResponsesInList.Text: This is really easy, as long as you use the same software ( database software, specially) and version in the old and new servers and the same DNS name ( www.mymoodle.com ). Make a dump of your database (my sql dump, pg_dump, etc.) and copy that file to your new server. Create the database user and empty moodle database in the new server, and restore your dump in that new empty database. Next copy all of your Moodle files (both Moodle files and moodledata files) to the new server, adjust your config.php file, and ¡voila! you'r done Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nico and Leon, I'm making some tests just now! Checking zip files, cross platform issues and other things... I tell you my results ASAP! Sure! For now, one test that you can do is to run zip and unzip external executables under Win32 (instead of internal library, that is your case). To use external zip & unzip commands, please follow this steps: 1.- Download the "bin.zip" attached here. It contains zip and unzip commands for Win32 (from http://www.info-zip.org/pub/infozip/ ). 2.-Uncompress the "bin.zip" file. A "bin" folder will be created (it has two files inside: "zip.exe" and "unzip.exe"). 3.-Move the "bin" folder to c:\ 4.-Login to Moodle (as admin). 5.-Go to "Administration/Configure" 6.-Fill the "zip" and "unzip" fields with "c:\bin\zip" and "c:\bin\unzip" respectively. 7.-Make a backup of your courses. 8.-Try to restore them Is this working for you? Anyway I'll try to resolve the problem with internal zip library too. Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Why can't teachers restore backups on to courses they own?
ResponsesInList.Text: From Paolo: "As teacher you can only restore a backup upon the same course from which the backup file has been created" Well that's not 100% correct. You can perform a backup, then copy it ( download - upload ) to another course were you have teacher rights and then restore it there without problems. Only the possibility of executing the "remote" restore is forbidden, perhaps as a measure against accidental deletion of courses by mistake. By proceeding with the manual copy of the backup file to the destination course and then performing an allowed "local" restore is, if I'm not wrong, the way (and a bit more of work, yep). And, this has been the behaviour since the beginning (Moodle 1.2?). I remember myself coding it some years ago and basically it worked the same . Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Failure on Restore - 'Creating Scales'?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mike, some days ago I received one backup file with the same problem (binary data in DB). I tried to reproduce it but I got some errors uploading files and I forgot it, not being able to store binary data in wiki tables. Anyway, it's 100% true that, if you save binary data directly to the XML file it will be broken. Some type of encoding must be done before (to binhex, base64, unicode streams or something similar) to be "storable" in an XML file. I think that base64 is the recommended one and base64_encode() and base64_decode() should be the functions to use. I think that this type of functions (to read and write binary data in XML) should be created "centrally" to allow incoming modules to use them too. And finally, examining wiki tables, I've seen that columns in wiki module are defined as "textual" columns and I think that this could give you some problems too (character conversion...). Doesn't that type of columns be defined as "binary" columns? Perhaps having wiki attachments stored out could simplify things too... Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Failure on Restore - 'Creating Scales'?
ResponsesInList.Text: I fixed my own problem, with help from others here. Like someone guessed.....I had a corrupt character in a simple web page resource.  How it got there is a mystery.  But I simply deleted that resouce from my course, did another backup and moved the zip file to a new server where it then was able to restore! Lucky for me I had a linux box with a text editor that allowed me to seek to line 9600 in my xml backup file. Steps to debug a restore that does not work. ================================== - try the restore on a server that is not the one with the original course data - or just use the same server - it is best to use a moodle server with the same moodle version - attempt the restore with the moodle web interface - Write down the line number where the error occured - use a zip utility to unzip the backup.zip  file - use a good text editor to open the big old XML file - use the editor to seek out that line number, or just page down and down - see if there are any clues about the content, look above, look below - quit and do not save using the text editor - go back to your course on the original server if it is still working - login to moodle with teacher or admin privlidges - find the content that may have a corrupt character or binary data - delete that content - use the backup to create another zip file - copy the backup file to a new server - on my linux server the folder "backupdata" is hard to find /var/lib/moodle/1/backupdata/filename.zip - use the moodle web interface to select restore - hope you don't get an error in the same line number or close Thanks so much. I will be updating the moodle.org wiki documentation on backup and restore.  They need some major work. http://docs.moodle.org/en/Restore I'm guessing most people don't ever backup their courses.  Even fewer people ever practice a restore.     A real safety drill is to put the passengers into lifeboats and then on to a different boat! http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=15764#226017

ResponsesInList.Text: However, it seems section titles and course structure import is still not supported in import course data. It seems to me there should be an option to 'duplicate previous course'. Here is the scenario: say your institution uses LDAP or other method of automatically setting up course shells. So you taught My Course 101 in the fall semester, and you had it set up how you liked it. So your course shell gets automatically setup for My Course 101 for the spring semester, and of course it is empty as the 'template' course was. Cool, you'll use 'import course data' to bring in 'My Course 101' from the previous semester. But that loses all your section titles and your course organization (if you had more/less sections than the template course)8-(. So instead, you have to go into your fall course, backup the fall course, download it, upload to your spring course, and do a 'restore to current course, deleting it first', to get a duplicate of your fall course in your spring course. This is a real problem with large courses. It seems to me the best solution would be for an option in import course data, for teachers to duplicate a course they are a teacher of, over the course they are in (with a warning of course). A second, more awkward solution would be for teachers to be allowed to use the admin feature of copying one course over another course (Restore to existing course, deleting it first), if they are a teacher of both courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Significant improvement of Backup codes in 1.5.4 and 1.6 beta?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, we are currently using 1.5.2+ code base and regularly we need to backup 10000+ course (most of them are empty courses but we can't delete them) on weekly basis. The 1.5.2 backup code does not work very well. Although the backup process seems to be going through each course OK, but it would take a long time (sometimes days) to just backup all courses, and sometimes some of the courses could not even be restored correctly. I'm just curious whether in 1.5.4 or 1.6 beta there is any significant code changes for the backup / restore module, that might improve the performance?? Please let me know, thanks a lot!!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Significant improvement of Backup codes in 1.5.4 and 1.6 beta?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Wen, backup (and specially restore) are heavy tasks, so it's really difficult to improve their performance. For sites running thousand of courses (well, for every site in general) is highly recommended to perform FULL backups of the site (moodledata + db) to be 100% confident about nothing being lost. Also, minor improvements + bug fixes are added between releases (major and minor), so it's always recommended to use the last one version available for the release you are using. In this case 1.5.4+ for you. Anyway, under 1.6 one new feature will debut. It will allow to skip some courses to be backedup by the scheduled backup if they are hidden and they haven't been modified in the last 30 days. Perhaps this will help your site, reducing the number of courses to backup... Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error in Backup Error Email?
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Dave Kirby, mdl_course is the table in your moodle database that stores your courses. If you unzip and upload the database administration adon MYSQL Admin to your moodle/admin folder the administrator will see a new database icon on the main page. Click it to enter the database. You will see a long list of tables in your database in the left hand frame. One of them is the mdl_course table (or perhaphs moodle_course). If you click it and press view in the right hand frame you will see the array of data about your courses. I think that Eloy is asking how many rows there are in that table.  There should be one row for each course. It is not advisable to change anything in the database unless you know what you are doing, but it is okay to looko.

We've got a lot of students in the system who are graduating and I'm sure there are some instructors who won't be using their courses next year. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: stop @ zipping files
ResponsesInList.Text: If the backup stops at zipping files I'll suggest you to use external commands to execute the zip, instead of using Moodle internal routines. Yo can do that by configuring the "zip" and "unzip" settings in your "Administration/Configure/Variables" page. The reason is that, due to the nature of PHP, Apache and the internal zip routines, the memory needed to generate zip files are the sum of the size of the files being compressed. And, as the number of courses and their size grows, it's possible to raise some memory limit. If you use the external commands as suggested before, that memory problem will be avoided completely. Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What shall I backup in Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: You should also backup your database . That's about it. Of course if you have any hacks or add-ons, you may want to keep a copy of that code somewhere, but all of your "data" will be stored in moodledata and the database, so if you have those backed-up then you should be able to recover from any problems. How often to backup? That depends...I backup daily/weekly/monthly, (actually my server does it for me). Think of it this way...you can only restore from your latest backup, so if your latest backup was six months ago, then that is what you have available if you need to recover data. Steve

ResponsesInList.Text: Line 91 is irrelevant! When PHP scripts go through loops that cause them to exceed the maximum time limit, the time limit will often cause it to halt at a completely arbitrary point. I then changed all references to '/2/' in the new course to '/12/' and the diagrams all became visible. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup explanation needs work
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Jon, I think I can answer what gets backed up and where during the backups that go
on within moodle itself. You can choose which sections of a course and which files are saved in the back
up within the moodle backup interface. The backups are stored by default in the course folder within the moodledata
folder in zip format. Each course has a number. If you look in the
corresponding number folder in moodledata, you will find the backups. In the
zip file are folders containing the user and course data files you chose to
keep (in the same form they would exist in the moodledata folder), along with
an xml file that contains the data from the database for the things you chose
to back up. The moodle docs Backup FAQ has a section on what items are not included in
backups no matter what you choose. http://docs.moodle.org/en/Backup_FAQ For the automated backups that you can setup with in the admin configuration
section you can change the backup location to any directory you like, but the
zipfiles generated are exactly like the ones in the moodledata folder. Again, the hardest thing to get my mind around was the fact that these
selective course backups are really used mainly AFAIK to set up new courses and
transfer content from one course to another. Emergency backups, I take it, are
best done by backing up and restoring the entire moodledata folder and database
outside of moodle. Thank you for the information on the MYSQL database backup. I've been using PHPMYADMIN for some time, and my original question arose when I
got errors trying to restore my database in PHPMYADMIN. There are also issues with larger databases  (Over 8 MB) and character
encoding with PHPAdmin. (See the Backup FAQ http://docs.moodle.org/en/Backup_FAQ ) I haven't had any trouble backing up the database using various methods. It is
Restoring that gives me problems, and a backup that can't be restored isn't
worth much! The best account of the manual backup procedure I've seen was in this forum by
Sree Krao: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=16738&parent=81073 The restore procedure mentioned here, especially, seems to be missing from
moodledocs. The MoodleDocs Upgrading article mentions an optional database web interface.
Does anyone know if this is the same as the mySQLadmin Integration at http://download.moodle.org/modules/integrations.php (which is supposedly just a
repackaging of PHPmyadmin) or the dbadmin module in the CVS contrib folder? Wouldn't it be nice if there were one page that listed all the various mods and
additions, their official names in CVS, and what each one did? Does anyone know
of such a list? At any rate, thanks again Jon for the information and for the original
question. Things are getting a bit less foggy, for me at least.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Simple advice
ResponsesInList.Text: If you did a database backup (with my sql dump or similar tools), doing a restore is quite simple. You just feed the file into mysql command, and it restores the contents directly (a mysql backup is just a series of commands to create the tables and insert the values, in plain SQL syntax). Say you have your backup in a file called moodle.dump, that your moodle database is called 'moodledb', that you use a username 'moodleuser' with password 'moodlepass' to connect to that database, you just need to drop all of the existing tables (or the restore will add to the existing contents), and then execute: mysql -u moodleuser -p moodledb < moodle.dump and then type the 'moodlepass' password when you are prompted to. Saludos. Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, I managed to fix my issue. Here is how I did it, in hopes it may prove useful to others: The problem did seem to be the primary keys of the quiz_questions and/or quiz_categories tables. To fix the issue, I went into MySQL and found my leftover Categories in the 'quiz_categories' table. I noticed that the abandoned categories now related to the main Moodle site, instead of a course, since they had a foreign key 'course' set to 1. I changed the 'course' attribute to relate to an existing course, and swapped back over to Moodle. I browsed to the surrogate course and found my leftover Categories available for deletion. After deleting the Categories, my restore completed without a hitch! Perhaps during a restore there could be a function to test for the existence of the Categories to restore? This would prevent my issue from happening, but it might be such an isolated incident that it is not worth the time and trouble. Just a thought. Regards, Garnett

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: emergency backup situation - urgent help needed.
ResponsesInList.Text: Lev, You could do a new Moodle install and then do a course restore...that should work fine and would be the easiest. The advantage of using the original database is that you could still do a new Moodle install so that you have the latest code, but use your existing database so that you won't have to redo all your site configuration settings or restore your courses. Here is what I would do.... 1. From your backup files find the Moodle install that you were using. If there are four different ones, then they should have four different names. Open the moodle directory of the one you were using and open the config.php file. There you will be able to see the database that corresponds to that Moodle install. 2. Upload that database to your server ...if you have cpanel, you can easily do that using phpmyadmin. If the database is to large to restore (if it times out) then download bigdump and follow the directions for restoring the database using it. 3. Once the database is restored, then install a new version of Moodle. Copy the config.php file from the old moodle site to your new install and copy your moodledata directory to your new site...be sure to put it in the same place in the new site as it was in the old site. If you have any custome themes, copy them to the new install. 4. Open Moodle in your webbrowser and visit moodle/admin so that any updates can be activated (see the upgrade instructions at the download section of Moodle.org). That should do it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup & Restore / Import Course Data - links not updated in 1.5.2+
ResponsesInList.Text: Think I may have identified the source of this problem. I'm using PostgreSQL 7.3. In my database log, I'm seeing errors: Relation "mdl_assignment_submissions_id_seq" does not exist Relation "mdl_dialogue_conversations_id_seq" does not exist (The latter error isn't related to the backup/restore problem, I don't think, but reinforces my conclusions, below.) I'm guessing this table (mdl_assignment_submissions) has something to do with storing the assignments in courses and associating the course folder number used in the backup/restore & data import functions. Looking at my database via phpPgAdmin, I find the table "mdl_assignment_submissions" exists. However, in the "id" column, the default value is: nextval('"mdl_assignment_submissio_id_seq"'::text) Postgre SQL appears to have truncated "submissions" to "submissio" - and in the mdl_dialogue_conversations table's id column, the same thing has happened - it's "mdl_dialogue_conversatio_id_seq". I found the following explanation in a PostgreSQL-related site: When you create an object in PostgreSQL, you give that object a name. Every table has a name, every column has a name, and so on. PostgreSQL uses a single type to define all object names: the name type. A value of type name is a string of 31 or fewer characters1. A name must start with a letter or an underscore; the rest of the string can contain letters, digits, and underscores. If you examine the entry corresponding to name in the pg_type table, you will find that a name is really 32 characters long. Because the name type is used internally by the PostgreSQL engine, it is a null-terminated string. So, the maximum length of name value is 31 characters. You can enter more than 31 characters for an object name, but PostgreSQL stores only the first 31 characters. (Anyone able to confirm this and to say whether it's true in PostgreSQL 8.x also?) It appears that, because adding the "_id_seq" here causes the length of this name to exceed the 31 character limit, PostgreSQL truncates the table name before adding "_id_seq". The error is thrown whenever a call is made for "mdl_assignment_submissions_id_seq" If this is the cause, I don't know how to fix it...any suggestions? (I'll be reporting this as a bug, btw ...) Thanks! WB

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Users not restored with Moodle1.5 backup
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Abbas, Hi Eloy, I had actually the same problem and it took me some time to find the reason: This problem comes up when you do a backup with ALL users (not just course). Internally, the options are assigned to numbers: 0 means all users 1 means course users 2 means no users Unfortunately, in backup/backup_execute.html on line 193 there is: 
```text
 if ($status && $preferences->backup_users) {
```
 So, if $preferences->backup_users is zero, the statement will not be entered and no users are backed up at all! I propose to rearrange the meaning of the numbers, so that zero means "no users" and 2 means "all users". For now, I just changed the mentioned line to 
```text
 if ($status && $preferences->backup_users || $preferences->backup_users == 0) {
```
 so that a backup with all users of the site is possible. I know this is not the way it should be! cheers, Christian

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Users not restored with Moodle1.5 backup
ResponsesInList.Text:
Oh, oh! Reviewing code changes it seems that the problem was introduced a lot of months ago and nobody has detected it until now. That line should be, simply: 
```text
if ($status) {
```
 This is because, at this stage of the backup, the backup_user_info() function just output to XML the collection of users calculated in previous stages (they have been stored in backup temporary tables some steps before) so that condition isn't needed at all! Just changing it both in 1.5.3+ and 1.6. Should be available in 24 hours from now. Congratulations Christian, you got it! Ciao PS: Please, confirm it works, TIA.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best Backup Method/Approach
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tad > Does this mean inside the zip file, the tool creates, there are files to restore each class? I am not quite sure of the meaning of "class," but yes, there are the files to restore each course. By default they are saved in the backup folder of each course. By the way, you can specify an alternative path to a directory where all backups are saved using the "Save to:" field. One advantage to specifying an alternative path is that if someone deletes a course by mistake, and deletes its files with it, then the backup.zip file will have been kept elsewhere. I have never had any need to restore an automatic backup (since there has never been any data corruption in my 2.5 year use of moodle) The automatic backup setup screen http://yoursite.com/moodle/admin/backup.php has pretty much the same setting as any manual backup screen (except not quite so fine-grained, to the module level) asking what you would like to backup. > Can you use the auto backup to restore one course or do you need to have the courses backed up individually? The autobackup does not restore. It only does backup. Also, the auto-backup does *not* allow you to specify which courses are backed up. It is a site-wide setting and does the whole lot. The time taken to backup depends upon the size of the course, but with my bigish courses we are looking at a bit shy of a minute. Let's say you do your bacups at 4am. Even if you have a hundred large courses then your server will be pretty busy from 4 am to 5:40 am. If you have a lot of users (and then probably a dedicated server) it might be a good idea to tell the users not to attempt to use the site between those times. BTW my server does not have a php accelerator and it is not particularly fast. Why do you want to auto-backup one course and not the others? Do you have a lot of courses and night-owl users? Or a global user base from various time zones? Backing up a lot of large courses does use server power. I guess that the desire to limit auto-backup to a subset of courses has not been an issue because most installations have users that sleep. Tim
