ResponsesInList.Title: Destination when restoring a course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everybody, I've created a beginners course - called beginners - in the category test on my server at home. It's no problem to save that course to a zip file. But I can't restore that course to the school server into a category called basics. It seems to me that the zip file contains the original category because after restore I all of a sudden have a new category test on my server. I've found some workarounds but is there any way to tell the system the destination category during restore? Thanks Stefan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Destination when restoring a course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stefan, there isn't any way to specify the category at restore. The restore looks for that category (test) in the destination server. If it isn't found, then tries to use the default category (that whose id is 1, usually "miscellaneous") and, if it doesn't exist, a new category is created. To avoid this you can: - Modify slightly the moodle. xml file (inside the backup zipped file). Go to the "MOODLE_BACKUP->COURSE->CATEGORY->NAME" entry and change it to your destination category (basics). Then zip everything again and the course will fit in such category. Or, - Create an empty course in your destination server, in the basics category, and restore your backup to existing course. Or, - Change the category once restored. Ciao PS: Perhaps this could be a nice new functionality for next release, if so, please add it to http://moodle.org/bugs .

ResponsesInList.Text:
I posted this earlier as a reply to another thread - but then I
realized the thread was over 6 months old!  I think this deserves
a new thread since I've compiled a lot of suggestions into a single
post. First some background information: The
problems started in 1.3.x and continued in 1.4.3 for awhile.  I
upgraded to 1.5.1 and then 1.5.2 and the problem continued. In an attempt to resolve this issue, I deleted the old installation of Moodle and removed all related databases.  I performed a clean installation of 1.5.2 and then restored the courses. My Moodle has 5 courses.  Manual backups work great.  Automatic/scheduled backups fail ~85% of the time. CRONTAB Every ~8 minutes, I run: lynx -connect_timeout=300 -dump http://www.constructiveteacher.com/admin/cron.php > /dev/null via the CRON daemon. (I just recently added the -connect_timeout=300 string to see if that would resolve the problem - it did not)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CRON Scheduled Backups Randomly Failing (>85% of the time) plus a "Work Around"
ResponsesInList.Text: Today was an interesting day! I think I've finally found a solution to the infamous... ----------------------------------------------- HTTP request sent; waiting for response. Alert!: Unexpected network read error; connection aborted. Can't Access ` http://www.constructiveteache r.com/admin/cron.php' Alert!: Unable to access document. lynx: Can't access startfile ----------------------------------------------- ...error! I had a feeling this was a Lynx related problem, but it was hard to tell.  From doing some google searches, I found that the average Lynx timeout was ~110 seconds.  For some reason that I do not understand, this timeout is a bit variable .  That could be why the problem starts out as an occasional problem and then gradually happens more and more often as your Moodle grows.  (on a bad Lynx day, the timeout can be as low as 25 seconds). So... why use Lynx anyway? I guess some hosts do not allow you to directly call the PHP binary.  But Total Choice Hosting does let you call PHP.  On my server it's kept in /usr/local/bin/php So, I altered my CRON process to call: /usr/local/bin/php /home3/constea/public_html/admin/cron.php > /dev/null And the problem seemed to go away. I let 3 complete backups run over the course of a couple hours to make sure it wasn't just a fluke that this fixed the problem. And I also have implemented all the suggestions I mentioned in the previous thread, so some of those changes could be contributing to this success. Good luck if you're having this problem! Caleb Benefiel

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to backup and restore a full Moodle site!
ResponsesInList.Text: I have used Moodle since 1.0 and never had to worrie about this till as of late. Here is what I did. Setup the new server , configured the PHP.INI and HTTP.CONF ect ect. On the old server, I tar the moodledata folder, and ran a backup of the database . I then tar up the themes and mod folder and the config.php file. I moved the MySQL . sql file, moodledata folder, themes folder and config.php to the new server. Next I renamed the moodle folder on the old server so no one could do anything while I converted over to the new server. One the new server, I downloaded a fresh copy of moodle and placed that in the web server root folder. I then copied over the moodledata folder from the old server and placed it in the same location that it was in on the old server /Library/www/moodledata. I then copied over the config.php into the new moodle folder. I set all the folder permissions and ownership of the files and folder to the same as I had on the old server. I then copied over the moodle.sql file that I created on the old server. Using MySQL commands I created a new database on the new server called moodle. I made sure the same user name and password was used on the new database as I had on the old server. So I did not have to change the config.php file in the moodle folder. Then I issued the command to dump my old database into the new database. mysql -p moodle < moodle.sql Changed the setting on the new server, to that of the old server, ie --- hostname, ip address ect ect. Then I loaded a browser and pointed to http://newserver/moodle/admin all updated fine and the outcome was a new moodle server with all my old data. I hope this gives you some idea on how it can be done. I did not go into great detail because each person will have something a little different. As far as settings go, and others may do this a bit differnt.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to backup and restore a full Moodle site!
ResponsesInList.Text: Try using mysqldump to create a backup of your original database (mysqldump -u user -ppassword moodle > moodle-backup.sql). Move the new file 'moodle-backup.sql' to the new server then recreate the database using 'mysql -u user -ppassword moodle < /path/to/moodle-backup.sql' this is a better practice than copying /var/lib/mysql/*. Some points here: 1) it's better security not to type -ppassword. Just type -p and you will be prompted; 2) Have you set up mysql with appropriate users and privileges on the new server?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: An error occurred deleting old backup data
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle uses one database to store all its info. Such database contains different table, each one specialised to handle some type of data (user info, course activities , grades...). Currently there are +150 tables in Moodle Database . Two of them, "xxx_backup_ids" and "xxx_ backup_files" (where "xxx" is the preffix that you have configured for them, usually "mdl_") are used in the backup (and restore) processes. Such processes include some code to delete old records from those tables and the "error occurred deleting old backup data" is showed when, due to some problem, Moodle can not access to that tables.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Robin and others, Just wanted to update you. Thanks for the help, you were right...my permissions were the problem, and would you believe it? My server doesn't seem to support the CHMOD command--but luckily I'm sitting two feet from my server, so I was able to fix them (using the "permissions wizard" available in IIS 5.1). After fixing those, the restore went through fine....BUT, none of my links to articles (kept in my moodledata folder) were working. My permissions on moodledata are at 777, so something else was happening. In the admin page variables, I switched the slash arguments (under the admin, config variables page)...interesting that now my articles showed up, but internal links to html pages weren't working. I read in the FAQ that I needed to AllowPathInfoForScriptMappings...so I tried this, to no avail. (because I have the wrong version of PHP) Also, I need slash arguments to work, for internal html pages to be loaded properly.  Finally, I found a string that said that I needed to edit my php.ini file so that cgi.fix_pathinfo = 1 (Do Not AllowPathInfoForScriptMappings for this to work) http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=9757#102032 and Ta-Da!!!  Now it's all working perfectly Thanks for all your help, Janice

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using backup and restore to duplicate courses... any way to update due dates automatically?
ResponsesInList.Text: I tried to use the Course Date Manager Block unsuccessfully, so I ended up doing it via MySQL.  Here's what I did: Given that 1 day is 86400 seconds... I needed to update all of my assignments and quizzes for this school year from last school year.  That was a 364 day change in my case (school started Sept. 7th 2004... this year it started Sept. 6th 2004). I used PhpMyAdmin to enter the following SQL commands.  This was across the board for ALL of my courses , you may have to adapt this command if you only want to fix one course (see link below): (1)  For assignments, I did the following (364 days forward): a) backup database b) UPDATE moodle_assignment SET timedue=timedue+31449600 (2)  For quizes, I needed to tweak both the start time (timeopen) and end time (timeclose) for every quiz (364 days forward): a) backup database b) UPDATE moodle_quiz SET timeclose=timeclose+31449600 c) UPDATE moodle_quiz SET timeopen=timeopen+31449600 This is not a magic fix... the admin may still have to tweak a date here and there.  But at least dates will match up correctly at the start of a new school year before any changes in curriculum and assignments are factored in. This post adapted from info contained here: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=13856&parent=66647

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Trying to move course to different domain
ResponsesInList.Text: What I believe Gustav was referring to by dumping the database is a way of backing up a mysql database.  You can do this with the PHPMyAdmin program (downloadable from the moodle website).  This allows you to save all the tables (structure and contents) to a single text file using SQL.  As it is a text file you can edit it to change all references to your old domain.  You may find that this file can be very large (last time I did this the sql file was >250Mb). You can then move this file to another clean install of moodle and again use PHPMyAdmin to create all the tables with their contents on the new site. Have fun!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Trying to move course to different domain
ResponsesInList.Text: For non-technical colleagues, the terminology of dumping a database etc. may seem frightening (general comment - not reflective of the specific individuals commenting on this forum!!). For clarification - and indeed my own use, could I ask if anyone would edit/correct/update my sequence of events above, please? If i was going to move a course from domain1.com to domain2.com I would: 1. Login to http://download.moodle.org/modules/integrations.php and note the sentence "This module is a repackaged version of phpMyAdmin 2.6.2. To install, just unzip this archive inside the moodle/admin folder. You should end up with a folder in there called 'mysql' in there that contains all the necessary files. Now when you look at your Moodle admin menus you will see a new item: ' Database '." 2. In this database admin area (on your original domain1.com), use phpMyAdmin to backup your whole SQL database (this will be a huge text file ending in .sql) 3. Backup your .sql file. Then, in this text file, replace all occurrences of domain1.com with domain2.com and save. 4. On domain2.com install Moodle and phpMyAdmin  (cf. Step 1). Go to the phpMyAdmin  area and import the SQL database. (Here I'm not sure if you can click something like 'import database' to upload the SQL file, or if you have to physically upload your SQL file on top of the new domain2.com one). I would imagine the former.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Not all courses backing up
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm having the same problem as everyone else in this thread... My Moodle has 5 courses.  Manual backups work great.  Automatic/scheduled backups fail ~85% of the time. First some background information: The problems started in 1.3.x and continued in 1.4.3 for awhile.  I upgraded to 1.5.1 and then 1.5.2 and the problem continued. In an attempt to resolve this issue, I deleted the old installation of Moodle and removed all related databases.  I performed a clean installation of 1.5.2 and then restored the courses. Every ~8 minutes, I run: lynx -connect_timeout=300 -dump http://www.constructiveteacher.com/admin/cron.php > /dev/null via the CRON daemon. (I just recently added the -connect_timeout=300 string to see if that would resolve the problem - it did not) When an automatic backup fails, I receive this email from the CRON Daemon at my webhost (Total Choice). ---------------------------------------------------------- Looking up www.constructiveteacher.com www.constructiveteacher.com Making HTTP connection to www.constructiveteacher.com Sending HTTP request. HTTP request sent; waiting for response. Alert!: Unexpected network read error; connection aborted. Can't Access ` http://www.constructiveteache r.com/admin/cron.php' Alert!: Unable to access document. lynx: Can't access startfile ---------------------------------------------------------- At this point, I can no longer manually run the cron process.  ../admin/cron.php reports that a Backup is in progress for the next ~45 minutes or so when I load that page in my web browser. I've tried some different user suggestions that I've read. I changed the backup directory to /moodledata/globalbackups/ instead of the individual course directories.  This did not seem to help. I manually set the path to zip / gzip in the Moodle config.  This did not affect the problem. ---------------------------------------------------------- Click on a folder icon to navigate. Click on a name to view its properties. / mdata / globalbackups / (Current Folder) backup-biology_1-20050729-0826.zip 42986 k 2777 backup-cteacher-20050729-0826.zip 92 k 2777 backup-gs-20050729-0828.zip 1708 k 2777 backup-life_science_1-20050729-0826.zip 7152 k 2777 backup-ls_-_1-20050729-0828.zip 16 k 2777 ---------------------------------------------------------- The problem usually occurs on the biology backup - it's the 43MB backup.  Perhaps that has something to do with it?  It occasionally fails on life_science as well - the 7MB backup. Work Around If I change the moodle config to not include the course files, the backups are significantly smaller - all are less than 500k.  When I do this, the backups very rarely fail - only ~5% of the time or less. Then I just have to remember to do a manual backup every now and then to make sure that the course content has been backed up. Also, I haven't thoroughly tested this, but if I use my web browser to call /admin/cron.php instead of the CRON Daemon, a full backup fails much less frequently.  I'd say a full backup is successful ~25%+ of the time. Has anyone determined the cause of this?  There seems to be some random element involved... Caleb Benefiel

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Not all courses backing up
ResponsesInList.Text:
Well, I already posted this in another thread that I started - but since I know this thread is indexed by Google, and for the sake of completion, I'm going to double post in here ------------------------------ Today was an interesting day! I think I've finally found a solution to the infamous... ----------------------------------------------- HTTP request sent; waiting for response. Alert!: Unexpected network read error; connection aborted. Can't Access ` http://www.constructiveteache r.com/admin/cron.php' Alert!: Unable to access document. lynx: Can't access startfile ----------------------------------------------- ...error! I had a feeling this was a Lynx related problem, but it was hard to
tell.  From doing some google searches, I found that the average Lynx
timeout was ~110 seconds.  For some reason that I do not understand, this timeout is a bit variable . 
That could be why the problem starts out as an occasional problem and
then gradually happens more and more often as your Moodle grows.  (on a
bad Lynx day, the timeout can be as low as 25 seconds). So... why use Lynx anyway? I guess some hosts do not allow you to directly call the PHP binary. 
But Total Choice Hosting does let you call PHP.  On my server it's kept
in /usr/local/bin/php So, I altered my CRON process to call: /usr/local/bin/php /home3/constea/public_html/admin/cron.php > /dev/null And the problem seemed to go away. I let 3 complete backups run over the course of a couple hours to make sure it wasn't just a fluke that this fixed the problem. And I also have implemented all the suggestions I mentioned in the
previous thread, so some of those changes could be contributing to this
success. Good luck if you're having this problem! Caleb Benefiel

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course hangs on restore
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm not certain this will help but we were experiencing a similar problem on all our restores (actually from Blackboard exports) that exceeded a certain size.  Our people at The Linuxbox looked into it and found the bug detailed below: In /moodle/backup/restore.php: line ~115: raise_memory_limit("memory_limit","128M"); The problem here is, raise_memory_limit($newlimit) only takes one parameter (the new limit), but in restore.php it is passed two variables.  So it tries to up the memory limit to the string "memory_limit" which fails. Fix: To fix the problem, change: raise_memory_limit("memory_limit","128M"); to: raise_memory_limit("128M"); They've placed this problem in the bugtracker. Hope it brings about a solution for you. Bob Puffer

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course hangs on restore
ResponsesInList.Text: Just wanted to elaborate on what Bob Puffer had said. There is a slight difference from what Bob mentioned and what I see is happening to you.  Bob's restore process was failing silently.  Yours looks like it is printing things out (as you can tell where its failing).  So this might not be the right fix.  Regardless, this is still a bug in Moodle, and fixing it can only help the situation: We found the bug, and posted it to bugtracker ( http://moodle.org/bugs/bug.php?op=show&bugid=3800&pos=3 ), however, no one has committed the patch back into Moodle. If you are having trouble with Restores of large backups failing silently, it is very likely this is the problem. (Hint Hint) If any devs read this, could you commit it for the next release of Moodle?  Its obviously just a minor error, and a quick fix. =P

ResponsesInList.Title: Solved. But... why? (was: Backup causes segfaults. Help!)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi again, I was digging into the moodle source code of the backup routines, trying to find the source of the problem described in my previous post. After introducing a call to flush() after each "echo", and uncommenting some of the debugging "echoes" in moodle/backup/lib, I finally got that the function causing the problem was backup_copy_file(). Every time this function was called, the apache process died due to a "Segmentation fault" signal. Just for trying, I commented out the line 294 in moodle/backup/lib.php. This line contained the call clam_log_upload($to_file,null,true); and was executed only if the file was successfully copied. After this, the segfault dissapeared! Now I'm happy because I can do again my backups. However I'm still intrigated about what this function call was for, why it produced a segfault, and what are the possible side effects of having it commented out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Solved. But... why? (was: Backup causes segfaults. Help!)

Like you, I'm wondering whether commenting this line out may have possible side effects. If one of the Moodle gurus out there could express their opinion, that would be most appreciated. In the meanwhile, I'm a happy camper as it is.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Solved. But... why? (was: Backup causes segfaults. Help!)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: To what do the various course backup options refer?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bob, the "Metacourse" option is used to automatically enrol students in one course (metacourse or "parent course") if they belong to other ("child course"). If you enable this option and the course being exported is a parent or a child course in your site, that relations will be exported and the restore process will try to rebuild them in the destination server . All users will backup all the users in your site, course will backup only the users needed (with some info) in your course and none, say, none! The "userdata" switch near every module will determine if information related to users will be exported or no. For example, in a quiz, all the questions and quizzes will be exported always (module data), but attempts, answers and grades (user related data) will be decided by such setting. Finally, "Uses Files" will export, for now, user photos (as they are all the files related to one user currently). In the future, it's highly probable that this option control other files owned by the user, DMS....). Hope it helps...

If it's not working .... yet this is probably a bug that needs to go in the bug tracker for Eloy" (my snip) However some thoughts Were your categories published? If you publish your question categories, it can in effect have the REVERSE effect that you wish for http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=22460 because by publishing them it means that the quiz questions refer to the files referenced by the original published category, which means that courses may attempt to reference files in another course (which if the students are not enrolled in the other course they may not be able to do). So if you are sharing questions WITHIN an installation, especially those that reference files, it may be better NOT to publish them. Conceivably, this might have something to do with your problem. A possible partial solution to the persistance of links to media files accessed by quizes might be (1) Using a special multimedia folders in site files that is NOT open to everyone, and course files, that is referenced by quizes. (2) In combination with (1) the greater use of variables rather than URLs at to reference in GIFT and in database and at backup and restore, i.e. at all stages and in all forms of quiz import export (as implemented by Jamie in the TUI). E.g. LIsten to thisclick. Did you year it?{=yes, ~no} LIsten to thisclick. Did you year it?{=yes, ~no} I am not sure whether this would have any bearing on your problem but I think that Howard Miller, the king of quiz import/export, is thinking of instituting such variables at the GIFT level. Once this variables exist perhaps they might be kept at the quiz execution and back/uprestore level with would eliminate the need to parse to check for wwwroot . If you agree please vote for http://moodle.org/bugs/bug.php?op=show&bugid=2956&pos=20 which has been deffered. ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Lena Persson, There is a feature in the backup and restore routine such that if there are temporary problems, such as a lack of memory, the backup/restore is postponed by 30 minutes (I think). Zipping and unzipping uses a lot of memory especially if you use the zipping and unzipping functionality within php (pkzip??) rather than external zip/unzip programs, which you can set in the site settings. (I recommend you use an external zip program if you are not doing so already). If you have a lot of courses all being backed up at the same time, then perhaps your system is running out of memory, the backup is being postponed, and that is why you are seeing some zips being created later. You may wish to tier your backups so that they do not all load the system at the same time but in a sense the backup software is doing this for you. So if I am right, this is a feature, rather than a bug. Please also see

To attempt to import this file either create a new course, or go to an existing course (class) where you want to place this content. In the left panel select restore. Select Upload A File and then Browse to locate the file. Press Open to upload. Once the file has been uploaded select the files checkbox and select Restore. You will be asked to confirm the restoration. Select Yes. You will be presented with an alert advising you that the restore was unsuccessful because the file is Invalid or Corrupt. ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Harald, the "xml error- invalid token" error usually is due to some "not-allowed" char in the xml file moodle.xml (some control character pasted or something similar). Zip everything. Try it again. Hope it helps, ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restore doesn't finish the job
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, those are, really, BIG numbers! First of all, it's necessary to check if any error is sent to the apache errors file when your browser stops. It could give us some idea about the root cause for your problem (although I'm 95% sure about it's a memory problem). The second thing to do is to monitor your server processes (top) to see how the memory is being used by the httpd process running the restore. This could help to detect if the memory limit is reached. About your numbers, restore loads data per module basis so, in theory, if you have 40 quizzes, it will have to handle 2.000.000/40 = 50.000 answers at the same time. Those 50.000 answers, assuming 100 characters per answer will be 5.000.000 characters (aprox. 5MB). The critical process here is the function used to convert such XML data to an array. I can need 100x the original size to build the structure. And it's really a slooow parse and conversion routine (specially for >1MB structures) that could be causing the timeout in your browser. Perhaps it could be improved, sending some data to the browser (to avoid the timeouts) at some strategic points. But first, we need to be really sure about the root cause of your problem (max memory reached, browser timeout, PHP timeout...). Finally, if you can send me your file (privately, of course) I could do some deep tests in my servers to be able to find the exact cause and, if possible, to apply the correct solution. Anyway, it will be after Moodle 1.5 release (I'll be really busy until it). Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding backup/restore code for gradebook_cdc
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jeff, level at backup time is only to make the indentation of the XML file. It isn't mandatory at all, only is done to view such file correctly in text editors. Anyway level 0 is MOODLE_BACKUP, level 1 is COURSE and level 2 is SCALES (where level*2 = number of spaces to indent). But at restore time levels are very important, mainly because they determine where to start and end examining the file, reducing the time to parse it. So, every time that the parser finds a new enclosed tag it increments level and store it and whenever a tag is closed, level is reduced. So MOODLE_BACKUP will be level 1, COURSE level 2 and SCALES level 3. That's the reason for the difference. In backups it's only "cosmetic" (starting at 0), but in restore they are "true" levels of nested tags (starting at 1). If you have written your backup file visually correct, your restore level should be always 1 more. Hope this helps! Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding backup/restore code for gradebook_cdc
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jeff, at restore time, every table having "child" tables must store their "id" conversion in the "backup_ids" table. It mush contain the old id, read from XML file and the new id, inserted to DB. When the child table is being restored, you must look for the parent pair and update the field before inserting it. I'm not sure about your exact problem. I think that, of you have one table, with 4 FK to other tables (FKs always point to PK in other tables and PKs in Moodle must be always 1 column, id identifier), first you have to restore such (parent) tables, saving id changes to the "backup_ids" tables and then restore the "objective table", looking for each field pairs there (4 conversions). This system is used widely in modules restore. Forums can be a good example to examine because the have this type of inheritance from different (previously restored) tables. Perhaps if you specify your DB schema I'll be able to explain it a bit more... Ciao

ResponsesInList.Text: You mean files that you have uploaded? They are stored in your dataroot directory, which *should* be outside your dirroot . Or maybe you mean all the course content? That's all stored in the database, it won't be affected by putting the new code there. Say you have /home/covenofe/public_html/college as your dirroot (which is where you have all the moodle code) and, something like /home/covenofe/moodle_data configured to be your dataroot. (These are configured in config.php as $CFG->dirroot and $CFG->dataroot respectively) You LEAVE /home/covenofe/moodle_data completely alone. Backup /home/covenofe/public_html/college and unzip the latest version of moodle into where it was. Copy back config.php and your theme directory into /home/covenofe/public_html/college/config.php and /home/covenofe/public_html/college/themes/* Visit http://yoursite.com/yourmoodledirectory/admin/index.php with your browser. Any required upgrades will take place. If your dataroot is inside /home/covenofe/public_html/college, say something like /home/covenofe/public_html/college/moodle_data, then you'll need to copy that back across as well when you copy back config.php and your themes directory. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Big course: Backup fails without error

Try to use external commands instead (in "Administration/Configure"). And upgrade to Moodle 1.4.2 ASAP. It includes some important changes in such libraries. - PHP's resources limit: Some type of memory or time limit can be reached in the middle of the execution. Although such limits are "manually" expanded before each backup execution, is possible that they weren't enough. Try to modify "backup/backup.php" and edit values for "max_execution_time" and "memory_limit". And these are all the causes that I can imagine and their possible solutions. Feedback will be welcome! TIA and ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring 1.3.1 backup to 1.4.1
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Erlyn, I haven't done exact calculations but I think that the 50000 queries limit can be reached easily. Just imagine your 20 quizzes, each of them with 10 questions, in a course with 20 students (one attempt only each student). Only to restore this information from a backup you will need 20*10*20 = 4.000 records to be written (only answers!!). But records aren't written directly! Information is stored temporary in backup_XXX tables and retrieved from there again before writing them to their final location, so we should multiply by 3 our previous result (write to temp-read from temp-write to final) so, for now we have 4.000*3= 12.000 DB operations. And this isn't all! For each record written in final tables, a lot of re-coding work is done on the fly between original numbers in backup file and destination numbers in Moodle DB. So you could multiply this again by, say, 3 (to recode the userid, the courseid and the quizid, for example). Now we are using 12.000*3 = 36.000 DB operations. And I could continue but, as you can see, the number of operations performed against Moodle DB is really high and they happen in only some minutes! With this explanation, I'm not saying that the quiz module is the responsible to reach the limit (it's only an example). Other modules can need similar numbers... The restore process is really intensive because it must perform tons of calculations in order to fit everything in place. And I cannot imagine another way to do it (well we could inserts "pauses" of seconds after each DB operation but, then, your course would be restored in days, and I'm sure that it'll break another limit in your host! ). Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposal: Addition of Import / Export options to make "Back up" / "Restore" more intuitive
ResponsesInList.Text: Tim, I would interpret Backup/Restore and and Import/Export a little differently based on conventions used in other CMSs. Backup ->  Archiving of all course content and student generated data into one comprehensive file, usually zipped with very few options. It's basically an "image" of the course. Same as a backup file created by Word when the automatic backup is turned on. Restore-> Takes a backup file and unarchives/unpacks and re-establishes the course exactly as it was when the backup was created. Export-> Writes out all the content of a course including the structure of a course in a format that will allow it to be "imported" into another course or even another system. Same as saving a Word document in Rich Text Format. The "RTF" of courses would be the IMS specifications for exporting content. ( http://www.imsproject.org ) Import->Takes an exported course as a file and reads the content into the new course or system. Usually, restoring a backup will either create a new course or overwrite an existing course. On the other hand, importing will merge the content with an existing course. Moodle Backup/Restore is pretty good. Now we need the Export/Import features that follows the IMS specifications so we can start working with content in other systems. Not only importing content from Blackboard, WebCT and eCollege but also being able to export content from Moodle for use in those systems.  (This goes with another dicussion that one can get more "locked" into Moodle than WebCT right now because of WebCT's more extensive IMS export/import features.) Cheers, Bob

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Backup eats storage space (duplicate temp folders)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi A, An My SQL dump containing your mdl_course, mdl_backup_courses and mdl_backup_log should be enough for me. With them, I can see where (course and step) is crashing your scheduled backup. You can send it privately, of course. Anyway, making a few calculations: 240Mb * 12 executions per hour (once every 5 minutes) * 4 hours = 11Gb so really your disk is getting full before the 4 hours time limit!! As a quick fix, you can try this: - If you are running Unix, use external zip and unzip executables, specifying them in the Administration/Variables page. In the past, a memory bug in the PCLZIP library (used when such executables are not defined) has been the cause of similar issues. This could solve your problem with the course if the problem is its compression. - In admin/cron.php change line 147 from "@ini_set("memory_limit","128M");" to "@ini_set("memory_limit","256M");". The backup process itself doesn't need that amount of memory, but the PCLZIP library need as much memory as the total size being compressed. This could solve your problem with the course if the problem is its compression. - In backup/lib.php, change line 34 from "$hours = 4;" to "$hours = 1", this make that old temp files were deleted in 2 hours, so they will be deleted before your disk become full (you will need 2-3Gb "only"). But this doesn't solve the problem with your 240Mb course!! Ciao

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tan, sorry by the delay answering this but I've been out some days... First of all, to MOVE one Moodle installation between servers, the recommended method is to make a full backup of your Moodle server (DB dump, moode and moodledata dirs), and then transfer them to your new server. Making a DB import and some adjustments in your config.php file, your Moodle's server will be running perfectly in your new super-machine! This is called a SITE backup. Instead, COURSE backups are recommended to move INDIVIDUAL courses between servers. And they work! The error that you posted in your previous message ("Error checking backup file. Invalid or corrupted") can be caused by some zip/unzip incompatibilities between Moodle's internal zip and their external command equivalents. It has been solved in 1.4.2 and I hope that such incompatibilities will be out forever...!!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site Backup
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi jacob, if you are going to do a "major change on the site" it's always recommended to do a "SITE BACKUP", i.e, to save in a safe place your moodle and moodledata directories plus your moodle DB. That's the SAFEST way to rebuild everything if something goes wrong with your changes!! The use of the "COURSES BACKUP" is an alternative to that, but the time to rebuild a site from them is longer (you will have to restore every course individually), less reliable (you will have to reinstall and reconfigure everything) and, definitively, not the proper way. Use the "SITE BACKUP" approach to have the best ENTIRE backup of your SITE.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site Backup
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Albert, thanks for your feedback (absolutely complete). Really well done! The first "interesting" thing is the information that you receive by e-mail. It's short, but meaningful. There are three status: Ok: The backup has finished ok. Error: The backup haven't finished due to a "controlled" situation. The process has continued. Unfinished: The backup haven't finished due to an "uncontrolled" situation. The process has been aborted suddenly (although the rest of courses has been saved in the next cron invocation). Controlled situations are problems with file-names, some potential inconsistencies in Moodle DB, bad permissions to backup files... all of them are detected by the backup process itself and it will continue automatically with the rest of courses. Uncontrolled situations are problems with memory, disk or something related with the available (and configured) resources in your server installation. With them, the backup process will die but, in the next cron automatic invocation the rest of courses will be saved (where the "unfinished" course will be skipped to avoid the error to arrive again). Common causes for this uncontrolled situations can be: PHP's memory_limit problem: If the course is too big, it could need some extra-memory to be saved. By increasing this PHP's variable you will solve it. But this type of errors are produced (usually) always in the same exact point of the backup process and that doesn't seem to be your case. Using external zip utilities (instead of Moodle's internal zip libraries) could help with this type of problems too. PHP's max_execution_time: This variable controls the max amount of time that one script (and the whole cron system is one php script!!) can be running. It the time arrives, PHP kills automatically the process. Depending of the load of your server, the grown of your courses and other variables...this "killer" moment can arrive at different stages in your backup. This seems to be what is happening to you. Try increasing that value (although it's currently set to infinite in the cron execution to avoid this type of errors. Web server timeouts: Every web server can have their own timeouts, stopping one page generation when it has elapsed. This could be your problem too. Please, take a look to your web server documentation to see how to modify this value (if I'm not wrong, both Apache2 and IIS have it configured to 300 seconds by default). This is all I can tell with your info. Further investigations can be done, but they will require admin access to your Moodle server and root access to your host so, please, check above possibilities before... Hope they help! Feedback will be welcome, of course. Ciao PS: And one more recommendation: When you send all that info to a forum you should send it as an attachment instead of inline in the message. It will make easier to read the entire discussion... thanks again!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mirroring Moodle installations ...
ResponsesInList.Text: Synchronising separate Moodles would be very very hard. Everything in Moodle is numbered. So say, for example, you have two identical sites, and someone posts a new message to the same forum. The new number for the post on both servers is 36364 (say). Now, when merging the two sites, what do we do with these posts with this same number? We need to renumber one ... which means we need to renumber everything that refers to it, and the links in the email versions will be wrong and so on. There will also be all the previous posts which are the same and do not need to be renumbered, so we need to take that into account too. You can see it becomes a nightmare, and that's just forum posts. For resources and things I think it would be better to look at good local generic caching software (eg a Squid proxy).

ResponsesInList.Title: Are backups accessible to anyone?
ResponsesInList.Text: If course files are accessible to anyone, does that mean that automatic backups are too? If so, is it not a sort of security risk where one's entire course could be ripped off and reconstituted elsewhere?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Are backups accessible to anyone?
ResponsesInList.Text: Course files are not accessible to anyone, you need to be a member of the course. If you specify a system path for your automatic backups that is not within the Moodle dataroot or dirroot then there is no way anyone can get to them from the web (even if they are Moodle admin).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Are backups accessible to anyone?
ResponsesInList.Text: If a Moodle admin configures automated backup with the default Save to: value, i.e., the backup files are stored in the course directory, then members of a course (including students) can access the backups. Perhaps either this should not be a default, or the automated backup configuration page should warn of the risks involved? A possible risk is that students could download a backup and view sensitive information about the course -- information they would normally not be authorized to view.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Are backups accessible to anyone?
ResponsesInList.Text: I think perhaps there should be no default whatsoever, and when configuring automatic backup or running a backup for the first time, the user is forced to enter a location, and is told the consequences of where they put the file. You can't have a default that would be outside the Moodle directory because for each installation the user might want it in a different place.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Are backups accessible to anyone?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi N! One problem is there is no " Help " button on the backup page.  Therefore, directions are sparse.  I chose default because every other path I chose seem to be a problem.  Instructions are needed so Admins/Teachers would know how to backup into safe (protected) directories within or outside of the Moodle directory. [I think this would be safer??] If anyone knows how to have files backed-up into a secure directory would they please outline the procedure here.  It would be appreciated. Thanks in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Are backups accessible to anyone?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi WP -- The procedure depends on a number of variables: the Moodle host operating system; who has access to the host filesystem; the
permissions under which the backup process runs; which parts of the
host filesystem are served up by the host's web server software; etc. For instance, the following would work if: the Moodle host is Unix-based; you have access to a command shell on the host with root permission and no untrusted people do; the backup process (initiated by cron ) runs with root permission; the host's web server software is configured such that the following directory and its contents are not servable. [in a command shell on the host with root permission] # mkdir /moodle-backups # chown root.root /moodle-backups # chmod 700 /moodle-backups [then, as Moodle admin, set Save to: on the backup configuration page to /moodle-backups ] As you can see, ideally the Moodle admin should be -- or should be working together with -- an experienced system administrator of the host operating system.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Complete Restore not working...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Andrew, I think that you are a bit "confused" with backups: - COURSE backups are used to backup individual courses (to save or to move them to another server). They don't include any site-level information (theme, site configuration, active modules...). - SITE backups are used to backup and entire site (to save or to move it to another server). They are a "snapshot" of the entire Moodle site and, when restored, the new site will be exactly as the old one (same courses, configuration...). So, if you want to move your entire Moodle site from your tower to your laptop, you have to use the 2nd type of backup. You can see this link about how to do SITE backups. Ciao In your example above, I think that making a tar file of the MySQL database can produce problems. The proper manner to do it is to use the "mysqldump" command instead.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Complete Restore not working...
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually, moving all the database files directly (via tar or not) is OK as long as you shutdown the MySQL server cleanly before doing it. On Linux you can do this as root: mysqladmin shutdown then move or copy your files and then start the database again using /etc/init.d/mysql start

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ger, relative links (ie. "images/mylogo.jpg") needn't to be transformed in the backup/restore process at all. They will work in the new (destination) server without modifications. If relative links are modified by the HTML editor to absolute links (ie. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: gzinflate error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gustav, the "gzinflate: buffer error" problem is a weird problem under some PHP/ZLIB and ZIP files combinations. Some weeks ago, in "Moodle en Español" course, some users reported an that error when trying to restore the Spanish version of the "Moodle for Teachers" course. Curiously that course was restored without problems by the rest of participants. After some searches in the web looking for info about that error I wasn't able to find the exact cause/combination of the error. And users with problems were able to restore other courses. Then I tried to create 4 different slightly modified versions of the zip file: 1.-The course zipped with the Unix "zip" executable. 2.-The course zipped with "low compression settings". 3.-The course zipped with WinZip and without the "moddata" directory. 4.-The course zipped without compression at all. Users tried to restore that course into their "problematic" servers and the process failed in versions 1, 2 and 3, but it was successful with version 4. So, one workaround can be to unzip and zip the course again with the Unix executable and compression set to 0 (I don't know if there is some W32 application to do that). Obviously other alternative is to use the command executables instead of Moodle internal routines. When I was searching the web, I found one page about one PHP Bug in version 4.1.2 but one of my problematic users was using PHP 4.2.x, and a very new ZLIB library so I'm not able to determine the wrong combination. And this is the status of this issue. In my experience it affects to random zip files under some servers. I think that it isn't related with the backup/restore procedure at all but it's really an important problem in some servers. Any idea/alternative will be welcome, sure!! If people having this problem can post here his OS/ Apache /PHP/ZLIB version, perhaps we could advance something... Hope it heps, ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: recycling a course

It is quite time-consuming. So I was wondering whether this could not be made more comfortable: Select all courses that are to be recycled, Specify the suffix that should be added to the names of the old courses, Watch the script run while you have a cup of tea. Now you will probably say that if I want to have the cup of tea then I should simply code the above. Unfortunately the backup and restore scripts are rather complicated. Perhaps Eloy could provide us with a simple function backup_and_restore($courseid) which does what the name suggests. Then all the rest will be simple (calling this function once for every course desired and then doing the renaming of the courses).

ResponsesInList.Text: I was trying to set up "question banks" to be shared among several courses. I built a hidden Question Bank course Z that contained only questions (not content), then courses A and B that used questions from Z. When I back up A (or B) it copies all the questions from Z. So I have to keep moving a whole Moodle (not just one course) from one place to another.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring published quiz questions
ResponsesInList.Text: If you move the whole site to a different server , I think a better option would be to dump the whole database and restore it on the new server using PhpMyadmin, rather than creating backups of individual courses and restoring them on the new server using the Moodle restore function. It would save you a lot of work and you would not run into this problem with duplicate questions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restoring published quiz questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Marilyn, Let's imagine that your "original" Z, A and B courses are in server 1. Z is the "owner" of the questions. If you backup and restore A or B in server 1, then the new courses, A2 or B2, will use Z questions too. If you restore A or B in another server called 2, if Z exists there, the new restored courses will use its questions too. But if Z doesn't exists in server 2, A or B will restore the questions as owners. This is the expected behaviour to ensure the integrity of the quizzes across different servers !! So, I recommend you that always restore your Z (repository) course in the new server before restore the A or B (dependent) courses on it. Has this sense for you ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Absolute vs Relative links
ResponsesInList.Text: It's a messy issue in general that does need to be dealt with, but it's not easy. One problem is that links (including images) which get sent out via email do need to be absolute. Another is that relative links may mean different things within different contexts - for example, a relative image in the editor is relative TO THE EDITOR PAGE, not it's final location, so to get the correct final result people would need to put up with broken images in the editor. One solution is to continually parse all incoming text looking for absolute URLs within the Moodle-space and convert them to relative links for storage, while always parsing outgoing texts and converting relative links to absolute ones. Alternatively, we can use absolute references all the time and only do this conversion during backup and restore ...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Absolute vs Relative links
ResponsesInList.Text: ... or we can make all links point to a new script link.php and pass a MRL (Moodle Resource Locator) as an argument. All link.php will do is look up the URL from the MRL in a table and forward to the URL. This table would have to be dealt with appropriately by backup and restore. One nice thing about his proposal is that it can be phased in gradually without breaking anything. All that is required is that someone writes the lookup-and-redirect script and updates the backup module. We can then slowly start using MRL's in more and more places in Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem withg backup/restore
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rob, some "technical" comments about your post: 1.-About the ZIP/UNZIP issue, in previous versions of Moodle (some time ago) ZIP support was only allowed for *X machines and this worked invoking an external (shell) zip program. Currently zip support in built in Moodle for ALL platforms and leaving that fields empty you'll use it. And after tons of tests it's really the more reliable method to run backup/restore because it handles complex structures (and backups can become to complex!! ). 2.-About the BROWSERS issue, there are some internal timeouts in some of them affecting long tasks. The first timeout is the "inactivity" one. Some browsers, after some "idle" period (without receiving data from the server) close the connection. This timeout has been solved inside the backup/restore utility forcing it to send data to the browser (blank lines and spaces) continuously. The second "timeout" is the "maxtime" one. Some browsers close the connection after some (fixed) time. This avoid some long restores to be completed. And we cannot do anything here !! It's a browser limitation.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Where are my questions gone?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ger, after some tests to simulate your situation, I've found that it seems to be a "bug" in the "delete course" functionality. I explain it now: Say you have an "A" course. You have two categories there (A1 and A2). Every category has some questions associated. If you use questions from that categories in a new course "B", when you delete the "A" course, the same problem (cannot edit questions) occurs. The root cause for this is that your original quiz_categories records (A1 and A2) continue pointing to the deleted course A. One workaround to have this working is to update every record in quiz_categories whose course field is A to B. I've done it and now I can edit the questions again !! If you think this has sense, please open a bug in http://moodle.org/bugs I hope this helps, Eloy.

I use bug-report only for bugs and do wishes in the forums. But your wishes will be fulfilled if the bug is solved, isn't it. And it's a *real* bug, I think Question: when I get a zipped  course from you, I am not the owner of the categories in the original course, will the same happen? Then the workaround doesn't help, isn 't it? Every time you restore a course, this steps are processed: If the category doesn't exists, create it in destination and remap questions here. If the category exists: If it belongs to destination course simply remap questions here. If it doesn't belong to destination course: If its publish field is set to No (0), create a new category in destination course and remap questions here. If its publish field is set to Yes (1), simply remap questions here. (where destination course could be a new, empty one or a existing one).

The workaround in my previous post was based in the "delete course" action. I think that it's the buggy problem. If you don't delete the original course, problem doesn't occur, isn't it ? Would be nice to have the chance to point to the datadir of the first course, instead of copying all these multimedia files. About this, I think that such "functionality" must be out of the backup/restore process. I think that the OS links "technique" could be used here to minimize disk space usage, but I think that this is a "particular" decision to every installation. Ciao, Eloy

ResponsesInList.Title: Backup/restore of front page and main news forum
ResponsesInList.Text: Eloy's backup and restore feature can actually not only deal with courses but also with the front page . This is so because internally the front page is actually treated as just another course. The only problem is that the front page does not have a backup link like the other courses. The workaround is to directly open the page /backup/backup.php in your browser. You will then see a course carrying the name of your whole site. That is the one you want to backup. Perhaps the backup link could be added to the admin box on the front page, as it is in other courses?
